Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r103/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: its two Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r103 and -r103b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; samp.sh, walk.sh, ab.sh (`V=v3kb.sh` for the second tree),
read103.sh, env-console.txt, STATE.md). Base runs on celosia-r101.vpk: runsb/sampA0 (sampler, the altar),
runs/walkA0 (`SOTC_WALK79_LOG`, the altar).

**Looking for whole layers.** The task was to find what the game thread still does in the display walk only
because the original fed the PS2 (packets the native renderer re-parses, matrices it recomputes) and hand the
renderer its inputs directly. The sampler at the altar (runsb/sampA0, % of the game thread) has the whole
display path at ~15%, spread over ~80 functions: the walk's natives 3.7 (clip83 1.1, the walk 1.0, the class
lookup 0.6), the model / mesh hooks 4.7 (the hook front 0.5, the palette read out of the VU1 packet 0.75, the
texture scroll rows 0.75, the lane joins 0.3), the light pass 1.4, round 67's prefetch 1.2, the sort lists 0.6,
the particle draw chain ~2.1. walk79's host clock gives the draws 11-25 ms for ~48 models at the altar, but the
sampler's CPU under them is a fraction of that: the rest is waiting (the frame change's syncFrame, the lane) and
Vita3K's own stalls, not the walk's work. What is PS2-only in it:

| layer | % of the game thread (altar) | done |
|---|---|---|
| particleDraw's ptclman packets: Mat / Env (with two fog factors) / Vtx packets, ptclmanBegin / End, the display list put, the VU1 microcode upload, the chain | ~1.1 | ptcl103 |
| the solid models' VU1 matrix blocks (camera +0x1a0 x part, into the instance packet's +0x104 block) and their camera lookup | ~0.2 | solid103 |
| the skin palette written into the VU1 packet, then read back out of its UNPACKs by the hook (readChainPaletteLean) | ~0.75 | no: the kick's deferred palette copies (round 34) read the same packets |
| iosDlLockObj (the drawn object into the display list's lock group) | ~0.7 | no: it defers the object's delete past the frame's DMA; the hook jobs and the lane read the instance after the walk |
| the heat haze strips' GIF packet (glVertex kick), parsed again by glEnd's hook | ~0.4 | no (small) |

So removing every PS2-format layer of the display path is ~3% of the game thread; the rest of the walk's ~15% is
its own per-object work (class lookups, clip, sort lists, light colours, the hook's copies for the worker).

**What changed (default on; A/B names `ptcl103`, `solid103`, `r103all` both off).**
- **ptcl103** (`SOTC_PTCL103`; decomp_ptcldraw.cpp `tail103`, sotc_native.cpp `ptclDirect103`). particleDraw
  (0x113e940, the per-emitter draw of the lit puffs, type 4) ends at 0x113eafc: the environment matrix (VU0:
  *0x1216e40's rows x the scale matrix at sp), then ptclDisplayListPut, transMicroCode(7), ptclmanBegin,
  BuildMatPacket(material +0x14), BuildEnvPacket(vec, 4, matrix, light s2 + 0x90, shade sp + 0x40, fade),
  BuildVtxPacket(the particles, count), ptclmanEnd. None of it is read by the native renderer: the hooks on
  Mat / Env / Vtx copy their inputs (blend, environment, particles) into a job. The tail now computes the matrix
  with the same VU0 operations and makes that job from the same inputs (ptclEnvTake / ptclVtxTake, the hooks'
  own code, split out), in the same place of the job order; nothing goes into the display list (the particles'
  48-byte records stay in its free room, copied into the job at once). Other particle drawers still go through
  the packets and the hooks. `SOTC_PTCL103_CHECK=1`: the direct job is kept, the original packets are built and
  hooked, and the hooks' job is compared with it field for field (count, texture, layer, blend, the environment's
  bytes, the particles' words): 0 differences in 148 000 particle draws at the altar (runs/checkA1) and 140 000
  on route 6 (runsb/checkR1). The same draws, so the same pixels.
- **solid103** (`SOTC_SOLID103`; decomp_walk.cpp `solidDisp`). 010F3A08 writes each part's camera +0x1a0 x part
  matrix into the instance packet's block: the PS2's VU1 input. The model hook draws from the parts' own
  matrices (a1) and the camera's +0x5a0; no native code reads the blocks. With the native renderer drawing
  (`sotc_native::nativeDraws`: the hook installed, no PS2 lists, no GS raster), for a model without a shadow
  (shadowDisp's rigid matrix comes from its packets) and without the LOD record's lens scale, the blocks and
  their GetCameraContext call are left out. `SOTC_SOLID103_POISON=1` (checking) fills the skipped blocks with
  NaNs: the altar and route 6 drew as before (runs/checkA1, runsb/checkR1 captures, pics/r103_poisonR.png).

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz).**
- Sampler, the altar, the same VPK with the round on / off (runsb/sampA1on, sampA1off; window 160-290 s): the
  functions the round touches 3.07% -> 2.00% of the game thread (BuildEnvPacket 0.37 -> 0.07, BuildVtxPacket
  0.24 -> 0.05, ptclmanEnd 0.20 -> 0.04, the fog factors 0.26 -> 0.06, BuildMatPacket 0.13 -> 0.02, the display
  list put / begin / microcode 0.32 -> 0.13, solidDisp 0.26 -> 0.09; new: tail103 0.23, ptclDirect103 0.07).
  ~1.1% of the game thread, ~0.5 ms a frame there.
- In-run A/B (`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r103all,ptcl103,solid103 SOTC_AB_ROTATE=1 SOTC_AB_PERIOD=60`, ab89.py matched by
  draws, off minus on):

| run | part (frame, all on) | ptcl103 | solid103 | r103all |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/altar1 | from 3 300 (52.4 ms) | +0.70 | +0.00 | +1.40 |
| runs/route1 | from 3 000 (35.0 ms) | +0.44 | -0.08 | +0.47 |
| runsb/attract1 (600 s) | riding, from 13 000 | +1.85 | +0.60 | +1.33 |
| runsb/attract1 | the world and riding, from 10 000 | -0.25 | -0.89 | +0.05 |
| runs/finalR (route 6, 600 s, the console env) | the plain, from 4 300 | +0.55 | +0.36 | +0.29 |

The signs agree with the sampler but every value is inside the in-run A/B's +-1 ms noise.

**Pictures and behaviour.** ptcl103 hands the renderer byte-identical particle jobs (the check), solid103
removes writes nothing reads (the poison runs); nothing is drawn later or less often. No fault: the altar 300 s
x2, route 6 420 s x2, the attract demo with riding 600 s, route 6 600 s with the console env.

**What this says about the walk.** Even all of the display path's PS2-format work is ~3% of the game thread
(~1.5 ms on the console); the walk's remaining ~12% is its per-object management (two sort lists, class lookups
and the clip for ~180 objects, the hook's copies for the worker) and the particle systems' per-emitter guest
chain (geodisp -> 0113ACB8 -> 1140ED0 -> disp_particle_emitter, ~10 guest calls an emitter). Halving that needs
a different walk (a host list of the drawn objects kept across frames, the static ones' clip by a spatial
structure, the particle emitters drawn in one native loop), not more layer cuts.

The runs above are on main 4ead274 (p1). The shipped build is rebased on main 9be600e (round 102, p2):
runsb/checkA2 (the altar, `SOTC_PTCL103_CHECK=1`) 252 000 particle draws, 0 differ; runs/finalR2 (route 6,
600 s, the console env) no fault, r103all +0.35 ms matched on the plain.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r103.vpk (main 9be600e + this round) with r103/env-console.txt
(`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r103all,ptcl103,solid103`), read with `build/agent-scratch/r103/read103.sh err.txt <from>`.

## Fix 103: the console crash loading a save (walk101's ends read 16-aligned on an 8-aligned stack) (2026-11-08)

celosia-r103.vpk crashed on the console during the area load after Load Game (~frame 776). Both core dumps
(build/agent-scratch/r103/console/psp2core-*.psp2dmp.tmp, parsed with vita-parse-core, symbolized with r103/p2.elf whose
eboot is byte-identical to the console's) stop the game thread on a data abort at
`decomp_collision::walk101Run(WalkCtx&, walk101::Ends, ...)+0x12a`: `vld1.64 {d16-d17}, [ip :128]`, ip = sp + 0xce0 =
0x911ffd28 / 0x910ffc68 (8-aligned, not 16), called from rootF.

Cause: `walk101::Ends` had `alignas(16)` members and walk101Run takes it by value. Under the AAPCS part of it arrives in
r2/r3 and the rest on the caller's stack; GCC stores r2/r3 below the stacked part (`sub sp, #8`) and uses the argument in
place, so it is only as aligned as the caller's sp (8), yet GCC reads it with 16-byte-aligned NEON loads. A data abort
whenever the call path leaves sp 8 mod 16 (the save load's does); Vita3K does not check alignment, so no Vita3K run showed it.

Fix: no `alignas` on Ends (ld / st go through memcpy). The fixed ELF has no `:128` / `:256` access at an sp-based address
anywhere (a scan of the whole disassembly; the r103 ELF had 7, all in walk101Run). Build: build/agent-scratch/celosia-fix103.vpk.

## Round 104: the characters' geometry on the guest worker (char104): exact, but no overlap to win; what blocks it (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r104/`: build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees
../vita3k-celosia-r104 / r104b), run.sh (one run: tree, VPK, route, seconds, env), ab.sh, read104.sh,
env-console.txt, syn.sh (host syntax check); runs/ and runsb/: censusA2 (the census), serialA1 / A2,
chk5A, chk6S (mode 2 checks), chk6P, chk8P (mode 1 checks), chk8R (the recompiled code against the
natives), par1A / par5A (first mode 1 runs), altar7 / attract8 / runsb/route7 (the A/B), finalR (600 s,
the console env). p0-p6 on main 9be600e, p7 / p8 rebased on b419fc5 (fix 103); p8 = celosia-r104.vpk.

**Why.** The console's game thread is 45-55 ms of CPU a 3D frame alone on core 0; the exact local
rewrites are exhausted (rounds 97, 101, 102). Cutting it by many ms needs part of its work on another
core. The brief: the characters' per-frame body work (ExecCharaGeometry: pose, IK, cloth, root dynamics
and their collision) of characters that do not interact this frame, on round 91's guest worker, with
identical results.

### Where each character's geometry sits (census, `SOTC_CHAR104_LOG=<n>`, the altar, Vita3K 222 MHz)

Each character's ExecCharaGeometry runs at its own sub-thread's frame end (decomp_scriptvm3 charaGeometry),
between the scripts of the objects woken before and after it. The census times every call since the
frame's first wake and wraps the class accessors (GetCharacterClass, GetLayoutClass, GetAnimationClass,
GetScriptClass, GetGeometryPointerObject / Position / Quaternion) to find the first read of a character by
another object after its geometry ran (`[char104o]`, `[char104r]`, `[seq104]`). Frames 5 657-6 257
(geometry 14.5-15.4 ms a frame of a 57-62 ms frame, probes included):

| character | geometry ms | first foreign read after it |
|---|---|---|
| Wander (the player) | 6.9 | 0.2 ms (the managers' tasks, the camera) |
| Wander's head (4-5 units away) | 3.4-4.0 | 0.04 ms (manager_sub_010AC4A0) |
| Mono's body / head / hair, two doves next to them | 0.3-0.8 each | 0.1-1 ms for two of them (the hair reads the head), 17-22 ms for the others |
| eight birds (0.1-0.2 ms each) | ~1.0 together | 25-29 ms (none until the walk) |

So the characters whose results nobody reads for long (the far birds, two of Mono's parts, the doves) are
the cheap ones: ~2.5-3 ms together at the altar; the expensive ones (Wander, his head) are read at once.

### What the geometry touches (`SOTC_CHAR104=2 SOTC_CHAR104_CALLS=1`: the worker's call targets)

296 functions under the 18 characters' geometry, among them shared state of every kind: the heap
(iosMallocAlign, malloc_from_src_partition), isys objects and groups (_isysCreateObj,
isysAddGroupWithLinkParam, isysGroupForFirst / Next / Exit: these take the isys kernel's global
recursive lock, a WaitSema), two-way links into the object a character stands on
(LinkSecureParentInfoByGP / UnlinkSecureParentInfo: every character, every frame, into the parent's +0x118
list), the collision finders and work areas, the skinned surfaces' caches of other characters
(EntryModifiedManager), sound (sePlay3D, sndSepReq), particle creation (create_and_boot_particle_geodisp,
boot_particle_emitter), the anime tables' sub-threads (ExecAnimeTableInfo, SequenceKickSE / Particle),
`rand`, and VU0's R register (the cloth step draws three random numbers a grid point: 1 050 of 1 957 jobs
drew some).

### What was built (decomp_char104.cpp, sotc_worker; `SOTC_CHAR104`, default 0)

- `SOTC_CHAR104=2`: a character's geometry, its area test and its Postprocess handed to the worker and
  joined at its frame end (no overlap): the worker's result against the game thread's.
- `SOTC_CHAR104=1`: an eligible character's (not the player, not the active colossus, farther than
  `SOTC_CHAR104_NEAR` = 12 from the player) geometry, area test (class +0x539) and Postprocess run on the
  worker; the frame end goes on (letters, sleep) and the script pass wakes the next objects. Eligible
  characters reached while it runs are queued behind it (a batch, in the pass's order).
- The worker's view: the game thread's context at the hand-over (R included: one random stream), the
  game's scratchpad, VU0 data and the work stack's bytes below 0x11f7140 at the same offsets in its own
  copies (callees that read slots they did not write read what the original would); a queued character's
  view is brought up to the game's at its own hand-over. At the join the three areas are merged back (a byte
  the game thread changed since the last hand-over stays; the work stack only below the game thread's sp:
  above it are live frames), and saved frame pointers / addresses of locals in the worker's copy of the work
  stack are moved to the work stack (without that, the mode 2 check found every saved pointer different).
- Beside the game thread the worker runs the recompiled code, not the natives (their host caches:
  decomp_collision's epochs and kept matrices, seg80's slots, are the game thread's), and parks (waits for
  the join) before libkernel, libc's heap, the heap, the isys kernel and the sound driver's requests, the
  partitions' malloc, the sound module, the anime tables and rand (`admitGeo`); after the join the rest runs
  alone with the natives.
- The game thread joins before anything the job may also do (kGate: another character's geometry and
  Postprocess, the random numbers (the cloth step, iosGetRandom*, rand / srand), the heap, objects, groups
  and links, collision finders and work areas, the skinned caches, sound, the anime tables; and round 91's
  particle / wind module gates), when it names a character of the batch (the accessors above), at the end of
  the script pass's group and at the frame's end. All the job's own side effects therefore come before the
  game thread's in the original order; the random stream is handed back at the join (`[char104] ... random
  taken N conflicts 0` in every run).
- A/B names `char104`, `r104all` (the same switch). Logs: `[char104]` every 600 frames (characters and
  batches a frame on the worker, the worker's ms, the game thread's wait at the joins, joins by site),
  `[char104g]` (joins by gate), round 91's `[worker91]` (job time, parks and where).

### Checks (`SOTC_CHAR104_CHECK=<n>`: every n-th batch, one character)

Main RAM is copied at the hand-over (S0); at the join the parallel outcome P is kept aside, S0 put back,
the reference run made (mode 2: the same calls on the game thread with the natives, on the work stack and
the frame end's sp; mode 1: the same recompiled code on the worker with the game thread waiting), S1
compared with P, and P put back. A word the reference wrote that P does not hold is a difference; the work
stack's and the sub-thread stacks' dead slots below their sp are counted apart (the sub-thread stack's
Postprocess frame is not merged back on purpose: by the join the frame end has slept there and a saved
register equal to the old value could not be told from an untouched one).

| run | mode | checks | differences (live words) | dead slots (work stack / sub-thread) | scratchpad / VU0 data |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/chk6S (p6) | 2, natives on the worker | 109 | 0 (307 counted then: all the Postprocess frame, apart since p8) | 0 / (307) | 0 / 0 |
| runsb/chk8P (p8) | 1, beside the game thread | 52 | 0 | 3 577 / 1 137 | 0 / 0 |
| runsb/chk8R (p8) | 2, the recompiled code on the worker against the natives on the game thread | 76 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 (registers too) |

The registers left at the job's end (caller-saved values) differ from the reference's in mode 1 (the
parked part runs with the natives after the join); nothing reads them (the frame end reloads its own).

### Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz, in-run A/B `SOTC_CHAR104=1 SOTC_AB_FLAG=char104 SOTC_AB_ROTATE=1 SOTC_AB_PERIOD=60`, matched by draws, off minus on)

| run | part | frame (on / off) | char104 |
|---|---|---|---|
| runs/altar7 | from 3 300 | 72.1 / 57.4 | -14.66 ms (the worker costs) |
| runsb/route7 | from 3 000 | 74.3 / 59.0 | -15.24 |
| runs/attract8 | riding, from 10 000 | 39.0 / 34.9 | -3.86 |
| runs/finalR | route 6 600 s, console env (guest on core 1), from 3 000 | | -12.11 |

At the altar 8-16 characters a frame go to the worker in 5-10 batches; the worker spends ~9-18 ms a frame
on them (the recompiled code is ~2-3x the natives) and the game thread waits ~9-16 ms a frame at the joins:
almost nothing runs in parallel. The joins come ~2 ms after the hand-over, at FlushCollisionWork (another
object's collision work, ~2 a frame), UpdateLayoutClassParentGeometry (the parent's children, 1 a frame),
iosMallocAlign (1 a frame), the anime tables (1 a frame) and the next batch's hand-over; 40-46% of the
batches park in their first 0.3-0.4 ms at isysGroupForFirst (the isys kernel's global lock) or at the
anime tables, after which the rest waits for the join. No crash or fault in any run: par1A, par5A, the
checks, the A/B (altar 4 800 frames, route 6 7 200, attract 17 900), runs/finalR (route 6, 600 s, the console env with the worker on core 1 only: 8 268 frames; char104 -12.11 ms matched).

### Conclusion: default off; what a real split needs

The mechanism is exact (0 differences in live words in both modes) but gains nothing: the characters
that could run long beside the game thread are the cheap ones (~3 ms at the altar, less elsewhere), and
even those are cut short by shared state the game uses everywhere: the isys kernel's global lock (group
walks), the heap, the parent links, collision work areas, the random stream. A split that pays needs, in
order: (1) the natives under ExecCharaGeometry made safe for two threads (the collision natives' epochs,
kept matrices and seg80 / probe84 slots per thread: the worker on the recompiled code is 2-3x slower), (2)
the collision object group's walk without the isys lock (a host snapshot of the group taken by the game
thread at the hand-over), (3) the secure-parent links and FlushCollisionWork deferred to the join in order
(nothing reads them in between while the parent is static), (4) a larger independent unit than one cheap
character (Agro while not ridden: ~3-4.5 ms, but Wander's scripts and collision read him). Without
(1)-(3) no selection of characters wins.

The ELF has no `:128` / `:256` NEON access at an sp-based address (fix 103's scan); the round's two aligned
accesses (kickAs, char104's static init) use registers realigned with `bic #15`.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r104.vpk (main b419fc5 + this round, p8). `SOTC_CHAR104` is 0
unless set: with r104/env-console.txt (`SOTC_CHAR104=1 SOTC_THREAD_CORES=guest:2 SOTC_AB_FLAG=char104`)
half the windows run the worker on core 1 and are expected to be slower; read with
`build/agent-scratch/r104/read104.sh err.txt <from>` (ab89's matched block; `[char104]` the waits).

## Round 105: room on cores 1-2: the hook worker's shadow volumes, the idle threads' 2 ms polling, the frame log's dtoa (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r105/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: its own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r105 and
-r105b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh (`load`: the console memcard and fix103's Load Game input), read105.sh, env-console.txt,
tools/threads105.py (per-thread CPU from a console log), thrcmp105.py / thr105.py (the Vita3K sampler by thread),
spalign105.py (the ELF's sp-based :128 / :256 NEON accesses), STATE.md).

**Where cores 1-2 go (console, r103/console/err-nowalk.txt, 3D frames from 1 500, 6 120 frames; ms a frame, mean / p90).**

| thread | mean | p90 | | game thread's waits | mean | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| game (core 0) | 46.3 | 65.4 | | jobs join (hookjoin sites) | 0.50 | 0.0 (move 0.39, screenblur 0.09) |
| render (core 2) | 21.8 | 29.4 | | sync end (endFrame) | 1.84 | 6.8 |
| hook worker | 9.5 | 16.5 | | sync log (the frame log, game thread) | 0.80 | 0.9 |
| loader | 5.2 | 6.2 | | lanehelp (38 jobs, 6.6 joins) | 1.04 | 1.5 |
| audio | 4.7 | 10.1 | | sched (blocked 0.55, hookjoin 0.08) | 0.64 | 0.6 |
| lane | 2.7 | 4.2 | | | | |
| build | 2.5 | 3.0 | | | | |
| dma | 2.4 | 3.1 | | | | |
| log | 2.4 | 3.1 | | | | |
| offload | 2.1 | 2.5 | | | | |
| main | 1.0 | 1.3 | | | | |
| cores 1-2 without render | 32.6 | | | | | |

(r100/console/err.txt, 1 824 frames: frame 60.5, game 56.8, worker 12.3, audio 8.7, loader 6.6, build 3.4, lane 3.1, dma 3.0,
log 2.8, offload 2.4; joins 1.61, cores 1-2 without render 43.4.) The game thread's joins on the worker and the lane are
already small (round 100's camera blur join); the threads beside the worker are what fills cores 1-2.

The Vita3K sampler at the altar (r105/runsb/sampBase, celosia-fix103) by thread: the hook worker is shadowDispDraw 35%,
newlib's memcmp 12.4%, modelDispDraw 13%, poseSkinned 7.6%, truncf 3.6%. The build thread (no builds in steady play) is
almost all pthread timed-wait machinery (sceKernelWaitSema / GetProcessTimeLow / LibcGettimeofday / PollEventFlag /
__udivmoddi4): its loop waited on a condition with a 2 ms timeout, ~25 wake-ups a frame for nothing, which on the console
are real syscalls (~2.5 ms of CPU a frame there with nothing to build). The render thread's idle wait was the same 2 ms
recheck. The log thread is _svfprintf_r / _dtoa_r (the per-frame line's ~60 float conversions) and the ring's memmove.

**What changed (default on; A/B names `worker105`, `build105`, `render105`, `log105`, `r105all` all four).**
- **worker105** (`SOTC_WORKER105`, sotc_native.cpp): the shadow volumes and the kick pass, the same results bit for bit.
  The parsed shadow model's guest bytes (compared at every shadow draw to know the parse still holds: ~15 KB a draw) and
  the skin records' palettes (skinAtKickWith) are compared 64 bytes at a time in NEON (`sameBytes105`; newlib's memcmp is
  a word loop with a branch per word); a skinned shadow vertex's bone index is `(float)(int)packed` for |packed| < 2^23
  (trunc's value; the weight `packed - index` the same, -0 included) instead of the truncf call, with the vertex in
  registers (the old loop reloaded x / y / z after each store: possible aliasing); the corner table's 24-byte memcmp is
  six word compares. `SOTC_WORKER105_CHECK=1` runs both ways: altar (runs/checkA1) 14 000 shadow draws, 215 MB of model
  bytes compared, 6.5 M skinned vertices, 4.8 M probes, **0 differences**.
- **build105** (`SOTC_BUILD105`, native_renderer.cpp AsyncBuilds): the build worker idles on a kernel semaphore. It says
  it sleeps under the mutex; flush() pushes under the same mutex and signals when it saw it asleep; the semaphore counts, so
  a signal before the wait is kept (no lost wake-up, the reason for the old 2 ms recheck in Vita3K); 20 ms timeout, as the
  hook worker's. The jobs run as soon as handed over, as before.
- **render105** (`SOTC_RENDER105`, native_renderer_gl.cpp): the render thread's idle wait the same way (every
  `m_work.notify_one()`, all under m_mutex, is followed by `wake105()`).
- **log105** (`SOTC_LOG105`, native_renderer.cpp `fmt105` / `logf105`): the frame log thread's per-frame lines (log76's
  write, its splits, threads::lineOf) formatted without newlib's dtoa: %.Nf (N 0-3) by integer arithmetic on v * 10^N,
  with snprintf for any number within 1e-6 of a rounding half, -0, NaN / inf or large; other conversions as before. The
  same text: `SOTC_LOG105_CHECK=1` compares every text with vsnprintf's (0 differ at the altar; a Mac test of 4 M random
  values against the C library, 0 differ).
- Thread placement is unchanged (priorities, cores). Build note: `sotc_vita_elf_room` 40 KB (vita-elf-create's "segment 1
  overlaps" came back with round 104 and this round together).

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz; Vita3K has no per-thread run clocks, so the per-thread CPU is the sampler's).**
- Sampler, the altar 160-290 s, the same VPK (p1) with the four off (runsb/sampOff) and on (runsb/sampOn), weight per game
  frame: hook worker 4.53 -> 3.97 (-12%: memcmp and truncf gone, sameBytes105 1.4% of it), build thread 0.189 -> 0.087
  (-54%), log thread 0.118 -> under 0.03, lane / dma / offload / audio unchanged. The render thread's guest code is
  unchanged; its HLE stubs (sceGxmSet*, sceClibMemcpy) cost twice the host time in the "on" run while sceGxmDraw stayed

## Round 107: Frame rate "Steady 20": an even 50 ms cadence on the game's own clock (2026-11-08)

**Why.** The console's frames (r103 console log, 6 637 3D frames) take 2, 3 or 4 VBlanks
(27 / 48 / 15%, 3% more): the game's step (dt) follows (27% 2, 52% 3, 15% 4 VBlanks) and the
display shows each picture as soon as the render thread has it, so the motion alternates 33 / 50 /
67 ms. The work is mostly between 33 and 50 ms (median period 48.1 ms): a fixed 50 ms cadence holds
for ~82% of the frames as they are.

**What the game does.** SotC's frame starts when its GP thread, polling at each VBlank once the GS has
finished the previous frame, receives the game thread's message on the bufferless frame box (0x1c8078,
iosRecvMsg(0x26d9a8, 0, 0): a poll; the game thread waits on the box's sender list +0x18). The step is
the EE clock (T0) between frame starts (round 10). The EE clock catches up with the host's when the game
thread parks; while a long frame runs the guest's VBlanks fall behind and are delivered in a burst at
its end, off the VBlank grid on the wall clock.

**Steady 20** (menu: Renderer, "Frame rate" / "Taxa de quadros": Auto | Steady 20 / 20 estável;
`frame_rate` in settings.cfg; `SOTC_CAP20=0/1` over it; default Auto, never forced):

- The release (sotc_overrides.cpp `cap20`, always hooked now; Auto passes every poll through) waits
  until 3 guest VBlanks have passed since the previous release and the wall time since it is within
  4 ms of a whole number of VBlanks (at least 2.5): a poll that comes late (the burst at a long frame's
  end) waits for the next VBlank, once. So a frame that fits starts 50 ms after the previous one, a long
  one 66.7 ms (the next VBlank after it ends), and the cadence counts from that release: no short frame
  after a long one. The game thread waits in its own frame wait: the other guest threads, the VBlank
  thread and the sound run on. Input is read at the frame's start as before.
- Only in frames with a scene (the round-36 rule of the 30 fps cap: 150 draws or more on, under 40
  off): loading screens, logos and menus over black run as in Auto (the loader steps once a frame).
  `[cap20] steady 20 on/off at vblank V` at each switch.
- The Vita's display holds each picture 3 refreshes (`g_cap20Active` -> the host loop's SetTargetFPS(20)
  -> vitaGL vsync interval 3: the display queue sets the picture and waits 3 VBlanks; a late picture is
  set when it is ready and shown from the next refresh, the next one 3 or more after it). Over the 30 fps
  cap. Tried and dropped (p6): the display callback (vglSetDisplayCallback, before vitaGL's vsync wait)
  setting vsync_interval to the latest release's interval, so a picture after a long frame would stay 4+
  refreshes like the game's step. The latest release is not the picture's own when pictures queue: a 5
  or 6 given to an older picture slowed the display, the swap blocked (present 35 ms, wait 16), frames
  ran over and released at 5-6, and it fed itself (final600b: releases 3: 2 671, 4: 2 086, 5: 1 238,
  6: 699; final600, p5, the same card and route: 581-585 of 600 at 3 after the first heavy minute). Doing
  it right needs each picture tagged with its frame's release through the render thread. With the fixed
  minimum, where frames run over (Vita3K's first heavy minute of the card's save, releases 4: 572 of
  600) the pictures came 3: 104, 4: 374, 5: 70 refreshes apart as the render thread's time moved.
- Latency: at most one picture waits for the display at a release (the game's 60.00 Hz VBlanks against
  a 59.94 Hz display, or a picture the render thread finished late, would fill vitaGL's 2-entry queue):
  with 2 or more waiting the release waits one VBlank (`SOTC_CAP20_QUEUE`, 0 off). A frame's picture
  is shown at the first 3-refresh slot after Auto would show it: at most one frame (50 ms) later.
- `[cap20] steady20|auto N frames` every 600 frames (while on, or with the frame log): the wall time
  between releases and the step in VBlanks, the step within 1 ms of 50, game time / wall, and on the Vita
  each picture's time on screen in display refreshes (vglSetDisplayCallback: the display's VBlank count
  between two pictures handed to the display). `SOTC_CAP20_TRACE=<n>`: `[cap20t]` per release.
  `PS2X_SETTINGS_PRESS=<key>` (testing): a menu item changed once at start as X does, and saved.

**Measured (own Vita3K tree, 222 MHz, route 6: Load Game -> altar -> out to the plain; the host had two
other Vita3K instances and builds running, load ~16-18, and ~1 s Vita3K stalls every ~4 s).**

| run | 3D frames | release intervals (VBlanks, wall) | step vs the wall interval | shown (refreshes) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s20c, Steady 20 (p3) | 4 157 released while on | 3: 3 739, 4: 382, 5: 29, 6+: 7; the 3s 50.05 ms sd 1.14 | within 2 ms in 99.4%; game / wall 0.981 | quiet windows: 3: 581-584 of 600, the rest 1 + 7+ pairs at the host stalls; the walk: 3: 260, 4: 223, 5: 71 (Vita3K at 222 MHz runs that scene over 50 ms) |
| autob, Auto (p2) | 5 951 | 1: 2 349, 2: 2 841, 3: 425, 4: 284 | within 2 ms in 85.2%; game / wall 0.938 (3D frames 20-130 ms) | mixed 1 / 2 / 3 (e.g. 1: 222, 2: 371) |

- Game speed: the route's input is timed in VBlanks; Wander's position by VBlank (SOTC_POS_LOG,
  r107/poscmp.py) follows Auto's within 5-22 units along the walk (the path is chaotic in frame timing,
  round 10) and ends 5.4 units from Auto's end point (s20a, p1: 4.1). The step tracks the wall clock
  closer than in Auto (0.981 against 0.938): each frame start follows a park, where the EE clock catches up.
- A first version (p2) anchored the release to the wall grid and held polls more than 4 ms early with no
  limit: when the guest's VBlanks came out of phase with the anchor the game thread was held 1-27 s
  (s20b). Every off-grid hold is now once per release (p3+).
- Settings: `PS2X_SETTINGS_PRESS=frame_rate` (runs/press) set Steady 20 as X does and saved
  `frame_rate=1`; runs on that file without SOTC_CAP20 started Steady 20 from it.
- 600 s, the final build (p5 = main 5d00aa0 + this round): runs/final600, the console's card
  (avion/console/Mcd001-console.ps2 copied into r107's own Vita3K tree), Load Game, the settings file
  above, the console env's logs: 7 271 frames, no crash or fault; after the save's first heavy minute
  (frames over 50 ms in Vita3K: releases 4: 572 of 600, shown 3: 104, 4: 374, 5: 70) every window had
  578-590 of 600 releases at 3 VBlanks and 581-585 pictures shown 3 refreshes (the rest: Vita3K's ~1 s
  host stalls, a 7+ and a 1 each). The ELF has no `:128` / `:256` NEON access at an sp-based address
  (r107/spalign.py over the whole disassembly; it finds round 103's seven in r103/p2.elf).

**The spike causes (console r103, spike100.py --local 15).** The game thread's own CPU (28%) and the
render thread (draw 20%, present / GPU 20%) are most of the spikes' excess; "sched: blocked" (11%) is
not the disc: 305 3D frames had more than 5 ms blocked, 227 of them with no disc read at all
(r107/blocked.py): it is the game waiting for the next VBlank (every guest thread waiting, the frame
release), which Steady 20 makes the cadence. "join: move" (5%) is the hook worker's join before a heap
move (round 105's code) and "frame end" (3%) the hand-over waiting for the render thread. Nothing cheap
and exact was left to cut in this round's scope.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r107.vpk (main 5d00aa0 + this round). Steady 20 is off unless
chosen: Select twice, R1 to the Renderer tab, "Frame rate" (just above "30 fps cap", near the end of the
list), X switches Auto / Steady 20 and saves at once. r107/env-console.txt has the frame and spike logs and
no A/B (the cadence is judged by playing). Read the log with `build/agent-scratch/r107/vbdist.py err.txt`
(3D frames by VBlanks per frame and step, and the `[cap20]` lines: the shown refreshes per 600 frames).

## Round 106: the scripts' subsystems as plain native code: the frame start's group fix-up (grp106), the animals' leader search (ai106), three object-animation evaluators (oan106, off) (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r106/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: its two Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r106 and -r106b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; v3km.sh / v3kbm.sh the same with `MCD=` a memcard to copy in;
samp.sh, check.sh, ab.sh, final.sh (the console env with the console memcard), read106.sh, env-console.txt,
tools/spalign.py (round 105's scan for sp-based :128 / :256 NEON accesses), STATE.md).

**Where the time is (Vita3K host sampler, the altar, % of the game thread; runs/sampOff vs runsb/sampOn, the same
VPK with the round off / on, window 160-290 s).** Round 102's probe sampler put the scripts' items at 1.5 ms (the
small animals' AI), 0.9 ms (object animations) and 1.3 ms (the frame start / finish managers) at the altar, but with
its probes on (~1.2x) and counting guest pcs that natives set: most of those functions were already native
(animalStep, steer, animalMove, aiParam, curveEval, execObjectAnimation, texResetFast ...). Without probes the
whole small-animal set is 2.7% of the game thread, 40 functions, the biggest recompiled one 0.12%; the object
animations 3.5% (1.15 of it the characters' motion key decoder, round 104's area); the frame managers ~1%. What
was left recompiled or wasted calls:

| function | off | on | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| groupFix (gamecore_sub_013448C0, the frame start task's attachment fix-up) | 0.33 | 0.15 | grp106 |
| isysGetGroupSrhNext (called only by groupFix) | 0.11 | 0 | grp106 |
| isysGroupForNext + decomp_group::nextAt | 0.17 | 0.17 | grp106 (the same work, no call) |
| gamecore_sub_013E1520 (the animals' leader search) + GetScriptCharacterClass | 0.16 | 0.08 | ai106 |
| 010AF2A0 / 010AF4D8 / 010B06A8 (object-animation key evaluators) | 0.30 | 0.33 | oan106: no gain, left off |

grp106 + ai106: -0.37% of the game thread at the altar (~0.18 ms of ~48 ms in Vita3K; ~0.15-0.2 ms on the console's
~45 ms). The animals' leader search runs ~3 times a frame at the altar, groupFix once.

**What changed.**
- **grp106** (`SOTC_GRP106`, default on; decomp_hot44c.cpp `groupFix`, decomp_group.cpp `nextAt`). groupFix walks
  the frame's group: for each object its layout class, for an attached one its legal parent searched along the rest
  of the group (isysGetGroupSrhNext per step: O(n^2) guest calls), else its character class. Those leaves
  (GetLayoutClass's plain cases: +0x20 / +0x90 / none by the type byte's table; GetCharacterClass: types 9 / 0x16;
  SrhNext: the raw chain's next entry; ForNext: decomp_group::next, the native's own body, with its iteration counts)
  are done in place when their jal sites name them (read live); ForFirst / ForExit (the group's semaphore), the
  legal parent, the geometry pointer and the delete / insert of a move stay guest calls. The same values and RAM
  writes in the same order; only scratch registers between guest calls differ (none is read).
  `SOTC_GRP106_CHECK=1`: every inline leaf also runs as the recompiled leaf and the two results are compared.
- **ai106** (`SOTC_AI106`, default on; decomp_ai106.cpp). 013E1520, called by every small animal's script body
  each frame: leaders (kinds 6 / 8) lead themselves; others look through the animals' group (0x146590c) for the
  first leader of the same flock (+8, +4), not in state 0x24 and below state 0x12, and set +0x28 / +0x2c / +0x38 /
  +0x3c / +0x584 (013E1460 when it becomes its own leader, the +0x360 handle freed when it stops). Natively with
  isysGetThisSubThread, GetScriptCharacterClass and ForNext in place, ForFirst / ForExit / 013E1460 / 1B0328 as
  guest calls with the original's ra and frame. `SOTC_AI106_CHECK=1`: the record's result is predicted (a read-only
  walk), the native runs on the live state (when no 013E1460 / free is due), the record (0x600 bytes) and the
  context are put back, the recompiled code runs to its return; native, prediction and recompiled compared.
- **oan106** (`SOTC_OAN106=1`, default OFF; decomp_hot46h.cpp). GetObjectAnimationFloatFrame's evaluators 010AF2A0
  (objectAnimSample's code with the record in s4 and out +0x30 = the record's +0x10: a template now), 010AF4D8 (a
  float-vector channel) and 010B06A8 (a curve key, a vec3 key, an int and a colour). Exact (below), but in the
  register-for-register form of round 46 they cost what the recompiled code does (0.30 -> 0.33%); a gain would need
  the keys decoded in host locals with no context traffic. Left in, off.
- Full checks for any of the three: `SOTC_xxx106_CHECK=2` puts its natives in the difftest's list (every RAM byte;
  ~0.7 s a check in Vita3K: use SOTC_DIFFTEST_FIRST / _EVERY to thin it).

**Checks (Vita3K, every call checked).** runs/checkA1 (the altar, 300 s): grp106 2.1 M leaf compares, ai106 16 400
calls (16 370 with the native leg), oan106 49 000 / 49 000 / 65 000 calls; 0 differences. runsb/checkR1 (route 6,
600 s): grp106 1.8 M, ai106 32 800 (32 750), oan106 16 000 each; 0 differences. runsb/checkT2 (the attract demo
with riding, 600 s, p2 with `SOTC_OAN106=1`): grp106 2.6 M, ai106 16 400 (16 370), oan106 16 000 / 16 000 / 33 000;
0 differences. The full difftest (`SOTC_GRP106_CHECK=2 SOTC_AI106_CHECK=2`, every RAM byte, the first 30 calls then one in 150;
runs/diffA1, the altar 360 s): groupFix and 013E1520 matched in every check but groupFix's first, one byte at
0x29126c; the control run with grp106 off (runsb/diffC1: the round-44 native, the same checks) differs in the same
byte at the same first check: an artifact of the check around the group's semaphore calls, not of this round.

draws, off minus on, ms; the p2 runs with `r106all,grp106,ai106`).**

## Round 108: the character jobs' blockers as infrastructure: the collision natives per thread, the worker on the natives, the isys group walks from a snapshot (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r108/` (build.sh pN, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r108 /
-r108b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh <a|b> <vpk> <name> <secs> <route2|route6|load|none> [env]; read108.sh; tools/globals108.py
(an override object's writable data: the host state audit); env-console.txt; STATE.md). p1-p6 on main 5d00aa0 (round 105),
p7 rebased on 4e18b7f (round 107), p8 on 3a1b641 (round 106) = celosia-r108.vpk.

**Why.** The first of the rounds aimed at real parallelism of the game thread. Round 104 put far characters' geometry on
round 91's guest worker: exact but slower, for three reasons it named: (1) the collision natives keep host caches the game
thread uses, so the worker ran the recompiled code (2-3x slower); (2) 40-46% of batches parked at isysGroupForFirst (the isys
kernel's global lock) or the anime tables; (3) the game thread hits gates ~2 ms after the hand-over. This round removes what
can be removed as infrastructure, with nothing changed on the game thread, and measures what is left. `SOTC_CHAR104` stays 0.

### What changed

- **Lanes** (always on; sotc_decomp.h `lane()` / `onWorkerLane()`: 0 the game thread, 1 the guest worker, told by its runtime
  shell, one compare; no TLS: the Vita's `thread_local` is emutls). The host state was found by listing every override
  object's writable data (tools/globals108.py) and reading the natives under ExecCharaGeometry:
  - decomp_collision: the epoch (`g_guestRuns`, now one per lane with `g_guestRunsW`; both go up at a job's hand-over and
    join), round 101's kept matrices (the leaf's `keptM` / `keptM2`) and the plane-table, boundary and attribute "chains":
    one per lane. They live within one native entry, so each lane's values are good exactly as before.
  - The memos (answers kept across entries and frames): seg80 and round 84's path pool, round 65's cammemo, probe84's water
    probe, decomp_hot47j's find84 and g85, probe85's records, ground85's capture (`g_cap`: its depth stack is now only written
    while capturing) and view (`g_view`). Lane 0's only: on the worker the computation runs (the original's), so a job
    neither reads the game thread's kept answers nor fills them, and the game thread's hits are its own calls'.
  - Stats-only state (NativeCount, FastCheck, the log counters, env switches) is left as it is.
- **nat108** (`SOTC_NAT108`, 1 with `SOTC_CHAR104=1`): beside the game thread a job runs 81 natives of an audited list
  (sotc_worker.cpp `kNat108`: ExecCharaGeometry itself, the motion / IK / cloth / layout natives, the collision finder,
  leaf, node, clipDB, keep, boundary, plane, attribute, vertices, EntryModified / FlushModified, FlushCollisionWork, ...)
  instead of their recompiled code; any other native stays recompiled. Each was read for host state (none but statistics,
  or laned) and for direct C++ calls into code the worker may not run beside the game thread (none: their guest calls go
  through callGuest / callNative, so through hookCall's admit and park, as the recompiled code's do).
- **snap108** (`SOTC_SNAP108`, 1 with `SOTC_CHAR104=1`): isysGroupForFirst / Next / Exit of the groups jobs walk are
  answered on the worker from a copy of their lists the game thread makes at the hand-over (sotc_worker `snapGroups`: each
  group's links as the walk functions would find them then), without the isys lock (taken and given back, nothing else)
  and without the objects' walk counts (+9): the job's walks keep their own counts, so a walk of another group (the
  recompiled code's) keeps the real ones, and a count a walk leaves raised goes into +9 at the join (0 in every run). The
  groups are learned (a job's ForFirst of a group not in the copy parks as before and names it; kept while walked, dropped
  after 600 frames, up to 64): the collision object group 0x0146588c, 0x014658a4 / 0x01465884, and each cloth's
  string-object group (the cloth velocity step's walk at 0x01137728). A character queued behind a running batch is refused
  when a copied group changed since the copy (appends refused: 0 in every run).
- **anime108** (`SOTC_ANIME108`, default 0): ExecAnimeTableInfo's calls (ExecCharaGeometry's last step) kept with their
  context and 0x400 bytes of stack and made at the batch's end after the join, each character's area test and Postprocess
  after its own (sotc_worker `deferNext` / `deferHost`). Not exact: the check found 100 words differing in 165 checks (0
  without it): the tables' events read the game's state of the moment they run (the running sub-thread's object at
  0x1e1550, which the game thread has moved on by then), so their sound / effect records differ. Left off.
- admitGeo: the anime tables' deny range now ends at 0x01169B70 (and rand / srand 0x0116AD00-0x0116AD80): the path data
  getters, the segment / triangle test at 0x0116A0D4 (a native), qsort and rintf between them run beside the game thread.
- Measuring: `[char108]` every 600 frames (the worker's time before it parked within each batch's hand-over-to-join window,
  "beside the game thread"; the game thread's time in those windows; its waits; snapshot answers / misses / links / left
  counts / groups; appends refused; anime tables kept), `[worker91]`'s park sites (target / caller), `[char104g]`'s joins by
  gate and caller and whether a FlushCollisionWork / UpdateLayoutClassParentGeometry a0 is one of the batch's characters.
  Check reference `SOTC_CHAR108_REF` (bit 1, default on: the same natives; bit 0: the snapshot too; by default the isys

## Round 109: the character jobs beside the game thread: the anime tables when no event is due, the worker's open queue, the gates by object; what still joins (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r109/` (build.sh pN, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r109 /
-r109b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh, ab.sh, read109.sh, env-console.txt, STATE.md). p1-p3 on main 6c652cc (round 108); p3 =
celosia-r109.vpk.

**Why.** Round 108 left char104 (far characters' geometry on round 91's guest worker) exact but a loss: at the altar only
1.2-1.5 ms of the worker's 8-12 ms a frame ran beside the game thread, the worker parked in ~45% of the batches at the anime
tables and the game thread waited 9-14 ms a frame at its joins. This round takes the plan's steps 1-4 as far as they go
exactly, each with a switch, a check and an A/B.

### What changed (all under `SOTC_CHAR104=1`, which stays 0 by default)

- **anime109** (`SOTC_ANIME109`, 1): ExecAnimeTableInfo (0x1169020: a0 the table info, a1 the object, f12 the time) read
  from the code: per list (+0 / +8 non-zero, cursor +4 / +0xc, 8-byte entries: time, handle) it writes the tables' globals
  (0x118fe88-0x118fe98 and three quads at 0x122b860) and from the cursor either ends the list (a handle with no owner, the
  empty owner 0x1e0ed4, or one that resolves to 0: cursor cleared), stops (the entry's time above f12: cursor kept) or runs
  the entry's event (manager_sub_011688A8: sounds, particles, sequences, rand) and goes on. A call that runs no event
  ("quiet") writes only the globals, its cursors and its frame; the globals are read only by the events' code (xref:
  manager_sub_01167928 .. 011688A8, reached only from ExecAnimeTableInfo / ExecEff, which write them first), so they are
  dead between calls.
  - On the worker a quiet call runs beside the game thread (sotc_worker `setAdmitCtx`: a refused target admitted from its
    arguments); a call with an event due still parks.
  - On the game thread a quiet call (manager_sub_01107090's script animation tables) goes on without the join; the
    globals it leaves are put back at the join (the game thread's calls come after the job's in the original order). Not
    in a checked batch (the reference would write the job's globals last).
  - ExecEff (0x1169388, also writes and reads the globals) joins (new gate).
  - The predictor (p3): an event's handlers read the game's state of their moment (the player, the camera, the effect
    pools), so an event run late after a park is not exact (the long check of p2 found it: 3 words in 1 of 125 batches,
    the effect pool's heads 0x270c14 / 0x270c84 and an event sub-thread's stack word). Each table info's time of its last
    calls (game thread and worker) gives the next one; a character with a cursor entry not above last + 2 steps is not
    handed over (it runs on the game thread, the batch joined at its geometry's gate). A miss is counted ("events on the
    worker").
- **open109** (`SOTC_OPEN109`, 1): the worker waits for the next character at the end of its queue until the game thread
  joins (sotc_worker `setJoinHook`: every join first closes the queue), so a character reached while the worker is idle is
  an append instead of a join and a new batch.
- **obj109** (`SOTC_OBJ109`, 1; `SOTC_OBJ109_R`, 40): FlushCollisionWork / UpdateLayoutClassParentGeometry (and the
  object's own FlushCollisionWorkByWorkStruct / FlushModifiedManager inside) go on without the join when the object's
  position (its layout class's +0x150, the class by FlushCollisionWork's type table) is farther than R from every
  character of the batch. A monitor checks it: the worker's GetLayoutClass (a visit) and EntryCollisionFinder (an entry)
  calls with the game thread's sequence number of the gates let go; a visit / entry of such an object after it was let go
  is a violation (`[obj109]`). In checked batches too.
- **cur109** (`SOTC_CUR109`, 1, no A/B): while the worker runs exclusive (after a park; the game thread waits), 0x1e1550
  (the running sub-thread's object) holds the value of the current character's hand-over (sotc_worker `setResumeHook`),
  the game thread's put back at the batch's end.
- Measuring: `[char109]` every 600 frames (quiet calls on the worker / game thread, globals put back, characters held for
  an event, events on the worker, open-queue waits and appends, gates let go and why kept (near: object and distance; the

With everything on, more characters go to the worker (the kick joins that ended a batch are gone, so far characters
reached later in the pass join the batch) and 2.5x as much of its time runs beside the game thread; the game thread's
waits stay ~10 ms because the remaining joins (below) come ~0.5 ms after a hand-over while a batch takes ~1.8 ms.

### What still joins, and why the worker still loses


- The flush / parent gates the game thread still meets are for objects **at** a batch character (distance 0-1): the
  characters' own collision aliases and carried objects, moved by their scripts every frame (st_collisionalias,
  nico_weaponUpdateGeometry). Real dependencies; R makes no difference (the far objects are let go: 0-1 a frame).
- Access joins (~1 a frame, 1.7-3 ms each, the worst): gamecore_sub_013DD8D0+0x7c (GetLayoutClass of a batch character,
  through a pointer: a script reading another character) and nico_horseClothOverSurfDetectFunc (Agro's cloth testing a
  character's surface). Real reads of the job's results.
- create_letter's iosMallocAlign (1 a frame): not removable exactly. The jobs allocate every frame
  (CreateSubLinkObjByGeometryPointer -> _isysCreateObj -> iosMallocAlign / iosCreatePartitionWithPc, ~1 a frame; particle
  geodisps rarely, `[worker91]` exclusive heap calls), so a letter allocated before the job's allocation would change the
  heap's order. Step 4 of the plan is dropped; a separate deterministic arena for the jobs would be the way.
- The worker is ~2x slower than the game thread on the same characters (0.6-0.8 ms a character), so every join that
  comes ~0.5 ms after a hand-over still waits ~1 ms.

### Conclusion

The round's three parts work as intended and are exact in the checks: the anime tables' park is gone (8-10% of the
batches park instead of 45%, with everything on), the kick joins became appends, and the part of the worker's time spent
beside the game thread went from 1.2-1.5 ms to 2-4 ms a frame at the altar. anime109 and open109 are each worth 3-4.6 ms
a frame inside char104 (altar and route 6). char104 as a whole is still a loss (altar -6.1 / -6.4 ms, route 6 -5.8 / -3.1,
attract -3.4; round 108: -9.3 / -5.6), because what remains are real dependencies on the characters' results within ~0.5 ms of
their hand-over and the worker's 2x speed. `SOTC_CHAR104` stays 0. Step 5 (a bigger unit) is where a win could come from:
a unit whose results nobody reads for many ms (round 104's census: only the cheap far birds qualify at the altar), or a
worker as fast as the game thread (the remaining recompiled callees of the jobs as natives).

The ELF has no `:128` / `:256` NEON access at an sp-based address (spalign105: 0 of 566).

## Round 110: per-picture display timing: each picture shown on the refresh its game time asks for (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r110/` (build.sh pN; v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: two Vita3K trees of its own,
../vita3k-celosia-r110 and -r110b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; go.sh a|b pN name route6 secs [env]: the round's logs; MCD=<card> copies a
memcard into that tree only; pace110.py the reader; poscmp.py, spalign.py from round 107; STATE.md).

**Why.** Round 107's Steady 20 holds the game's frame starts to a 3-VBlank grid and vitaGL's vsync interval 3 holds each
picture at least 3 refreshes. Where frames run over 50 ms the frame starts stay on the grid (3 or 4 VBlanks) but the pictures
landed 3 / 4 / 5 refreshes apart: the display showed each picture when the render thread had it, so the render thread's time
moved the motion. Its p6 (the display interval from the latest release) gave timing to the wrong picture when pictures queued.

**What changed (SOTC_PACE110, default on; A/B `pace110`).**
- Tag: every frame release (sotc_overrides.cpp cap20, Auto and Steady 20) is counted (`native_renderer::g_paceSeq`) and timed,
  with the game's dt of the frame before (`ps2x_vita_pace_release`). The native renderer's hand-over takes the count into the
  frame (read by the render thread when it picks the frame up: a deferred present runs after the next hand-over may start);
  `presentNow` passes it with the present (`ps2x_vita_pace_tag`, the render thread's own), and EndDrawing queues it beside
  vitaGL's display queue (one entry a swap, in order). Measured: the tagged release is the picture's own frame (swap 33-60 ms
  after its release; its dt matches its release interval).
- Present: vitaGL's display callback (the display queue's thread, before sceDisplaySetFrameBuf) takes the tag back and sets
  the picture on the refresh before its slot: slot = the previous slot + the frame's release interval in VBlanks (at least the
  minimum hold: 3 in Steady 20, 2 with the 30 fps cap). So each picture stays on screen as long as the game's time moved
  (Steady 20's 4-VBlank frames: exactly 4). vitaGL's own vsync wait is 1 while on (the slot is held in the callback).
- Late pictures: shown at the next refresh, the slots go on from there (one interval longer, none shorter after it).
- Latency: the slots aim at the floor A = the least arrival latency (swap + 2 refreshes - release) of the last 64 pictures.
  After a hitch (a release gap or 12+ refreshes on screen, or a picture 6+ refreshes late) the pictures queued behind it are
  shown a refresh apart (at least) until the latency is back at A ("catch-up": the hitch is the glitch, nothing after it).
  Otherwise, when 6 pictures in a row were already queued as the one before went on screen and the latency is above A + 1, one
  slot comes a refresh earlier ("pull"; the 60.00 Hz game against the 59.94 Hz display adds a refresh every ~17 s).
  `SOTC_PACE110_CALM=<n>` (6) is that count.
- The callback takes no lock: in Vita3K a lock wait there (stdio in the trace, a static-init guard) ended in a host
  `condition_variable wait failed: Invalid argument` abort at boot (3 of 5 runs of p3: the guest thread waits on the lock's
  own mutex with the display thread's condition variable while Vita3K's display queue waits on the same variable with the
  thread's mutex). The callback's windows and trace are handed to the presenting thread, which prints them after its swap;
  the settings are read before the callback is installed. 0 such aborts in the 14 runs after it.
- `[pace110]` every 600 pictures (on / off apart, one display mode a window; the statistics run with the pacing off too):
  refreshes each picture stayed; shown against the release interval and against the game's dt (in refreshes: 0 = shown as long
  as the game's time moved); latency release -> on screen; late pictures, pulls, catch-ups, chain resets; the same for the
  quiet pictures (20 or more after a hitch: in Vita3K the host stalls ~1 s every few seconds; the console has no such stalls).
  `SOTC_PACE110_TRACE=<n>`: `[pace110t]`, one line per picture. Reader: `build/agent-scratch/r110/pace110.py [--skip N] err.txt`.
- `SOTC_PACE110_HYST=1` (default off): Auto's frame floor with hysteresis (the frame's own length into a ring; up one when 5 of
  the last 15 needed more, down when at most 3 of the last 30 needed more than one less; 1-3 VBlanks, held with Steady 20's grid
  rules); `[cap20]` lines count the floor. Left off: in autoHyst6 it sat at 3 for 60% of the frames (Auto became Steady 20 with
  4s: shown 3: 35%, 4: 13%) and the route's walk desynced; the pacing alone already makes Auto's display follow its steps.

**Measured (own Vita3K trees, 222 MHz; the host ran round 109's two Vita3K and builds: ~1 s stalls every few seconds, so the
quiet columns are the cadence, the totals include the stalls' catch-up).** Pairs ran at the same time on the two trees.

| run (600 s, console card, Load Game, route 6) | shown 3 / 4 (all) | shown = release interval (all) | quiet: shown = release interval | quiet -1 / +1 | latency mean (refreshes), mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steady 20, pace off (off600s20, p7) | 76% / 15% | 81% | 91% | 4% / 5% | 11.4, 6-7 |
| Steady 20, pace on (final600s20, p7) | 70% / 18% | 84% | **99%** | 0% / 1% | 12.2, 6 |
| Auto, pace off (off600auto, p7) | shown 2: 13%, 3: 52% | 69% | 78% | 13% / 8% | 10.1, 6 |
| Auto, pace on (final600auto, p7) | shown 2: 68%, 3: 9% | 85% | **93%** | 2% / 5% | 8.7, 4 |

## Round 111: the character jobs' own costs: the worker's 2x was the hand-over's copies; areas as deltas, characters read early kept; a win before round 110, not after (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r111/` (build.sh pN, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r111 /
-r111b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh, ab.sh (TL / TR / TA: the altar's / route 6's / attract's seconds), read111.sh,
env-console.txt, STATE.md). p0-p12 on main 34d21ac (round 109), p13 / p14 rebased on c183511 (round 110); p14 =
a default-on candidate (measured below); p15 = p14 with SOTC_CHAR104 still 0 = celosia-r111.vpk.

**Why.** Round 109 left char104 (far characters' geometry on round 91's guest worker) exact but a loss (altar -6.4 ms,
route 6 -3.1 to -5.8): the game thread waited ~10 ms a frame at its joins and the worker took ~2x the game thread's time per
character. The brief, in order: (1) the census's hottest recompiled callees as lane-safe natives until a character costs the
worker what it costs the game thread; (2) characters read early by others kept on the game thread or handed over first;
(3) a deterministic allocation scheme for the jobs, only if exact.

### 1. Where the worker's time went (census with time, `SOTC_CHAR104_CALLS=2`)

The census now times each call the worker makes (hookCall: self and inclusive us, park waits taken out; `[calls104t]`,
N: a native the game thread runs, L: in nat108's list). runs/census1 (p1, the altar, 600 frames): ExecCharaGeometry's
inclusive time on the worker 0.39 ms a character (with the census's own cost) against 0.28 on the game thread
(runsb/serial1, `SOTC_CHAR104_LOG`); the natives the game thread runs and the worker did not were few and small:
motionKeys (010B81F8, 97 ms self / 138 inclusive over 600 frames), axisRotate (001BBDA8, 88 / 97), curveEval (010AC6C8, 84,
82 532 calls), windZones (01145F78, 35 / 45), acosExact (001BE388, 33 / 36), then sqrtf, atan2Exact, atanf, axisDirZY, diffQuat
(under 4 ms). All ten were read for host state (none but statistics: decomp_curve's counters, NativeCount; their guest calls go
through callGuest) and joined nat108's list (91 entries). The hottest recompiled callees left (GetClothDynamics 01137A68
88 / 312 ms, CalcRootFitting 010E21C0 84 / 121, GetMotionNodeQuaternionPosToolCoord 010B63F8 80 / 90, 010AEE18 74 / 109,
nico_neckFitToParentInvDirIK 01374D98 45 / 75, ExecAnimeTableInfo 37 / 49, ...) have no native: they cost both threads alike.

The worker's missing time was outside the calls: the item's `[char104]` time was 0.69 ms a character against 0.39 in its
calls. Timing the parts (p2, runs/diag2, the altar, a frame): **bringing the areas 2.7-3.1 ms on the worker** (round 104's
bring: the work stack's copy, the scratchpad and VU0 data brought to each character's hand-over), **the hand-over copies
1.2 ms and the joins' merges 1.8-2.2 ms on the game thread**. Round 104's bring / merge compared 16 bytes at a time with
memcmp (a call per 16 bytes); with a NEON select (the same rule byte by byte: a byte the game changed takes the game's; at the
join a byte the game did not change takes the worker's) and a NEON relocate (p3, runs/diag3): areas 0.33 ms, merges 0.21,
the game thread's waits 7.0 -> 2.8 ms a frame, the worker's characters 3.9 ms for 14 (0.28 ms each: the game thread's speed).

| build (altar, a frame, everything on) | worker: areas / characters | game thread: copies / merges / hand-over path | waits |
|---|---|---|---|
| p2 (round 109's copies) | 2.73-3.14 / 4.1-4.4 ms | 1.18 / 1.84-2.18 / - | 7.03 |
| p3 (NEON bring / merge) | 0.32-0.33 / 3.87-3.90 | 0.86-0.92 / 0.21 / - | 2.79-2.80 |
| p8 (delta111, a test per 16-byte chunk) | 0.013 / 3.31 | 0.08 / 0.33 / 1.75 (deltas 1.43) | 2.6 |
| p9 (256-byte block tests) | 0.016 / 3.37 | 0.08 / 0.30 / 1.25 (deltas 0.93) | 2.6 |
| p11 (+ spr111) | 0.015 / 3.36 | 0.07 / 0.38 / 0.96 (deltas 0.65) | 2.7 |

### delta111: the areas as deltas (`SOTC_DELTA111`, 1; A/B `delta111`)

What changes between hand-overs (`SOTC_CHAR111_DIFF=1`, `[char111d]`, altar and route 6): ~24 of the work stack copy's 772
16-byte chunks, **none** of the scratchpad's 1 024 or VU0 data's 256. So the game thread keeps one copy of its areas as of the
last hand-over / join (`g_roll`): a batch's first character brings the worker's areas (equal to the copy since the last join)
to the game's now at kickAs's setup by the chunks that changed (the worker idle); an appended character carries the chunks
changed since the previous hand-over, old and new values (the worker applies round 104's byte rule to them); the join merges
against the copy and writes the result to the game's area (the work stack's below the game's sp only, as before), the copy and
the worker's area. When another job ran on the worker since (round 91's particle job, a check's reference) everything is
copied whole. A first version tested chunk by chunk (each test a NEON-to-core move) and cost more than the copies it replaced
(1.43 ms a frame); the tests are now by 256-byte blocks.
**spr111** (`SOTC_SPR111`, 1): the scratchpad out of the appended characters' deltas (the game uses it in the display walk,
not in the script pass). Monitored: the join's merge sees whether the game changed the scratchpad in the batch's window, the
guest memory slow path counts the worker's scratchpad accesses (`ps2_worker::g_sprTouch`, ps2_memory.cpp); both in one batch
is a violation (counted, spr111 then off). In every run: the game changed it in 0 batches, the jobs used it in 0.

Exactness of the delta (`SOTC_DELTA111_VERIFY=1`: full copies taken too; on the worker round 104's bring on a copy of its
areas against the delta, the copy against the last hand-over's areas at each join and first character):
runs/ver5 (p5) 11 136 characters, runsb/chk7 (p7, 600 s) 23 511, runsb/ver9r (p9, route 6) 35 902, runsb/chk11 (p11, 600 s)
19 862, runs/ver15s2 / runsb/ver15b (p15, route 6, spr111 off / on) 26 870 / 27 982: **0 bytes off**, the copy 0 off.
Checked batches run the delta too (their full copies kept for the reference). One exception, open: runsb/chk15 (p15, the
checks and the verify together) counted 144 bytes off and 144 in the copy over 22 095 characters (27 by frame 1 218, then
growing), while its 101 checks found 0 differing words and the same build without the checks 0 in 54 852 characters; the
verify's full copies of a checked batch are taken before kickAs (which joins the previous job) and the delta's after, so the
two can see different moments, but this was not traced to the byte.

### 2. Characters read early: hold111 (`SOTC_HOLD111`, 1; `SOTC_HOLD111_FRAMES`, 60; A/B `hold111`)

The access joins (another object naming a batch character through the accessors: gamecore_sub_013DD8D0's GetLayoutClass,
Agro's cloth nico_horseClothOverSurfDetectFunc's GetCharacterClass; ~1 a frame at the altar, 1.7-3 ms each) are ordered by the
script pass: a character cannot be handed over earlier than its own frame end. So a character named by such a join is marked
and stays on the game thread while foreign reads of it go on (the accessors' wrappers refresh the mark; it lapses 60 frames
after the last). At the altar 1-2 characters a frame are held; access joins 750 -> 0-10 per 600 frames. A held character's
own geometry on the game thread joins a running batch at its geometry gate instead (0.21 ms a frame at the altar). A/B hold111
(off minus on): altar +0.21 (runs/altarAB3, p3), route 6 +0.03 (runsb/routeAB3), route 6 console env +0.24 (runsb/finalR12).

### 3. The jobs' allocations: not done

create_letter's iosMallocAlign join costs 0.15 ms a frame at the altar (the waits by gate below), and the jobs' own heap calls
are rare there (3 per 600 frames, `[worker91]` exclusive heap calls: _isysCreateObj's iosCreatePartitionWithPc / iosMallocAlign,
CreateSubLinkObjByGeometryPointer's iosMallocAlign). Letting the letter's allocation go first is exact only if the two
allocations touch disjoint heap state: they come from different heaps (the letters' at *(0x1e1344), the jobs' from a new
partition and the object's own), but the allocator updates one free-memory counter for all heaps (0x1e0bf0: commutative) under
one lock, and partition creation's parent heap was not traced. Not provable here for 0.15 ms; dropped.

All real dependencies (objects moved with the characters, their children, another character's geometry). The characters'
runs before the join: 1.15 of 3.38 ms a frame; 31% of the characters ran less than a quarter of their time before it
(runs/diag11).

### Few characters, no gain: SOTC_CHAR111_MIN (6)

A hand-over costs the game thread ~0.07 ms (deltas, kick) plus its share of the join's merge, ~0.1 ms a character. With
few characters a frame the overlap does not pay: attract riding (2.9 characters a frame) -0.57 ms (runs/attractQ12, p12),
route 6 after the shrine (3.3) +0.09, the altar (14) +0.41. Characters go to the worker only in frames after one with at
least 6 eligible characters (a choice of thread: the results are the same). In the attract demo it hardly applied (runs/attractQ14:
0.1 characters a frame left by it: those frames have 6 or more eligible characters, of which 3-5 reach the worker after
the holds and the anime predictor).

under ~0.4 ms are within it. Every run had Vita3K's 1 s host stalls (64-220 frames over 1 s a run: the host locked); ab89
leaves frames over 700 ms out.

### Conclusion

The brief's diagnosis was half right: the worker was ~2x slower, but not because of its callees (the ten natives it lacked
were worth little; the rest of its calls cost the game thread the same). It was round 104's hand-over itself: comparing and
copying ~32 KB of areas per character with a memcmp call per 16 bytes, on both threads. With that vectorized and turned into
deltas, a character costs the worker what it costs the game thread (0.24-0.28 ms at the altar), the game thread's waits fell
from ~10 ms to ~2.7 ms a frame, and its own cost of the jobs from ~3.4 to ~1.3 ms a frame. On main before round 110 that made
char104 a small gain (altar +0.41 ms, route 6 +0.27 and +0.36 in the console env; attract riding -0.57).

**It stays off by default**: rebased on round 110 (per-picture display timing), the qualification set was not clean in
Vita3K: the altar gained 1.13 ms but route 6 (console env) lost 0.71 and attract riding 3.52. In those two runs the worker
started 0.14-0.19 ms after a hand-over (`[worker91]` start latency; 0.016-0.019 in every earlier run, and in the rebased
altar run): each hand-over and each join then pays a slow thread wake. What remains of the dependency structure is real
(the waits by gate above: the characters' collision aliases and children moved by their own scripts, ~2.2 ms a frame at the
altar). Next: why the worker wakes 10x slower with round 110's pacing (thread placement against the pacing's waits; the
console run of r111/env-console.txt says whether it happens on the hardware), then the gainless hand-overs (31% of the
characters ran under a quarter of their time before the join) kept on the game thread.

No fault in any run: the checks, the A/B runs (altar, route 6, attract, 600 s each), runsb/finalR12 / finalR14 (route 6
600 s, console env), runs/load15 (p15, the console's memory card's save, 300 s, console env with SOTC_CHAR104=1: 6 993 frames; no character went to the worker there).

The ELF has no `:128` / `:256` NEON access at an sp-based address (spalign105: 0 of 589, p12-p15).

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r111.vpk (p15: main c183511, round 110, + this round; SOTC_CHAR104 0 unless set). r111/env-console.txt
(`SOTC_CHAR104=1 SOTC_THREAD_CORES=guest:2 SOTC_AB_FLAG=char104,hold111,delta111`): read with
`build/agent-scratch/r111/read111.sh err.txt <from>` (ab89's matched block; `[char111]`: the hand-over path by part, the
characters held / left on the game thread, spr111's monitor; `[char104g]`: the waits by gate). char104's windows say what the
jobs are worth on the console's cores (Vita3K does not model the placement).

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r113/` (PLAN.md: the budget tables and the ranked plan; STATE.md; run.sh,
chain1.sh / chain2.sh, v3k.sh: own tree ../vita3k-celosia-r113, 222 MHz, 3 cores; conframes.py, conres.py (a console
log's per-thread CPU and GPU busy by frame range), subsys2.py (SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF as disjoint rows), areas.py (the
sampler's namespace groups as the plan's areas, with r97/tools/grp.py)). Runs: loadN / loadP / loadS (the console
card's save at the shrine: frame log, profiler, sampler), attractP / attractS / attractC (the attract demo riding Agro:
profiler, sampler, collision census). No game code changed.

**The console (round 110's err.txt).** Per-thread CPU a game frame: the game thread 37.0 ms at the shrine, 60.5 riding
in the field (Steady 20), 68.7 in the heavy stretch out of the shrine area; the render thread 25-37 (49 at ~2600
draws); cores 1-2 together 52-88; the whole machine 90-156 ms of CPU a frame, against ~85 usable at 30 fps. GPU
occupancy (`[gpu86]`, scenes outstanding: an upper bound) 37-52 ms in the field, 42 at the shrine. At 30 fps cores 1-2
have ~10-15 ms a frame free, which is why the offloads of rounds 91-111 do not pay on the console yet.

**The game thread by area** (the Vita3K sampler's self-time shares, which the profiler's probes distort for per-call
paths: particles 15% probed, 6-8.5% sampled; times = share x the console's own `cpu game`), field riding / shrine:
collision 15.9% = 9.6 ms / 11.0% = 4.1; display path (walk, model hooks' game-thread part, light pass, sort lists,
prefetch) 14.5% = 8.8 / 19.2% = 7.1; particles 8.5% = 5.1 / 6.1% = 2.3; characters without their collision 11.0% = 6.7 /
16.0% = 5.9; recompiled guest code 16.7% = 10.1 / 15.1% = 5.6; runtime (sub-thread switches, memcpy of register frames,
kernel, timers) 11.2% = 6.8 / 10.9% = 4.0; other natives 15.4% = 9.3 / 14.9% = 5.5. Vita3K's absolute times follow the
Mac's load (the same spot: 68.5 and 88.4 ms busy with the same shares), so only shares are used.

**The ranked plan** (PLAN.md): 1 collision as a Vita-native system (host-format trees, batched rays, per-character
contact sets; -5..-6 ms console), 2 the display walk building draw records (-5), 3 particles as one native system
(-3, -4.5 on the worker), 4 the render thread with fewer, fatter draws (render 28 -> ~15-18 ms; room on cores 1-2), 5
far characters on the worker (uncertain after round 111), 6 the scripts' hot evaluators and the sub-thread runtime
(-5), 7 the GPU after 4, 8 the small natives. Sum: field riding 60.5 -> ~33-38 ms, heavy stretch ~40-44, shrine
~21-24.

**The ceiling under the rule** (nothing visible updates less often, no LOD or rate cuts, no interpolation): 30 fps is
reachable at the shrine and in light scenes once items 1-3 and the GPU work land; a locked 30 while riding in the
open field is not reachable with confidence (the game thread at best ~33-38 ms, the machine's CPU and the GPU both
over a 33 ms budget); the realistic target is a locked 20 without stutter everywhere first. Two shipped defaults bend
the rule and are for the user to decide: `sac_particles=1` in the console's settings (half the particles) and seg80
(a segment test's answer reused up to 5 frames while its ends move under 1 cm).

**Item 1 mapped (runs/attractC, `SOTC_COLL_CENSUS=1`, riding).** Collision queries 5.4-6.7 ms a frame of Vita3K host

## Round 116: the render thread's records kept whole (fat116); why fewer, fatter draws and a record-building walk do not fit the picture rule as planned (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r116/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: two own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r116 and -r116b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh / runb.sh scene runs; ab116.py: a frame log by A/B state
with the render thread's parts; shotgroups.py; env-console.txt; STATE.md). Base p0 = main a9ecc14 rebuilt.

**What the draws are split by (`SOTC_GL_MERGE_STATS=1`, p0, the attract demo).** Item 4 of round 113's plan wanted
~1300-1900 draws down to ~600-800 by merging per material, sorting by state and instancing. The draws next to each
other already merge whenever texture, state and matrix allow; what is left, per frame, riding (1426 draws, 538 GL
draws): another texture 508, another skin palette 8.6, another layer 10.9, another state 1.3, another matrix only 2.1
(the same mesh 1.8). Earlier in the demo (title, the plain): 245 leaders, texture 131, palette 55, matrix 15. So
94% of the splits are the texture: instancing (a matrix array, one draw for neighbours that differ only by matrix)
would merge 0.4-6% of the draws; merging across textures needs reordering (opaque draws at equal depth then keep
another one: round 87's sort87 measured slower and moved pixels) or atlases (other filtering at the edges). Neither
keeps the picture identical, so neither was built. Item 4 became the render thread's own cost per draw.

**fat116 (`SOTC_GL_FAT116`, default on; A/B `fat116`).** A model surface's packets reach the backend as one record
(drawMulti: one state, one matrix, several meshes; riding ~2.2 meshes a record). The render thread copied each
record once per mesh (expandDraws: ~330 bytes each, ~1400 a frame riding), then planFrame compared every neighbour
pair in full (state and matrix, ~300 bytes) and looked the texture up for every one. Now the records stay whole:
the frame's draws are members (record, mesh), in the same layer order; planFrame looks the texture up once a record
and takes a member after another of its own record as merging the way that one did (the same bits: the merge test
is an equivalence there; a record's first comparison and every comparison across records are made in full, so
shadow volumes and skinned palettes, which never merge, still do not). The plan, the passes and the GL calls are the
same, call for call. `SOTC_FAT116_CHECK=<n>`: every n-th frame the plan is made again with both short cuts off and
compared field by field (mesh, texture, run length, merged vertices, run copy pool / place, alpha and depth bounds).

**Checks.** runs/check1 (the attract demo, 480 s, `SOTC_FAT116_CHECK=7`): 2 400 frames checked, 1 808 474 draws in
832 261 records, 0 plan entries differ. Frozen frames (`SOTC_GL_FREEZE`, `SOTC_AB_FLAG=fat116` in 600 / 1200-frame
windows, the window captured every 3-4 s): the altar (runs/frzA1, frozen from game frame 3073, fat116 on, off from
3600, on from 4800; 61 captures over 180 s) one picture cycling with the bloom history (566 pixels by 1), the same
cycle in every window; the plain after the console card's load (runs/frzL1) the same (its pictures change once after
~100 s frozen: the per-frame meshes of the cloak and the shadow volumes are let go while the frame stays frozen, in
both states). No fault: route 6 520 s, the attract demo 620 s, the console card's load 420 s.

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz, in-run A/B `SOTC_AB_FLAG=fat116 SOTC_AB_ROTATE=1 SOTC_AB_PERIOD=60`, the phase log on,
`ab116.py`, matched by draws, off minus on: positive = fat116's gain).**

| run | scene | render thread a frame (on) | render (fat116 off minus on) | game thread | frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/abL1 | the console card's load: shrine, then the plain | 16.2 ms | **+1.61** | -0.44 | -0.48 |
| runs/abA1 | attract demo from frame 10 000 (riding) | 14.8 | **+1.95** | +0.45 | +0.17 |
| runs/abR1 | route 6 from frame 3 000 | 14.0 | **+1.64** | -0.22 | -0.25 |

The render thread's own time drops 1.6-2.0 ms a frame (~11-13%); the game thread and the frame are within the in-run
A/B's +-1 ms noise (the render thread runs beside them). Sampler (runs/sampL1 against round 113's loadS, the render
thread): memcpy 4.8 -> 1.3%, sameState 2.5 -> 0.85%. On the console the copies were ~450 KB written and read again a
frame through a 2 MB L2 shared with the game: the gain there should be larger; its A/B is in env-console.txt.

**Item 2 (the walk building draw records): not done; what the sampler says.** The display path is 14.5% of the game
thread riding / 19.2% at the shrine, spread over ~80 functions, the largest 1.1-1.7%: the walk's clip (clip83) 1.1-1.5,
the walk itself 1.1, glVertexKick 1.1-1.7, the model hook's front 0.4-1.1, scroll rows 0.9, the prefetch 0.9, the sort
lists 0.5-0.8, the light pass 0.4-0.6. Every native there keeps the guest's registers, VU0 state and memory exact for
the recompiled code around it; a host object table (class, callbacks, bounds and LOD kept across frames, NEON clip)
has to reproduce each guest-visible write the 50+ class callbacks make and the LOD / fade state the next frame reads.
The per-frame model state is already handed to the lane and the hook worker as records (round 61's lane, round 23's
jobs); what stays on the game thread is the walk's guest-exact bookkeeping. `SOTC_GLV116_LOG=1` (new) counts the
immediate-mode vertex kicks by caller: ~100 a frame, half from the heat haze strips (010F3FB0, eight a strip pair:
0x10f4698-0x10f47dc) and half from one particle drawer (0x11425bc), ~13 us each in Vita3K, ~1.1-1.7% of the game
thread; a direct path (the strips' vertices straight into the 2D assembler, no GIF packet, no glBegin / glEnd) is
the largest single exact cut found, but it must keep glBegin / glEnd's guest state and the VU0 registers the kick
leaves: next round's candidate (~0.7-1 ms console where the haze is on screen).

**Build note.** `sotc_vita_elf_room` 40 KB -> 48 KB (vita-elf-create's "segment 1 overlaps").
