`SOTC_AB_FLAG=fat116` rotating every 60 frames). Read with `python3 build/agent-scratch/r116/ab116.py err.txt --from
<frame>` (and `--slow` for the draw part's plan / pass / calls, which only the slow lines carry): fat116's row, render
and rdraw / plan positive = its gain on the console.

## Round 115: collision as a Vita-native system, slice 1: the segment test's walk and leaves on host-format data (coll115); seg80's reuse off with it (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r115/`: build.sh pN (worktree build, `r115/vita`), v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees
../vita3k-celosia-r115 / -r115b, 222 MHz, 3 cores), run115.sh <a|b> <load|altar|route6|attract> <vpk> <name> <secs> [env],
ab.sh (in-run A/B, 60-frame windows), read115.sh (the console / Vita3K reader: ab89's matched block, the [coll115*] lines,
faults), env-console.txt, STATE.md. p7 (main 025e264, rounds 112 and 116, + this round) = celosia-r115.vpk.

**Why.** Round 113's item 1: the segment test (ClipCollisionDirectCallBack and the object-array test) was ~4.8 of ~6.1 ms
of collision queries a frame riding in Vita3K, ~19 segments a frame at 150-350 us each: a whole terrain tile's split
tree walked in the guest's layout with the PS2's FPU and VU0 operations and guest frames per level, and per leaf every
surface's world boundary gathered from a per-frame guest cache and put through the segment's matrix.

**What changed (`SOTC_COLL115`, default on; A/B name `coll115`; coll115.h).**
- The walk: the guest's 8-byte split nodes read in place, on plain floats (the same order: the side the segment starts
  on first, the segment clipped at each split, the first leaf with a hit ends the walk), no guest frames, no f0 writes;
  at unit split scale the compares are integer keys of the float bits (no VFP compare and flag move per test). A host
  stack of 128 second sides (the deepest seen: 15); deeper: the original walk from the start (nothing is written to
  the result record before a hit).
- The leaves: each leaf's surfaces as a host block built at the leaf's first visit from the model's own data (the
  class's collision DB, part 0's vertex record: the index list and the packed / float vertices, as manager_sub_01114C70
  reads them before its matrix): per triangle a bounding sphere and the game's plane (the unit normal of
  (v0 - v1) x (v1 - v2), w = -n.v0) in local space, four surfaces a block in structure of arrays. A leaf is one NEON
  pass: the piece put into local space once (the tree's space is the local space times the class's uniform scale,
  checked per walk: class +0x15c is k times the leaf's +0xc matrix, the same translation, no mirror; else the
  original), each sphere against the piece (closest point) and the piece against each plane the way the side mode asks
  (mode 0: start in front, end behind; 2 the other way; 1 either), both with 2 mm margins, the tests as signs of
  differences in integer lanes (GCC makes NEON float compares four VFP compares without -funsafe-math-optimizations).
  Only the surfaces that pass go on to the surface / id filters (judge functions: pure) and the original
  ClipCollisionDB, which makes the hit, the record, the point and u / v as before. So the answers are the original's
  but for the piece ends at the splits (plain floats instead of the PS2's: sub-millimetre).
- Lifetime: models keyed by the tree's address, checked once a game frame (the tree's and the record's pointers, the
  root node, the first vertex and index words), each leaf on every visit (its leaf word); a 16-entry cache of the
  per-walk class checks (by tree, class and the two matrices' 128 bytes, within a frame); kept under `SOTC_COLL115_MB`
  (2) MB (riding: up to ~1.7 MB, 0.1-0.5 leaves built a frame, ~11 surfaces each). Game thread only: the worker lane
  (round 108) runs the original, its natives unchanged.
- Callers: ClipCollisionDirectCallBack's tree branch (the camera, the player and the horse, AI and scripts) and the
  object-array test's root sides (hot46g's ObjAry, its four call sites); the recompiled walkers for trees with +0x10
  set or a DB kind < 3 stay as they are.
- **seg80 under coll115**: the 1 cm / 5-frame reuse of the camera's, the characters' and the horse's segment answers is
  off (every segment answered every frame) unless `SOTC_SEG80=1`; round 84's AI path tests keep probe84's own memo
  (path scale, steering only, nothing drawn). With coll115 off (the A/B's off windows) seg80 is as before.
- Measuring: `SOTC_COLL115_LOG=1` ([coll115]: walks, nodes, leaves, surfaces, candidates, clips, hits, overflows and the
  deepest stack, leaves built, models / MB; [coll115o]: the object loop's objects / near / parts / skinned surfaces;
  [coll115t]: each query's host time and its tree walks' by state). Checks: `SOTC_COLL115_CHECK=1` each
  ClipCollisionDirectCallBack the original way, then this way from the same context and result record ([coll115c] by
  caller); `=2` each walk both ways ([coll115w] direct / objary; [coll115m] the first 40 differences in full).

## Round 118: the render thread's merged-run copies without reading GPU memory (RAM sources); the texture uploads' CPU parts (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r118/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: own Vita3K trees ../vita3k-celosia-r118
and -r118b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; turn.sh / turnb.sh: round 112's camera-turn script with the console's card; rend.py: the
render thread per frame window; env-console.txt; STATE.md).

**Why round 112 did not help on the console.** The r116 console log (shrine turns, riding): `[hitch112s]` per 600 frames
run copies 47-142 MB in 1.2-5.0 s, 16 000-56 000 copies, all by DMA, slowest frame 36-69 ms: ~35 ms per MB, ~90 us a
copy. The copies are small (2.5-16 KB; vitaGL's own vgl_memcpy uses DMA only from 8 KB) and each sceDmacMemcpy is a
kernel call that waits; before that (round 110) the CPU read the same bytes uncached. Either way the render thread read
vitaGL's mesh pools, GPU memory, every time a run was copied. Vita3K reads that memory at host speed (1.2 ms per MB), so
it never showed the cost.

**RAM sources (`SOTC_RUNSRC118`, default 1).** Every mesh pool (65 535 vertices, 2.25 MB) gets a twin in cached main RAM:
one memory block per pool (sceKernelAllocMemBlock USER_RW, outside the newlib heap, so the eviction's heap-pressure rules
see nothing new), the same bytes at the same offsets. A mesh's upload writes its vertices to the pool and to the twin;
pool compaction copies from the twin into the other pool and its twin; a merged run's copy reads its members' spans from
the twins. The CPU only writes GPU memory now (as the per-frame arena always did). A pool whose block could not be made
(`SOTC_RUNSRC118_MB`, default 64 MB of blocks) has no twin: runs with a member there are drawn one by one (the existing
fallback, same pixels) and compaction never drains it, so nothing reads GPU memory in any case. Up to 4 blocks of pools let
go are kept for the next pools. Memory: one block per live pool, 13 pools / 29 MB in Vita3K's turn; the console's r116 log
had 13-15 pools (29-34 MB) with ~78 MB of user memory free outside the heap. `SOTC_RUNSRC118=0`: round 112's path.

**Checks.** `SOTC_RUNSRC118_CHECK=1` compares every span read from a twin with the pool's own bytes (a test: it reads GPU
memory): the camera-turn run (runs/on1) 64 918 spans, 177.8 MB, 0 differ; route 6 (runs/route6) 14 577 spans, 39.3 MB, 0
differ. The plan, the draws and the run copies' contents are unchanged (the same bytes in the same places), so the picture
is the same by construction; no fault in 420 s turns x 4 and route 6 520 s.

**Churn (why 50-140 MB of runs are made per 600 frames).** New counters, Vita3K turn (runs/on2), the turning window: 2 292
copies of runs never copied before, 5 909 of runs copied before (2 354 within 60 frames of the last copy); copies let go
for budget room 8 201, compaction 8, unused 0; 4 041 runs known against ~285 copies held (6.0 of the 6.8 MB budget).
So the churn is the budget: a turn sees ~4 000 runs (~16 KB each), the budget holds ~300, LRU makes the rest again when
they come back into view. Neither key changes with the camera nor compaction is the cause (compaction: 36 copies per 600
frames at rest). Tried: copying a run only after 2 frames in a row (`SOTC_GL_RUN_FRAMES=2`, runs/rf2): half the copies
(86.6 against 180.6 MB over the run), but the heaviest window's render p90 45 against 35 ms (first frames drawn one by
one): not taken. A larger budget costs CDRAM, which the console has little of (vgl vram 84.7 of 96 MB used in r116):
left as is (`SOTC_RUNBUDGET118_KB` to try). With the twins the churn costs writes only; the per-frame limit
(`SOTC_RUNCOPY112_KB`, 1024) stays.

**What the old path costs, shown in Vita3K.** `SOTC_GPUREAD118_US_PER_CALL` / `_US_PER_MB` make the old path wait as the
console does. runs/off2pen (`SOTC_RUNSRC118=0 SOTC_GPUREAD118_US_PER_CALL=90`): turning windows 77.7 + 50.3 MB read in
10.0 + 6.5 s, slowest frame 242 ms, render p90 148 ms in the turn window; with the twins (runs/on2) the same window's render
p90 35 ms, median 23.6, copies 0 MB read from GPU memory.

**Texture uploads.** `[hitch118]` splits them: Vita3K, p1 (first build): 141 textures 188 ms, the alpha scan 120 ms,
swizzle 39, vitaGL 24. The scan stopped per texel on a two-value test: now blocks of 64 texels with no test, the block where
it stops scanned again texel by texel (`SOTC_ALPHA118`; the same least / greatest: 200 000 random cases compared): 148
textures 91 ms, alpha 11.6, swizzle 47, vitaGL 25. The swizzle writes its chain in destination order, 4 x 4 texel blocks of
64 bytes one after the other, instead of 4-byte stores scattered over the level (`SOTC_SWZ118`; 605 sizes x level counts
compared byte for byte), into a buffer kept between uploads. vitaGL's part (its allocation and the copy into GPU memory) is
now the largest per texture; the console log's split says whether it is the allocator.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r118.vpk with r118/env-console.txt (round 116's logs, no A/B rotation). Expect:
- `[hitch112]` / `[hitch112s]`: "copies by DMA 0 / CPU 0" (those count GPU-memory reads now); run copies MB as before
  (churn), their ms a fraction of r116's 1.2-5.0 s per 600 frames.
- `[hitch118s]`: "GPU memory read 0.00 MB 0.0 ms", "runs one by one for no RAM source 0", "RAM sources N pools X MB (made
  N, not made 0)"; "run copies whole" ms = the copies' real cost (writes, allocation, budget); new / made again / let go by
  budget = the churn.
- `[hitch118]` lines on slow frames: textures' alpha / swizzle / vitaGL ms (r116: ~10 ms a texture).
- `[vita:mem]` system free user lower by the blocks (~2.25 MB a pool).

## Round 114: the character jobs' slow wake was the host's load, not round 110; the jobs paused where their own account is negative (net114); char104 on by default (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r114/` (build.sh pN; v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r114 /
-r114b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh, ab.sh, ab2.sh (two A/B runs at once, one per tree), runpace.sh (the pacing on / off at
once), chk.sh (the checks); lat114.py (the worker's start latency by window against the host's load), loadfilt.py (a run's
frames with the host's load over a limit left out, for ab89), read114.sh, env-console.txt, STATE.md).
p0-p7 on main 2afa9e6 (round 111), p8 / p9 rebased on 025e264 (rounds 112, 113, 116), p10 on 2e1c6ab (+ round 115) = celosia-r114.vpk.

**Why.** Round 111 left char104 (far characters' geometry on the guest worker) off: rebased on round 110 the altar gained
1.13 ms but route 6 lost 0.71 and attract riding 3.52, and in those runs the worker started 0.14-0.19 ms after a hand-over
instead of 0.02. The brief: find why the worker wakes 10x slower since round 110 and fix it; keep the "gainless"
characters on the game thread; with a clean win everywhere, turn char104 on by default.

### 1. The slow wake: the host, not round 110

Every 10 s the run scripts log the host's `uptime` (load.txt). Mapped onto the `[worker91]` windows (lat114.py):

| run (round 111) | start latency by window, ms (host 1-minute load) |
|---|---|
| r111 runs/altarQ14 (the clean one) | 0.014-0.019 (load 2-5) |
| r111 runsb/finalR14 (route 6) | 0.030-0.043 at load 5-19, then 0.14-0.33 from frame 7 800 at load 37-47 |
| r111 runs/attractQ14 | 0.035-0.043 at load 33-43, 0.08-0.23 at load 43-47 |

finalR14 and attractQ14 ran at the same time as other agents' builds (load 25-47 on 18 host cores; the 1-minute load of
both runs ends with the same samples). With round 110's pacing on and off **at once** on the two trees (runs/pace1 and
runsb/pace0, r111's p15, route 6 console env, `SOTC_PACE110=1 / 0`): the same latency, rising with the load in both
(0.03 at load 15-19, 0.07-0.09 at 33-41). In every quiet run of this round (load under ~15): 0.017-0.035 ms. In Vita3K a
guest thread's wake is a host thread's wake plus a free slot of the 3-core semaphore (VITA3K_CORES, no priorities): a
loaded host delays it, and only the state with hand-overs pays for it, so the in-run A/B is biased against char104 by
the host's load. round 111's two losing runs, their frames at load 16 or less only (loadfilt.py): route 6 (finalR14)
-0.71 -> +0.69; attract (attractQ14, from 10 000) -3.52 -> -0.01.

Nothing to fix in the game for it: the worker's wait stays a condition variable (the console's kernel wakes a priority-140
thread on an idle core 1 in ~20 µs). What changed: the wake is now measured on the console too, with histograms, and the
round's A/B runs were read with the load next to them (lat114.py / loadfilt.py; a run whose latency windows pass ~0.05 ms
was loaded).
- `[char114]` (with the `[char111]` line, every 600 frames): the hand-overs' start latency (kick to the job running,
  sotc_worker::startLatHist) and the open queue's wake latency (an append's notify to the worker running again), each as a
  histogram (µs: <25 / <50 / <100 / <200 / more) and a mean. Quiet Vita3K: starts 0.017-0.032 ms (90% under 50 µs),
  open-queue wakes 0.013-0.026.

### 2. Gainless characters: kept on the game thread, a loss (gain114, off)

`SOTC_GAIN114=1` (default 0, A/B `gain114`): a character whose last hand-overs ran under `SOTC_GAIN114_US` (120 µs: what
a hand-over costs the game thread) before the join stays on the game thread when that costs no overlap: no batch running,
or the worker idle in the open queue (its geometry's gate then joins at once); behind a busy worker it is still appended.
Learned per object, tried again after `SOTC_GAIN114_PROBE` (30) frames. Exact (only the thread changes).

What the account shows (`[char114]` gainless by kind, quiet runs): at the altar 1 212 of 1 723 batches' first characters,
849 of 878 characters appended to an idle worker and 1 485 of 1 546 appended behind a busy one ran under 120 µs before the
join (runs/altarQ4); most of the worker's time comes after the join. But keeping them costs more: A/B gain114 (off minus on,
quiet): **altar -1.41, route 6 -1.03** (runs/altarG3, runsb/routeG3; 3.8 characters a frame kept). A character waited for
on the worker still costs the game thread less than running it itself (the worker's time per character is lower: its own
caches, the natives' list; the join's wait is not the whole run). gain114 stays in the code, off.

### 3. net114: the jobs paused by scene from their own account (`SOTC_NET114`, 1; A/B `net114`)

Per window of `SOTC_NET114_WIN` (300) frames with hand-overs: the characters' runs before the join (what ran beside the game
thread) less the hand-overs' cost to the game thread (the hand-over path and the joins' merges), a frame. Below
`-SOTC_NET114_US` (150 µs a frame) the jobs pause (characters stay on the game thread) for 600 frames, 1 200 after a second
window below in a row (p5-p8 doubled to 4 800: in a loaded run the menus' windows paused the jobs until frame ~8 400), then a
window of hand-overs again; a window above resets the pause to 600. With a pause the report lines print even without jobs. The account is
conservative (the quiet A/B gain at the altar is +0.4-0.7 where it reads -0.05): it only has to tell the scenes where the
jobs lose from those where they gain:

| run (quiet, 600 frames each) | runs before the join - (hand-over path + merges), ms a frame | A/B char104 |
|---|---|---|
| altar (runs/altarQ4) | -0.04 / -0.07 | +0.38 |
| route 6 (runsb/routeQ4 / runsb/routeN5) | -0.04 / -0.08, +0.09..+0.12 | +0.28 / +0.51 |
| attract riding (runs/attractA6 / runs/attractN5) | -0.11 / -0.29, -0.14 / -0.40 / -3.2 | -1.26 / -1.05 |

Attract riding's late part had 13.8 characters a frame in 10.4 batches (one character each, joined at once: chan joins), the
group snapshots 1.8 ms a frame and the hand-over path 3.2 ms. `[char114]`'s net114 line: windows, those below, the mean and
last account, frames paused, characters kept, paused now. Exact (only the thread changes).

### Checks and the delta's verify

| run | build | checks | differ (live words) | verify (characters, bytes off) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/chkl2 (altar, 600 s) | p2 | 88 | 0 | 23 719, **138** |
| runsb/chkr2 (route 6, 600 s) | p2 | 83 | 0 | 20 780, 0 |
| runsb/chkl6 (altar, 600 s, net114) | p6 | 55 | 0 | 11 672, 0 |

| runs/chkl10 (altar, 600 s, default on, with round 115's coll115) | p10 | 53 | 0 | 11 237, 0 |

## Round 117: the particle frame's remaining guest code and PS2 layers as host code (leaf117, pkt117, draw117); the immediate-mode quads (the heat haze strips, the particle quads) in one pass (glv117) (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r117/` (build.sh, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh: two own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r117 and -r117b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; run.sh / runb.sh scene runs; ab116.py (round 116's reader);
gen_aef8.py / gen_1142350.py (VU0 blocks lifted from build/runner); share117.py / touched117.py (two sampler runs
compared); env-console.txt; STATE.md). Measured on main 025e264
(= celosia-r116.vpk) + the round (p10 / p12); shipped rebased on main 07ab1ae (rounds 114, 115, 118: p13).

**What the particle frame still spent, riding (runs/attS0, the sampler on celosia-r116, the attract demo frames
~9 200-13 900).** Item 3 of round 113's plan, re-measured: the particle area 10.1% of the game thread. By function:
the per-particle step (particleUpdate and its helpers) 2.5%, the parameter blend 1.0%, the wind 0.9%, the emitter /
list / step natives 1.6%, the manager's layers and group walk 0.6%, texTransRequest per drawn emitter 0.4%, the
recompiled draw chain (disp_particle_geodisp, 0113ACB8, 01140ED0, disp_particle_emitter, 01141EA8) 0.95%, the
recompiled emitter leaves (0113AEF8, 011410D0, 01141150, 01141230, 01141400) 0.5%, the ptclman packets (BuildEnv /
Vtx / Mat / End, display list get / put, transMicroCode) 0.9%, the spawn (0113C1A8) 0.2%. And outside the particle
area, the immediate-mode vertices: glVertexKick 2.0%, glVertex3fv 0.24, glBeginWithDlLayerNo 0.26, glEnd 0.18 plus
its hook, the 2D assembler's vertex2D / feed2D 0.45: ~3.3%. `SOTC_GLV116_LOG`: 108 kicks a frame over the run, 98 of
them the heat haze strips (Wander's haze segments: 12 strip pairs of 2 x 4 vertices), the rest the quads drawer
01141D20 -> 01142350 (one glBegin / glEnd per particle) where it draws. Each particle system is 1-3 particles: the
cost is per emitter (its guest calls, PS2 frames, packets), not per particle.

**Why not a separate host-format particle system.** Every emitter, particle and geodisp is created, positioned and
freed by guest code (the scripts' effect starts, the nodes the emitters follow, the walk's class callbacks, the
free list the step and the list share); a host system would have to mirror each of those writes both ways. What the
plan's item 3 asks for instead (the emitter frame's remaining guest leaves, the draw chain native, no PS2 shape
per emitter) can be done exactly, checked against the original in the same run, and was.

**What changed (each default on; A/B names `leaf117`, `pkt117`, `draw117`, `glv117`, all four `r117all`).**
- **leaf117** (`SOTC_LEAF117`; decomp_ptclupdate.cpp, decomp_hot47e.cpp): the emitter frame's leaf calls as host
  code called straight: 0113AEF8 (last frame's position / orientation / direction kept; for a node-attached emitter
  the node's position and orientation (guest calls) and the direction by the jump table's six VU0 blocks, generated
  from the recompiled statements), 011410D0 (the distance fade), 01141150 with get_particle_lod_base_size /
  GetScreenRadiusParticle (the LOD index from the screen radius), 01141230 and 01141400 when they have nothing to do
  (their work paths stay guest calls), the parameter blend called straight with its two leaves inline (01145C70 the
  other set's record, 01145CD0 the weights). Same memory writes, f0 - f2, condition bit, VU0 registers.
- **pkt117** (`SOTC_PKT117`; decomp_hot46j.cpp, sotc_native.cpp `ptclDirect117`): round 103's particleDraw cut for
  the three other packet drawers (0113DBF8, 0113E6C8, 0113DEA0): the Mat / Env / Vtx hooks' state and job made from
  the packets' inputs, in the same order; no ptclDisplayListPut, transMicroCode, ptclmanBegin / BuildMat / BuildEnv
  / BuildVtx / End.
- **draw117** (`SOTC_DRAW117`; decomp_ptcl117.cpp, new): the draw chain from the walk's class callback:
  disp_particle_geodisp (GetGeoDispClass inline), 0113ACB8 (the layer, the runs of one draw key, the stack array
  and qsort for longer runs), 01140ED0 with 0113B408 (the emitter's fog-blended colour and view direction once a
  frame) and disp_particle_emitter (the drawer by kind). The recompiled code's frames, s-registers at every guest call
  and epilogues; callees through the table.
- **glv117** (`SOTC_GLV117`; decomp_walk.cpp `quad117`): the heat haze strips' four vertices between each glBegin and
  glEnd in one pass: glColor4f, glTexCoord2f, glVertex3fv's own part and the kick as before for each (the colour /
  ST words, the ring slot, the state words, the GIF pairs, UV through iosFTOI4Vector inline, the CLIP history,
  +0x1b4, the ADC byte, the ring index), the three matrices read and clamped once for the four (the VU0 clamp is
  idempotent: the same products and sums), no kick frame or register saves (dead stack), VU0 / Q / f0 - f2 / v0 /
  a0 / ra set once as the fourth kick leaves them. glBegin / glEnd and the GIF packet stay: the glEnd hook draws the
  same pairs. Anything else (no camera, untransformed vertices, another UV mode, a full ring) takes the calls.
  The particle quads drawer's 01142350 (one particle a call from 01141D20) is native too, its four corners through the
  same pass (glTexCoord2fv / glVertex4fv write the same words): the frame (the corner block, the size pair), the
  rotation (iosRotMatrixAxis, a guest call), the VU0 block (generated from build/runner by r117/gen_1142350.py),
  glBegin, glColor4fv, the quad, glEnd.

**Checks (in-run, every n-th call both ways from the same state, the original's result kept).**
- `SOTC_LEAF117_CHECK=<n>`: each native leaf against its guest call: the emitter's 0x200 bytes (the blend's 0x160-byte
  block), f0 - f7, the condition bit, vf8 / vf10 / vf14 - vf17 / ACC. runs/chkA8 (the attract demo, 900 s to frame
  24 800): 226 000 checks, 0 differ (keepFrame 56 500, distanceFade / lodIndex / blend 56 500 each); runs/chkL8 (the
  console card's load: shrine, plain) 180 000, 0 differ.
- `SOTC_PTCL103_CHECK=1` (round 103's, now also for pkt117's three drawers): the direct job kept, the packets built and
  hooked, the hooks' job compared field by field: chkA8 326 000 particle draws, chkL8 262 000, 0 differ.
- `SOTC_DRAW117_CHECK=<n>` (new): disp_particle_emitter and 0113ACB8 run recompiled and native from the same state
  with every callee replaced by a recorder (target, the argument registers it reads, ra, sp, s0 - s7, fp, f12), the
  call lists and the saved registers / frame compared; 0113B408 against the recompiled one (the emitter, its frame,
  vf5 - vf8, ACC, Q, f0 - f2). chkA8: 31 800 / 31 800 / 32 300, 0 differ apart from 2 viewOnce VU0-only differences:
  the upper half of vf6 (a qmtc2 of v1, whose upper 64 bits the default colour's `lq v1` had set); fixed in the
  shipped build (the lq now sets the whole register). chkL8 23 600 each, 0 differ.
- `SOTC_GLV117_CHECK=<n>` (new): quad117 against the four vertices through the calls: the gl block (0x5300 bytes from
  0x1186390), the packet's next 0x100 bytes, VU0 / ACC / Q / CLIP, f0 - f2. chkA8 95 500 strip quads, chkA11 65 000
  (with 01142350's particle quads: 138 500 of the run's 1.02 M kicks), 0 differ.
- The shipped build (rebased on rounds 114 / 115 / 118) again: runs/chkA13 (the attract demo 700 s) / chkL13 (the console
  card's load 500 s): leaf 170 000 / 144 000, packet jobs 252 000 / 244 000, the draw chain 23 600 / 22 000 per
  function (viewOnce included), quads 64 500: 0 differ.

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz; the Mac ran six other Vita3K instances of rounds 114 / 115 the whole time).**
- Sampler, the attract demo riding (runs/sampOn / sampOff: the same VPK with the four switches on / off, two trees at
  the same time, the 500 -> 700 s window = frames ~11 000-14 050 in both): the particle frame 12.43% -> 10.45% of the
  game thread, the immediate-mode vertices 4.03% -> 3.32% (glVertexKick 1.76% + glVertex3fv 0.38% -> quad117 1.42%);
  together 16.46% -> 13.77%: **the game thread ~3.1% shorter riding** (r117/share117.py). The functions removed
  3.79% -> 0.08%, those added or changed 2.63% -> 4.10% (touched117.py: -2.2% net). The next window (700 -> 900 s)
  covers different scenes in the two runs (18 075 / 18 353 at its end) and is not comparable.
- In-run A/B (`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r117all`, two states, 150-frame windows, ab116.py, off minus on; positive = the round's
  gain): the attract demo from frame 10 000 (runs/abA2, 5 600 frames a state): game thread +0.20 ms (matched by draws
  +0.33) of 25.6; route 6 from 3 000 (runs/abR2, 4 000 a state): +0.20 (matched +0.65) of 36.4. Five-state rotations

- On the console (round 113's scaling: field game thread 60.5 ms, particles 8.5% sampled): expect ~-1 to -2 ms riding

  per-particle step (particleUpdate, 2.5%), the parameter blend's 85 fields (0.7-0.8%), the wind (0.9%), the spawn and
  the manager's group walk are untouched and are now the particle frame's bulk.
- sac_particles: the round changes no particle count; with sac_particles=0 the console has twice the live particles

**Pictures and behaviour.** The four switches are exact (the checks above compare everything the original writes and

and -r120b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, the console card copied in only there; run.sh, ab.sh, areas.py, ab89.py; tools/asm.sh (a

(the sampler with the round on), runsb/attract7 / route7 / shrine7 (the A/B), runs/chkA7 (difftest + check).

The shrine (runs/shrineS0) and route 6 (runs/routeS0) have the same shape with less streaming: recompiled 7.7% of the
game thread in both by round 113's grouping, nothing over 0.33% (Agro's path 0142F4E8 at the shrine).

Round 102's guest pc sampler by task (runs/attractP0, probes on, % of the busy game thread riding): the scripts' own
10.3%: object animations (st_playObjAnim) 1.87 (natives: curveEval, ExecObjectAnimation, the layout geometry), the frame
start task 1.46 (texAnim, native), Agro 1.44 (its collision: round 119's area), the birds 1.33, sprites 0.67; the camera's
own code (innermost probe doit_game_camera) 2.28 spread over ~100 functions (each <= 0.06%, the largest its collision ray).

So item 6 as planned (-5 ms on the console riding from the script evaluators, the camera and the switch) is not there to
take as exact native rewrites: the camera is ~1.4% (0.85 ms console) in a hundred small VU0-macro functions, the object
animations are natives already (round 106's oan106 found register-for-register evaluators no faster), the AI is hundreds of
functions, and the particles / collision / characters that fill most of the bucket belong to rounds 117 / 119 / 114. What
was there as whole pieces of work: the module system's symbol resolution (1.7%, all of it streaming-time work done again
every call) and the game heap's allocator (0.37%, every scene).

**What changed (both exact, default on; A/B `sym120`, `heap120`, `r120all` both off).**
- **sym120** (`SOTC_SYM120`, decomp_sym120.cpp). While riding, the sheet manager (sheetMgrResolve, 0x115d170) runs every
  ~12-16 frames: for each of ~20 pending sheets it looks up every entry's symbol by hash (~2 200 lookups a call, ~120
  found) and tail-jumps into isysResolveAllProgramModule, which retries every module's unresolved imports
  (kernel_sub_001B4760: ~2 500 imports looked at, 500-760 retried by hash, 130-400 resolved a call). Natively: the sheet
  loop with the hash lookup inline (the group walk, the group add, the tick count, its seconds, the module resolve and
  the tail jump stay guest calls with the original's ra and frame), 001B4760's import loop with the reference-list moves,
  SearchStrHashKey, isysSearchSymbol and MakeStrHashValue (the original reads the string's strlen again at every
  character). The same reads and writes in the same order; module jal sites and the boot ELF's addresses read from the
  live words. MakeStrHashValue charges the EE cycles the original's loop does: the boot polls a module's names through
  it while the loader runs, and with no cycles charged the clock never moved and the boot waited for good (p4-p6; the
  Vita3K frame stuck at 242 ms).
  Per call (SOTC_SYM120_LOG=1, the A/B's windows decide native or recompiled; Vita3K riding and route 6): native 1.68 ms on
  average (639 calls), recompiled 5.95 ms (501); per 60 calls the native average 1.0-2.9 ms, the recompiled 4.7-10.7.
  Every 12-16 frames riding that call lands in one frame: a spike on the console too.
- **heap120** (`SOTC_HEAP120`, decomp_heap120.cpp): kernel_sub_001ADDC0, the heaps' block allocator (iosMalloc /
  iosMallocAlign, the module loader): the size class (the small heap 0x1e0c88's own table and steps, else the log2 class),
  the first fitting block in the class lists, the alignment, the split (the rest made a free block after the data) and
  the packed 24-bit header words, in the recompiled code's order; kernel_sub_001ADBC0 (a free block into its class list
  by size) native too and called inline by the split. v0 as the originals leave it.

**Checks.** The difftest no longer fits in the Vita build's 176 MB heap (it needs 64 MB of snapshots; the heap is at
~157 MB at boot since rounds 116-118): check VPKs are built with `_newlib_heap_size_user` at 240 MB (pchk7, not shipped).
Every RAM byte and the compared registers, Vita3K:
- runs/chkA7 (pchk7, the attract demo with riding, 1 000 s, six natives thinned): SearchStrHashKey, isysSearchSymbol and
  kernel_sub_001ADBC0 100+ checks each (166 541 calls), 001B4760 / sheetMgrResolve / 001ADDC0 fewer: 0 mismatches but two
  in 001ADDC0 on the one byte 0x29126c, the difftest's known noise byte (rounds 65, 71 and 106 saw it, also with
  `SOTC_DIFFTEST_CONTROL=1`, the recompiled code in both legs).
- runs/chkA8-err.txt (pchk8: the round's code on round 117): kernel_sub_001B4760 every call, 200 checks (module links at the boot and
  the area loads, resolved imports included), 0 mismatches.
- runs/chkA9 (pchk8): every sheetMgrResolve call, 200+ checks (~2 200 entries each) to frame ~9 900, 0 mismatches.
- runs/chkH8 (pchk8): kernel_sub_001ADDC0 the first 300 calls then one in 400: 400 checks of 39 901 calls, 0 mismatches;
  MakeStrHashValue 300 checks, 0 mismatches.
- `SOTC_SYM120_CHECK=1` runs the recompiled MakeStrHashValue to its return after the native on the same state and compares
  v0 / lo / hi: 35 000 calls, 0 differ (runs/dbgA7, runs/chkA7).
The difftest's unchecked calls run the recompiled code, so the A/B runs below are the long runs of the natives (attract
600 s x 3, route 6 420 s, the console card's shrine save 300-360 s x 3): no fault, the same boot, riding and load.

**A/B (Vita3K 222 MHz, `SOTC_AB_FLAG=r120all,sym120,heap120 SOTC_AB_ROTATE=1 SOTC_AB_PERIOD=60`, ab89.py matched by
draws, off minus on, the game thread's own ms).**

| run | sym120 | heap120 | r120all |
|---|---|---|---|
| runsb/attract7 (p7), riding from frame 10 000 (median ~28 ms) | +0.85 | +0.42 | +0.33 |
| runsb/attract8 (p8, rebased, the console's log flags), riding from 10 000 | +0.44 | -0.57 | +3.76 |
| runsb/route7 (p7), route 6 from 3 000 / the plain from 4 300 | -0.95 / -0.05 | +0.46 / +0.25 | -0.61 / +0.03 |
| runsb/shrine7 (p7), the console card's shrine save from 1 500 | +0.45 | +0.73 | +0.35 |
| runsb/shrine8 (p8) | +0.36 | -0.23 | -1.35 |

The in-run A/B cannot resolve these sizes: the sheet manager runs once in ~14 frames and costs ~0.1-0.4 ms a frame on
average, the allocator ~0.1, against +-1-3 ms of window noise on this loaded Mac (r120all's +3.76 and -1.35 are noise
too). The measurements are the per-call times in the same runs and the sampler. Per call over runsb/attract7, attract8 and
route7 (`[sym120]`, the A/B windows decide native or recompiled): 639 native calls 1.68 ms on average, 501 recompiled
5.95 ms (3.6x).

Sampler riding (runs/attractS0 -> runsb/attractS3, the same window): the five functions of sym120 1.66% -> 0.39% of the
game thread (sheetMgrResolve 0.43 -> 0.13 as native, 001B4760 0.31 -> 0.07, isysSearchSymbol / SearchStrHashKey inlined),
the allocator 0.39 -> 0.10. On the console's 60.5 ms riding that is ~0.75 ms (sym120) + ~0.18 ms (heap120), and the
sheet manager's 5-9 ms calls (Vita3K) every 12-16 frames become 1-2 ms.

**The sub-thread switch.** 0.71% riding (0.43 ms console): save 0.25, load 0.31, wake 0.13; the script pass, the frame end
and the resume path another ~0.7%. The copies are the register frames in guest RAM (0x2c0 bytes, ~560 copied each way, four
a round trip, ~90 round trips a frame): the sleep's save is what the next wake loads, and the wake's save is what the
sleep loads. An exact switch has to leave the same bytes in those frames; round 102 already made the copies inline NEON.
What would remove them is keeping only the callee-saved registers (s0-s7, fp, gp, f20-f31, the lo1 word the sleep
returns in v0) and nothing in the guest frame: the caller-saved registers are dead across the call by the ABI, but the
guest stack bytes would differ from the original's (no game state, but no longer exact for the difftest), for ~0.3 ms on
the console. Not done: below this round's bar for a non-exact change.

## Round 119: collision slices 2-3: where collision's time goes after round 115; the finder lists as host contact sets, the walk's dead pushes, the parts' clamps, the empty flushes (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r119/`: build.sh pN (worktree build, `r119/vita`), v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees
../vita3k-celosia-r119 / -r119b, 222 MHz, 3 cores), run119.sh <a|b> <load|altar|route6|attract> <vpk> <name> <secs> [env],
ab119.py (ab89 with `--riding`: only the attract demo's riding stretches, every cycle, found from the [pos] lines; `--ranges`),
t119.py (the [coll119t] lines: each touched call's host time by its switch's state, in-run), read119.sh (the console / Vita3K
reader), callers.py / lines.py / elflines.py (the sampler by caller and by source line: the hot function's offsets through the
same translation unit compiled with -g, coll_g2.obj / hot47j_g2.obj / finder_g2.obj, or the ELF's own -g1 line tables),
env-console.txt, STATE.md. Baseline p0r115 = celosia-r115.vpk (round 115's code).

**Where collision's time goes after round 115** (Vita3K 222 MHz, celosia-r115; route 6's plain, Wander standing, frames
13 000-16 000; the census `SOTC_COLL_CENSUS=1`, runsb/censR0, and the sampler, runs/sampR0, the game thread). Collision is
~15% of the game thread there (round 113's riding: 15.9%), and it is flat: no function above 3%.

| what | sampler (self, % of the game thread) | census |
|---|---|---|
| ClipCollisionDirectCallBack's object / part loop (directCallBackBody) | 2.4-2.9 | ~15 queries a frame, 183-195 us each, ~17 objects a query (4.5 near), every part of a near character: two transforms and a cylinder each |
| coll115's walk / leaves / walk set-up | 2.2 / 0.4-0.7 / 0.2-0.5 | 77-90 walks a frame, 16-24 us each |
| ClipCollisionDB (clipDBT) | 1.1-1.3 | callers: ClipCollisionFinder / ...CallBack 0.6, coll115's candidates 0.1 |
| the finder lists' passes: ClipCollisionFinder(CallBack), clipKeep, keepThenSlope, the keep test, slope, moved point | 0.6 + 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.2 | the slide's keep pass ~175 surfaces a frame; the landing / IK foot search 11-20 calls a frame |
| the ground fill (GetCollisionDBCallBack, g85, the skinned finder and its corners) | 0.9 + 0.2 + 0.7 + 0.3 | 3 fills a frame, ~32 surfaces entered each |
| cylinder (its exact path after the NEON rejection: 85%) | 0.6-1.0 | |
| GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr from guest code (player_HellDangerDetect's scan, 3 x 73 a frame) | 0.5-1.0 | |
| FlushCollisionWorkByWorkStruct / FlushModifiedManager | 0.25 + 0.2 | 4 x 150 list flushes a frame, most lists empty |
| water probes | 0.36 | |

By source line (lines.py) the object loop is mostly guest-memory bookkeeping: its reads / writes of guest words (the
frame's part index and matrix pointers per part, the records the filters get) are about half of its samples; the two part
transforms (the part's sphere, the skinned group's sphere, each with four row clamps) another ~20%. The walk's samples sit on
the node loop (the push of the second side at every node, the integer compares). g85's step spent half its samples on a
64-bit FNV hash of its 52-word key (a 64-bit multiply per word on the A9).

**What changed (each behind a switch, default off: `SOTC_FLUSH119=1` / `SOTC_WALK119=1` / `SOTC_PART119=1` / `SOTC_VIEW119=1` turn them on; `r119all` turns the four off together in an A/B).**
- `SOTC_WALK119` (coll115.h): coll115's walk pushes a node's second side only when the segment, as it is at the push, reaches
  it (the pop made the same test with the same values and went on). Nodes are counted in a local.
- `SOTC_PART119` (decomp_collision): transform() and matrixProduct() take the rows as they are when every lane (and v's) is
  small, finite below 2^61: the clamp of a small lane is that lane, a denormal the signed zero NEON reads anyway (round 49's
  argument), so the chain gives the clamped rows' bits without the four clamps. Every transform in decomp_collision (the
  object loop's part and skinned spheres, the tree set-up, the skinned surfaces, ClipCollisionDB's local point) goes through it.
- `SOTC_VIEW119` (coll119.h, decomp_hot44b): a finder list's host contact set. For the game frame, a list (its address and
  count) gets a view whose entries are made at their first test: the entry's two id words and the addresses of its plane and
  its plane's cached flag, as ClipCollisionDB / clipKeep compute them (the layout class, its collision work, the part's
  modified-list record, the plane table). A later pass reads the flag and the plane straight away (the id words compared
  first) and makes the same first test, round 49's NEON form bit for bit (not small, the flag clear, an id that moved: the
  call, which computes the plane as before):
  - ClipCollisionFinder / ...CallBack: an entry ClipCollisionDB would throw out at its plane test leaves f0 = 0 (its only
    write there) and the call is not made; the CallBack form asks its id filter first as before.
  - ClipCollisionFinderWithKeep (the slide's keep pass): an entry whose keep test clipKeep answers at its first return (plane
    cached, the point at least f12 in front: v0 2, keepThenSlope's v0 0) is not called at once; the last such one is called
    when the loop goes on to anything else or ends (it writes the same frame words and registers every earlier one would
    have, nothing ran in between), so the loop leaves what the original's leaves.
  - round 85's ground view (ground85::View, the landing / IK clips' pre-rejection): the list's words compared with a copy
    taken when the view was made, instead of the 64-bit FNV sum of every word on every call.
- `SOTC_FLUSH119` (decomp_collision): FlushCollisionWorkByWorkStruct does not hand an empty modified list (count 0) to
  FlushModifiedManager's native, which would only set v0 = 2 (a0 is still set to the list; ra / sp / v0 are set at the end).
- No switch (the same decisions): g85's key hash is a 32-bit FNV (the key's 52 words are compared in full after it); the
  ground view's slot age read once, not per slot.
- coll115 (no switch: its answers made the original's where they were not): a walk whose segment ends are not small (finite,
  below 2^61) goes to the original walk (round 115's unexplained route 6 differences, below; `ends not small` in [coll115]).
- Logs: `SOTC_COLL115_LOG=1` adds `[coll119t]` (each touched call's host time by its switch's state: coll115's walks by
  walk119, ClipCollisionDirectCallBack by part119, the finder clips by view119, the keep pass by view119, the work flushes by
  flush119), `[view119c]` (views, entries made, tested, thrown out) and `[view119]` (keep tests, not called). Checks:
  `SOTC_VIEW119_CHECK=1` (nothing skipped; each prediction against the call's answer: the clip's v0 and f0, clipKeep's v0),
  `SOTC_PART119_CHECK=1` (each raw-row transform against the clamped one, FastCheck collision.part119), and round 115's
  `SOTC_COLL115_CHECK=2` (each walk both ways) for walk119.

**Reading it, and why they ship off.** Every touched call is faster in the same run (walks ~5%, the segment queries ~3%, the finder clips ~3%, the
keep pass ~3-5%, the work flushes ~8%), all exact, but together that is ~0.1-0.15 ms a frame of Vita3K host time, below the

other way in four of six runs (-0.1..-0.5 ms: the frame slightly faster with the four off), while the largest riding run
(only r119all rotating, 13 800 frames a state) gives +0.14 ms of the game thread (+0.20 frame), in line with the per-call sum, which the per-call times do not
explain (every touched call is timed and faster) and noise may. With route 6 at -0.21 in the same kind of run, the rule
(default on only with a measured win) is not met everywhere: the four ship off; env-console.txt turns them on and rotates `r119all`, so the console's A/B, where the contact sets' fewer
dependent loads should matter most, decides. The coll115 fix and g85's hash are on (exact, no switch). The planned host object table does
not fit the rule as hoped: the objects' and parts' positions are read live per query in the original (characters animate
between queries in the same frame), so a table kept across queries needs the same reads to be validated; what a query pays
is the guest-exact bookkeeping per object and part (round 49 already batches the empty parts) and the two transforms per part
(now without clamps). The camera's six rays as one bundle needs the camera's code rewritten around it (round 115's note).
What is left that is large: the object loop's guest-word traffic (keeping the frame's part index and matrix pointers in host
registers between guest calls, written before each guest call and at the end, as round 49 does for empty parts), the
cylinder's exact path (85% of its samples, every near part), ClipCollisionDB's own preamble for the coll115 candidates and the
ObjAry one-by-one surfaces, and the recompiled callers' attribute scans (player_HellDangerDetect: 220 GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr
calls a frame on the plain).

## Round 121: global speedups: GCC PGO of the natives, the runtime and the recompiled game; the hot-code order regenerated; the generator and the toolchain sized (2026-11-08)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r121/` (build.sh pN [dir]; v3k.sh / v3kb.sh, run.sh / runb.sh: own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r121 and -r121b, 222 MHz, 3 cores; pair.sh / timing3.sh: two builds at once, one per tree, then swapped;
cmp.py: the runs over the same frames, raw and matched by draws; train.sh / traina.sh: PGO training runs; classify.py /
layout.py / insmix.py: the profile by class, the hot set's pages, the instruction mix; env-console.txt; STATE.md).

**SOTC_CHAR104 off on the Vita** (its own commit, 3560189): the r117 console A/B (`ab116.py err.txt --from 2500`) has the
character jobs losing 0.4-1.1 ms a frame on the real Vita (game thread off minus on -1.12, matched -0.37). Default 0 on the
Vita build, `SOTC_CHAR104=1` still turns them on; the Mac keeps 1.

**Where the game thread's time is now** (Vita3K profiles of main + that commit, p0: attract, altar, route 6, the console
card's load; game thread): the natives (decomp_* / sotc_native / pose / hooks) 72.5-74.4%, the recompiled game 18.7-20.6%,
the runtime (dispatch, scheduler, sub-threads, callGuest) 3.0-3.8%, libc / libgcc 2.5-3.0% (memcpy 1.3%, the A9's software
division 0.4%, memset / memcmp 0.3% each), veneers 0.7% (see below). The generated code's hot set: 50% of its samples in 107
functions / 930 KB, 90% in ~600 / 3.5 MB; the whole game thread's: 50% in ~110 functions / 0.6-0.75 MB, 90% in ~670 /
3.1-3.7 MB, 99% in ~1 800 / 6.4-6.8 MB. Far beyond the A9's 32 KB I-cache either way; the 2 MB L2 holds the 50% set.

Two things the Vita3K sampler does that matter when reading its profiles:
- It attributes a sample to the start of the guest block that runs (85.7% of the generated code's samples fall on the
  first instruction after a branch, which are 18.4% of its instructions): instruction-level mixes from it are wrong; only
  function-level shares hold.
- The "veneer" samples (0.7% of the game thread, ~55% of the render thread in r117's p12 attribution) are mostly time in
  imported system calls: the import stubs sit right after the veneer island at the end of .text and the HLE call is charged
  to the last block, a veneer or a `_from_thumb` stub (e.g. `__glDeleteFramebuffers_veneer` called from hookjobs::push,
  `__getreent_for_thread`, `pte_osSemaphorePost`). Real veneers on hot paths are few.

### 1. The hot-code order regenerated (game/overrides/vita_hot_order.ld)

Round 66's order (3 948 functions from five profiles of r56-r64) no longer covered the natives written since: decomp_tex64,
the particle chain, the collision body and dozens more sat at the end of .text (0x830xxxxx), 32-35 MB from the rest of the
hot set. Regenerated from the four p0 profiles (4 530 functions; tools/vita_hot_order.py unchanged but for the header and
`.text.hot.<name>`, below). The game thread's hot set, p0 -> p1 (same code, relinked):

| profile | 50%: 4 KB pages / 64 KB pages / span | 90%: 4 KB / 64 KB pages |
|---|---|---|
| attract | 199 / 31 / 32.7 MB -> 184 / 23 / 11.9 MB | 912 / 84 -> 904 / 80 |
| altar | 203 / 31 -> 187 / 21 | 916 / 100 -> 877 / 73 |
| route 6 | 256 / 44 -> 215 / 21 | 1 148 / 125 -> 1 010 / 78 |
| load (console card) | 240 / 43 -> 205 / 21 | 1 082 / 126 -> 947 / 79 |

Exact by construction (the same instructions placed elsewhere); Vita3K cannot show it (its JIT translates by guest
address). On the console: fewer distinct 64 KB regions for the A9's TLBs (the main TLB holds 128 entries, shared with data)
and the L2; regenerate the order after big native changes (`tools/vita_hot_order.py game/overrides/vita_hot_order.ld
<prof>:<elf> ...`, profiles taken with PROF=1).

### 2. PGO (GCC profile-guided optimisation), default on for the Vita build

**How** (CMakeLists.txt, `PS2X_VITA_PGO`). `PS2X_VITA_PGO=gen` builds an instrumented VPK (the overrides and the runtime;
`PS2X_VITA_PGO_GAME=ON` the recompiled game's unity batches too; vu1rec is never instrumented: its largest microcode
function then fails to assemble, Thumb conditional branches out of range; the instrumented build gets its own
sotc_vita_elf_room through `PS2X_VITA_PGO_ELF_ROOM`, 64 KB). Run it in Vita3K with `SOTC_GCOV_DUMP_FRAME=<n>` (the earlier PGO trial's
gcovDump writes the .gcda files to ux0:data/celosia/pgo every n frames), pull the directories, and
`tools/pgo_fix.py --root <tree> <out> <run> [<run> ...]`: sums the runs' arc counters per object, writes the object summary
GCC 15's `__gcov_info_to_gcda` leaves out (runs 1, sum_max; without it GCC takes every function as never run) and names
the overrides' objects by `@ROOT@` instead of the tree's path. `tar -C <out> -cJf game/pgo/vita-pgo.tar.xz .` makes the
committed profile, which CMake uses by default (`PS2X_VITA_PGO=<dir or .tar.xz>`; `OFF` / empty: none): extracted into the
build directory, `@ROOT@` replaced by the building tree's path, in a directory named by the profiles' contents (a new
profile changes the flags, so ninja rebuilds what it covers), then `-fprofile-use -fprofile-prefix-path=<build dir>
-fprofile-partial-training -fprofile-correction -fno-profile-values -fno-profile-reorder-functions -Wno-missing-profile
-Wno-coverage-mismatch` on the overrides, the runtime and (when the profile has the unity batches) the recompiled game.
The .gcda names are the objects' paths below the build directory, so any build directory of any tree uses them.

**Staleness.** GCC checks each function's CFG / line checksums: a function changed since the training loses its profile
and is compiled as before (partial training); unchanged ones keep it. The natives change every round, so the profile
fades slowly; retrain every few rounds (~1.5 h: the instrumented build ~40 min, four 8-9 minute runs in two trees, the
PGO build ~30 min). The recompiled game's profile lasts until the generator changes (the unity batches' grouping is by
file name).

**Training** (this round's): attract demo 540 s, altar 540 s, route 6 540 s, the console card's load 480 s, each from the

**PGO and the hot order.** With a profile GCC names hot functions' sections `.text.hot.<name>`, which round 66's order

against p1's 215). vita_hot_order.py now writes `*(.text.<name> .text.hot.<name>)`: p3o 222 / 22 (50%), 1 013 / 77
(90%), as p1.

### 3. The generator (ps2xRecomp), sized, not changed

Regenerating build/runner with the current generator reproduces it byte for byte (5 s; `build/r121/gen0`), so a generator
change costs a regeneration plus a full rebuild (~25 min Vita) and a difftest. What a guest call costs now (glBegin-
WithDlLayerNo's code, -O2 Thumb-2): ~27 instructions around the `bl`: the live instruction word for linker-bound JALs (48%
of the 34 727 known-call sites: one guest-RAM load at a constant address, the mask, the slot index range-checked), the
function table slot (one load; the table is 20 MB, 4 bytes per guest word, so every hot function's slot is its own cache
line and, with 4 KB pages, its own page), the host stack floor, the EE clock's charge (two loads, add, compare, store),
the jump serial, the known-function compare, the three argument moves; after the call ctx->pc and the unwinding flag.
Rounds 16 / 18 / 29-31 / 43 already took the large parts out. What is left is semantics (overrides replace slots at run
time, the scheduler's checkpoints, sub-thread unwinding). The generated code is ~19% of the game thread; the levers
left (a guarded constant target for linker-bound JALs instead of the live word; folding the unwinding flag into the pc
compare) are worth a few instructions per call on ~10-20 000 calls a frame (~0.1-0.3 ms on the console, mostly the
live words' and slots' cache / TLB misses) and need a guard for code the loader rewrites. Not done this round: PGO on the
generated code (above) was the larger and safer lever.

### 4. Toolchain flags, sized

`-fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math` on a collision TU: 291 490 -> 291 442 bytes, nothing to gain. -O3 / LTO for the
runtime and overrides were measured with the earlier PGO trial (LTO nothing). The runtime hot paths outside the game logic are small
(memcpy 1.3% of the game thread, mostly decomp_collision's copies; EeScheduler ~0.7%; the sub-thread switches 1% are
round 120's).

99% in 6.8 MB.

## Round 123: a port, not an emulator: the particle step in plain floats (ptcl123), the parameter blend / copy through host pointers (blend123), segment answers kept while the world they were tested against stays the same (seg123) (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r123/`: build.sh pN (`r123/vita`), v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r123 /
-r123b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0), run.sh <a|b> <load|altar|route6|attract> <vpk> <name> <secs> [env], ab.sh, ab89.py / ab119.py
(the frame A/B, `--riding`), read123.sh (console / Vita3K reader), seg123sum.py (the [seg123] / [seg123t] lines summed, the checks),
drift.py (two runs' [pos] tracks compared frame by frame), env-console.txt, STATE.md.

**The new rule.** From this round results need not be bit-exact with the recompiled PS2 code, only functionally the same (the same
gameplay, the same picture to the eye). Rounds 115 / 117 / 119 kept every answer exact and got ~1-2 ms each.

**The console's round 119 data first** (r119/console/err.txt, from frame 3600): with coll115 the segment queries cost 150 us on the
A9 against 110 us without, although coll115's tree walks are 2.4x faster there too (17 vs 41 us). The difference is not the walk:
with coll115 on, seg80's reuse is off (round 115), so every query walks (3.7 walks a query against 1.4 with seg80 answering the
repeats). coll115's host data is ~1.2 MB (51 models, 32 bytes a surface in blocks of four); per walk it is the faster path on the
console. What the console lost was seg80's answers, which round 115 dropped because they were blind (a character or a colossus
moving into a kept segment went unseen for up to 5 frames). seg123 below brings the reuse back with the blindness removed.

### What changed (each behind a switch, default on; A/B names `ptcl123`, `blend123`, `seg123`, all three `r123all`)

- **ptcl123** (`SOTC_PTCL123`; decomp_particles.cpp `update123`, decomp_ptclupdate.cpp): each live particle's step as ordinary
  C++ floats on the guest record, called straight from the emitter's particle loop (no guest call frame, no register set-up, no
  FPU_* clamps / operand alignment / compare keys, no VU0 clamps): age, the local-space transform of types 2 / 3, the acceleration
  and decay factors by age, size and growth, the move (velocity, acceleration, the list's drift, the local offset, the spin about
  the list's axis), the floor / ceiling bounce (iosGetReflectVector still a guest call), velocity and its decay, the three colour
  channels clamped to 0..1, rotation (wrap / stop), the spin by shape. Every particle is still stepped every frame. The jitter and
  shape 4's random axis draw from a host xorshift generator instead of iosGetRandom (VU0's R): the game's other random draws get
  another sequence (random either way). 0113C8C8 (the particle damage test) is called only when its own first test passes (the
  damage target and the emitter's handle resolve to an entry): on route 6 and riding it never did (every particle made that guest
  call for nothing before). The particles the original sends to the recompiled code (dying this frame, the collision test, shape
  0, pointers outside RAM) still go there.
- **blend123** (`SOTC_BLEND123`; decomp_hot47e.cpp): get_particle_parameter_blend_doit. Every call measured (route 6, the shrine
  save, the attract demo riding: ~20 a frame, 791 178 in one run) is the straight copy (no other set): the 85 fields copied through
  host pointers (the same words). With another set: the 85 fields as w0 a + w1 b in plain floats (the three positive-only fields,
  +8 through floats and truncated), no frame, callee-saved registers untouched (no call seen). (A host acosf / asinf, tried as
  libm123 in p2-p16, was taken out: round 122's quat122 covers those helpers.)
- **seg123** (`SOTC_SEG123`; coll123.h, decomp_collision.cpp segMemo): under coll115, ClipCollisionDirectCallBack /
  ...DoubleSide answers kept and reused while (1) the query is the same (caller, group, filters, user and its six judge words) with
  both ends within 1 cm (`SOTC_SEG123_EPS`, seg80's tolerance) and (2) **the world it was tested against is the same**: the group's
  objects that pass the query's object filter, in order (hidden ones skipped as isysGroupForNext does), each either *far* (its
  bound, the sphere the object loop's first cylinder test uses, further from the segment than radius x sqrt 2 + 5 cm: no pose of it
  can reach the segment) or *near* with a fingerprint of everything the object loop reads of it before its trees (layout class,
  collision DB, flags, scale, root position and the three per-part matrix arrays: any moving bone changes it). Fingerprints are made
  once an object a game frame (a 256-entry host table), the matrix arrays hashed only for an object near some segment. Anything not
  computable natively (a guest object filter, a class GetLayoutClass computes by a call, a group over 48 objects, the worker lane)
  runs the test. A caller that kept under a quarter of its last 32 queries (riding: the ends move more than 1 cm nearly every frame)
  goes straight to the test for its next 96 (the walk and fingerprints cost ~10-20 us a query in Vita3K). Round 84's AI path pool
  (probe84) is unchanged; seg80 is as before with coll115 off. Logs: `SOTC_COLL115_LOG=1` adds [seg123] (kept, misses by kind: no
  key / world moved (by object type and caller) / not validatable, fingerprints, bypassed) and [seg123t] (query time by seg123's
  state); `SOTC_SEG123_CHECK=1` runs the test on every kept answer and compares.
- `SOTC_PTCL_STATS=1` adds to the [ptcl] line: particles by path, damage tests made / skipped, the particle loop's time per particle by
  ptcl123's state; [blend123] (copies / blends). Checks: `SOTC_PTCL123_CHECK=1` ([ptcl123c]), `SOTC_BLEND123_CHECK=1` ([blend123c]).

### Checks (functional: the answers against the original's in the same run, the original's used)

| run | what | compared | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| runsb/chkR11, route 6 700 s (p11), `SOTC_PTCL123_CHECK=1` | the host step against the original from the same record (the guest generator and VU0's R kept for the check) | 1 037 994 particles, 43.6 M float fields | 2 fields over 1e-4 relative (and 1e-5 absolute); largest relative difference 0.18% (a position x near 0); list links 0 differ |
| runsb/chkR11, `SOTC_SEG123_CHECK=1` (1 cm) | each kept answer against the test run again | 22 262 kept of 65 914 | hit / no hit 0 differ; other surface at the same place 626 (2.8%: the neighbouring triangle across an edge within the centimetre); hit point max 12.9 mm |
| runsb/chkR4, the same, p4 (1 cm) | | 31 622 kept of 88 720 | 0 hit / no hit; 670 other surface; point max 11.3 mm |
| runsb/chkR7, the same with `SOTC_SEG123_EPS=0.001` (1 mm) | | 26 482 kept of 148 213 | 0 hit / no hit; 0 other surface; point max 1.3 mm |

The 1 mm tolerance keeps the hit points within ~1 mm but keeps only 18% on route 6 (34-55% at 1 cm) and on the plain nearly nothing
(Wander's idle sway moves the ends by more than 1 mm): at 1 mm seg123 cost more than it saved (runs/abR6: 130.2 vs 128.2 us a query).
It ships at 1 cm (seg80's, shipped in rounds 80-114): hit / no hit agree in every compared case; a kept hit point can be up to ~1.3 cm
from a fresh one (the segment's own movement within the tolerance). `SOTC_SEG123_EPS=0.001` gives the strict form.
The blend's copy path writes the same words; its blend path never ran in any run (`SOTC_BLEND123_CHECK=1` compares it when it does).

**Gameplay drift.** The route 6 input (frame-clocked, but with vblank waits) does not replay the same way twice in Vita3K under this
load: runsb/posOff (the round off) entered the game at frame ~1 200, runs/posOn (on) not at all in 600 s, runsb/abR12 at ~10 800,
so the per-frame position compare (r123/drift.py) has nothing to pair (round 122 saw the same: its replays part at the area load).
The functional evidence is the per-answer compares above (every kept segment answer agreed on hit / no hit; the particle
fields to 1e-4 relative but two in a million) and play: the attract demo (4 runs to frame 28 000-39 000), route 6 (6 runs) and the
console card's shrine save ran with the switches on and rotating without a fault, Wander standing on the shrine floor and the plain

**Reading it.** The round is ~0.4-1.5 ms of the game thread in Vita3K by the A/B rows (+0.4..+1.55 for r123all in five runs; the

## Round 122: the characters' frame work as host code, not as translations (gaze122, cloth122, quat122, keys122): a port's tolerances instead of bit-exactness (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r122/`: build.sh pN, v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r122 /
-r122b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0), run.sh <a|b> <scene> <vpk> <name> <secs> [env] (r.sh / rb.sh: tree a / b with
r122/<pN>.vpk), geo.sh (round 97's character probes + `[chargeo80]`), geoprobes.txt; tools: geo80.py (the `[chargeo80]` lines
by object and callee), prof.py (SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF entries), drift.py (a replay's `[rstate]` against its recording's S lines),
ab119.py (round 119's A/B reader, `--riding`). runs/ and runsb/: geoA0 / geoL0 (probe profiles, riding / shrine, main),
sampOn6 / sampOff6 (the sampler, attract riding, the round on / off), chkA2..chkA10b, chkL3 (checks), abA5 / abA6 / abL6 / abA10
(A/B), rec7 / recR10 (input recordings), repOff9a / repOn9 / repOffR1 / repOnR1 (replays). p0 = main 6c24d41, p1-p9 on it, p10
= rebased on a320162 (round 124), p11 + gaze diagnostics, p12 = p11 with gaze122 off by default, p13 = p12 rebased on baea142 (rounds 121 / 123: PGO on, sotc_vita_elf_room 64 KB) = celosia-r122.vpk.

**The rule of this round.** A port, not an emulator: the characters' code need not give the recompiled code's bits, only the
same game: the same keys and branches, rotations and positions within float rounding, no visible difference, no drift. Rounds
41-120 translated each function with the PS2's operations (every VU0 op clamped, the whole VU0 register file copied in and
out, newlib's float libm replayed, guest frames written for dead locals); this round writes the hot ones as plain float NEON
host code on the same inputs, writing only what the game reads (the output qwords, f0 where a caller reads it).

### Where the characters' time is (and how much the probes overstate it)

The probe profile (geo.sh: SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF with 29 extra probes and `[chargeo80]`, runs/geoA0, riding) puts the characters'
body at 6.3 ms a frame of Vita3K host time: root dynamics 1.84 (collision mostly), cloth 1.44, IK 1.0 (its script callbacks
0.46), the pre-process 0.76 (the motion keys 0.31 + curveEval 0.36), gaze 0.54, root fitting 0.53, pose 0.37, layout 0.23, option
nodes 0.22, strands 0.21; control 1.47. The probes inflate per-call-heavy paths several times: `[char122]`'s own host clock gives
the old gaze 0.10 ms a frame (probes: 0.54) and the cloth 0.5-0.9 (with its callbacks). The sampler (runs/sampOff6, riding,
self time on the game thread) is the reliable view: the character-related natives are flat, the largest pose82::pose 1.0%,
charaLinks 0.9%, the cloth step 1.0%, getSinCos 1.1%, strands 0.7%, gaze 0.7%, the curve decoder 1.1%, the quaternion /
arc helpers ~2.5%, the bridle 0.7%. ~11% of the thread in the functions this round touches.

### What changed (each a switch; A/B names in brackets, `r122all` all four off)

- **gaze122** (`SOTC_GAZE122`, **default off**, decomp_char122.cpp): GetCharacterClassGazeAddMotions (0x10c6c80) and its per-gaze worker
  (010C6238, round 41's native) as one host loop: the direction's angle (host atan2f) picks two of the gaze motion's eight
  direction keys, the length blends each from the identity; per node the three keys decoded by host code (decodeKey: the
  curve formats 0, 3-9, 12, 13 in plain floats), the keys relative to the base, the blends and the product into the node's
  quaternion in NEON. No curveEval guest calls, no VU0 state. A cache of the decoded keys by resource address (p2-p7) was
  wrong: the heap gives a freed motion's address to another one with the same channel pointers (the check found 11-18 deg
  off after a motion change, `[gaze122d]` showed the decoded keys equal to curveEval's: the cache was stale); p8 on decode
  every frame.
- **keys122** (`SOTC_KEYS122`, decomp_char122.cpp, hooked in decomp_motionframe.cpp): GetMotionFloatFrameNoCaribration
  (0x10ad1b0, the motion's keys at a float frame, ~4 calls / ~120 keys a frame riding): the keys of frames k and k + 1 decoded
  by decodeKey and blended the short way round, as the original keeps the nearer key's sign; no motionKeys / curveEval round
  trips, no guest frame. Fallback counters (`[keys122]`): 0 of 40 000 calls fell back.
- **quat122** (`SOTC_QUAT122`, decomp_char122.cpp, hooked in decomp_quat / decomp_math / decomp_hot43b): atanf, atan2f
  (both entries), iosGetATan2fExact, acosf (both), iosGetACosfExact, asinf as host libm; iosGetSinCosf as the PS2's own
  polynomial (its coefficients from the boot ELF) in plain floats; SetQuaternionByAxisRotateV (the boot ELF's quarter-wave
  table, as the original), GetDifferencialQuaternionWithNoRegularize and GetQuaternionByAxisDirZY as closed forms (the
  rotation from a to b; the turn to z then about z by v's angle, 1/65536-turn steps as the original). The VU0 register file
  and the scratch registers are not reproduced (leaf helpers of C callers that load their operands again; not audited caller by caller: the checks and the runs are the evidence).
- **cloth122** (`SOTC_CLOTH122`, decomp_char122.cpp, decomp_bridle.cpp): GetClothDynamics (0x1137a68) as one host loop a
  cloth (the row buffers' flip, the step with the same three VU0 R draws a point in the same order, the pins, the rows'
  length constraint and the velocities fused a row: the rows are independent), and the reins' collision callbacks
  (013978E8, 013976B8) in plain NEON. Type-1 cloths and anything out of range take the old natives.

`SOTC_CHAR122_CHECK=1`: the checks below (each runs the old path on the same input, keeps the old result, compares);
`SOTC_CHAR122_LOG=<n>`: `[char122]` (gaze / cloth calls and host ms a frame, new and old path), `[keys122]`.

### Tolerances observed (checks, attract riding 640 s and the shrine; the old path's result against the new one)

| part | checked | largest difference | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| cloth: positions / velocities | ~7 200 cloths | 2.4e-4 units in a position (one float step at 2 048-4 096), 0.016 in a velocity (that step / dt); R stream identical | float rounding only |
| reins (bridle) | ~6 400 calls | 2.0e-3 units in a point (16 float steps at ~2 700 units) | the cylinder push's sqrt and the constraint's 1/sqrt |
| quat: axisRotate | 280 000 | 0 (the same table) | |
| quat: axisDirZY | 40 000 | 0.0116 deg (two 1/65536-turn steps: the truncation boundary) | the original's own angle quantum |
| quat: diffQuat | 40 000 | 0.045 deg in 2 calls (near-opposite / near-equal vectors), < 0.01 deg in the rest | conditioning |
| atan / atan2 / acos / asin | 20 000-60 000 each | 2.4e-7 rad | |
| sinCos | 280 000 | 6.9e-4 in the computed lane near |sin| = 1 (~0.04 deg) | sqrt(1 - s^2) is ill-conditioned there in both; the PS2 rounds toward zero |
| keys (motion frame) | ~4 000 | 1.45e-3 in a component, 0.12 deg | the same sqrt(1 - |xyz|^2) near w = 0, below the keys' own 9-bit step (1/255 of the range, ~0.45 deg) |

Not traced: **gaze122 ships off** |

Angles are measured in double (4 atan(|a - b| / |a + b|)): a float dot's acos bottoms out at ~0.04 deg (p2-p5's early
"0.056 deg" were that floor). Nothing differs in kind (the same keys, the same branches, the same R stream).

**Drift.** The attract demo does not replay (the camera diverged from tick 120 even with the round off). Route 6 recorded with
the round off (recR10, 2 880 ticks) and replayed off (repOffR1) and on (repOnR1): Wander's and Agro's positions equal the

at the area load (tick 960) both replays, the off one too, part from the recording (the loader's timing on a loaded host: 400
units, a different streaming moment), so the replay cannot resolve drift after it here. Per step the checks bound the
error (above); the stateful parts (cloth positions, the R stream) stay at one float step per frame and do not feed gameplay.

## Round 125: collision as a native object system, part 2: the finder lists' surfaces as a host cache with whole triangles (fin125), the segment tests' object / part loop in host locals (obj125) (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r125/`: build.sh pN (`r125/vita`), v3k.sh / v3kb.sh (own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r125 /
-r125b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0), run.sh <a|b> <load|altar|route6|attract> <vpk> <name> <secs> [env], ab125.sh (an A/B run in
the background), samp.sh (a sampler run, the round on or off), rec.sh (route 6 recorded / replayed), stop.sh, ab89.py / ab119.py,
read125.sh (console / Vita3K reader), t125.py (the per-call times by switch state, the checks), prof125.py (two sampler profiles side by
side, the collision family summed), drift_rep.py (replays against their recording and each other), env-console.txt, STATE.md.
Note for the scripts: the shell here is zsh, which does not word-split an env list held in a variable (two A/B runs, abA3-noab /
abR3-noab, ran without their A/B because of it).

**Where collision's time was** (the Vita3K sampler on celosia-r123, route 6's plain standing, runsb/sampR0 500-800 s; the game thread's
self time): collision ~14% of the game thread, flat: ClipCollisionDirectCallBack's object / part loop 2.52% (+ its cylinder 0.46,
matrixProduct 0.22, guest calls 0.13, seg123's memo 0.26 + its world 0.21), ClipCollisionDB 1.50 (mostly the finder clips'), the finder
clips' own loops 0.60, coll115's walk / leaves 1.6, the skinned finder step 0.67 + corners 0.30, the ground fill 0.70, clipKeep 0.45
(+ keepThenSlope 0.17, the keep loop 0.14), GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr 0.56, the work flushes 0.53. The console (round 124's err.txt):
the segment queries 157 us each, ~8.6 a frame (1.36 ms); the finder clips 15.3 us each, ~88 a frame (1.35 ms); the walks 17 us.

### What changed (each behind a switch, default on; A/B names `fin125`, `obj125`, both `r125all`)

- **fin125** (`SOTC_FIN125`; coll125.h, decomp_collision.cpp finderClipBody / keepEarlyFrom / attributeAddress / flushModified /
  flushWorkBody, decomp_hot44b.cpp): the surfaces of the finder lists (the ground fill's and the finder steps' surface ids) as a
  **host surface cache**: per surface (keyed by its two id words: the ground fill makes its list again every frame, in an order that
  changes), made at its first test, the plane and the boundary sphere (centre, r^2) as cached, the first vertex and ClipCollisionDB's
  triangle terms (the clamped edges' n x e1 / n x e2 and their two denominators, its own VU0 macros, made once), and its
  GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr answer; 512 slots of ~190 bytes (96 KB; a clip touches the plane and the stamps of most), open addressing (8 probes, least recently used replaced). They come
  from the game's own per-object caches the way ClipCollisionDB reaches them (a plane, boundary or vertex not cached yet is made by
  the same calls, EntryModifiedManager included). ClipCollisionFinder / ...CallBack then make one pass over the list with host data:
  ClipCollisionDB's tests after its lookups with the same operations on the same values (the plane test in round 49's NEON form, the
  crossing, the sphere, u / v), the segment shortened at each hit, the id filter (pure judge functions) asked only for an entry
  that hits, and the hit record (+0 / +4 the id, +8 / +0xc u / v, +0x10 the local point of an independent surface, +0x30 the kind,
  +0x40 the point) written once, for the last hit, as the last ClipCollisionDB that hit leaves it. No guest chain per entry
  (object, class, collision work, part records, cached flag, plane: four to ten dependent loads on the A9) and no call. The keep pass
  (ClipCollisionFinderWithKeep) asks the cache for clipKeep's first return (the point at least f12 in front of the kept plane, its
  NEON form): such an entry is not called (round 119's pending-call scheme, on now with fin125 as well as with view119).
  GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr (player_HellDangerDetect's scans, the filters) answers a cached surface from the cache.
  **Lifetime:** the caches a surface comes from change only through FlushModifiedManager (an object that moved has its flags
  cleared). A flush made by FlushCollisionWorkByWorkStruct moves that collision work's epoch (a small host table of the works some
  cached surface belongs to); any other flush on the game thread moves a global epoch, any flush on the guest worker's lane a worker
  epoch. A surface is used as kept while its frame, its work's epoch and the two others are the ones it was checked at; else it is
  checked again (its plane and boundary flags still set and their values the same as kept) or made again. Route 6: 22 work flushes
  a frame, 0 others; 8% of the entries used needed the check. Anything else (a class made by a call, a lane not small, a list over
  256) goes to ClipCollisionDB as before. Logs: `SOTC_COLL115_LOG=1` adds [fin125] (clips, entries, plane passes, hits, made,
  checks, dropped, keep tests and attributes answered), [fin125e] (flushes by kind) and [fin125t] (each clip's host time by the
  switch's state); `SOTC_FIN125_CHECK=1` runs each clip the original way first (its answer used) and compares ([fin125m]).
- **obj125** (`SOTC_OBJ125`; decomp_collision.cpp obj125Run, decomp_hot46g.cpp): ClipCollisionDirectCallBack's and
  ClipCollisionDirectCallBackObjAry's object / part loop with its state in host locals: the original (directCallBackBody / hot46g's
  objAry, guest-exact) keeps the segment, the filters, the current object, class, DB and part, the three per-part matrix pointers, the
  two ends and the hit flags in its guest frame (~30 words written and read back per object and part) and makes every compare the
  PS2's way. Here: per object its bound against the segment's cylinder, per part its sphere through the part's matrix and the
  segment's (plain NEON when every lane is small: transform()'s bits, part119's argument; else transform()) and the cylinder in plain
  floats with the radius grown by 0.1% + 1 mm (nothing the PS2's compares call near is called far), then the tree walk (coll115 / the
  recompiled walkers as before) with the record the leaves read written once; iosAbsVector (a guest call per near part) inline. The
  frame words a callee reads are written before that call (the part filter's sphere; the walk's record and segment); the one-by-one
  surfaces get the loop's words spilled and run the original's code, the skinned surfaces the original's code with their own words.
  `SOTC_OBJ125_CHECK=1`: each query the original way first (its answer used), then obj125's from the same context and record
  ([obj125c], [obj125m]); `SOTC_COLL115_LOG=1` adds [obj125] (queries, objects, near, parts, walks, spilled, the part filters called)
  and [obj125t] (each query's host time by the switch's state).
- Dead frames: neither path writes the guest frames the original's loops leave below the caller's sp (ClipCollisionDirectCallBack's
  0x270 bytes, ClipCollisionDB's 0xf0 per entry). seg80 / seg123 (every kept answer: the whole query skipped) and round 85's host view
  (rejected candidates: no ClipCollisionDB call) have shipped for many rounds without those frames, so no caller reads them.

### Checks (Vita3K, each answer against the original's in the same run and state, the original's used)

| run | build | what | compared | hit / no hit differ | other surface | hit point max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/chkA1, the attract demo 900 s / runsb/chkR1, route 6 900 s | p1 | obj125 queries (`SOTC_OBJ125_CHECK=1`) | 58 656 + 115 793 (25 099 both hit) | 0 | 0 | 0 mm |
| runs/chkA2 / runsb/chkR2 (attract / route 6, 1000 s) | p2 | obj125 queries | 40 261 + 59 382 | 0 | 0 | 0 mm |
| runs/chkR8, route 6 900 s | p8 | obj125 queries (direct and ObjAry) | 265 251 (58 183 both hit) | 0 | 0 | 0 mm |
| runs/chkA1, runsb/chkR1 | p1 (fin125's crossing in plain floats) | finder clips (`SOTC_FIN125_CHECK=1`) | 67 618 + 154 999 | **865 + 882** | 7 + 1 | 0.33 / 1.44 mm |
| runs/chkA2, runsb/chkR2 | p2 (ClipCollisionDB's operations) | finder clips | 45 215 + 131 272 | 0 | 0 | 0 mm |
| runs/chkR8, route 6 900 s | p8 (the surface cache, per-work epochs, attributes, triangle terms made once) | finder clips | 360 344 | 0 | 0 | 0 mm |

p1's fin125 made the crossing tests in plain host floats (the game thread's VFP rounds toward zero; ClipCollisionDB's plane test is
NEON, round to nearest): 0.4-1.3% of the clips disagreed on hit / no hit, all of them a probe that starts on the surface's plane
(d0 within rounding of 0: the foot / landing probes start at the last contact point) where the original says "hit at the start" and
the plain floats said "behind the plane, no hit". That is a gameplay difference (ground contact lost for a frame), so from p2 the
cache keeps the cached plane, sphere and vertices as they are and the clip makes ClipCollisionDB's own operations on them: the
answers are the original's bit for bit while the caches are current; what fin125 removes is the lookup chain and the call per
entry, not the arithmetic. obj125 has no such case: its plain-float tests only choose which parts are walked (with the radius
grown by 0.1% + 1 mm), and the walks and ClipCollisionDB decide as before (0 differences in ~540 000 queries, p1-p8).
Tolerances, then: fin125 and obj125 give the original's hit / no hit, surface and point in every compared case (the check's
threshold for "other point" was 1 cm; the largest seen 0.00 mm); the only non-exact parts are the obj125 cylinder pre-tests
(conservative by construction) and, in principle, a cached surface used after its object moved without a flush (none seen: the
checks compare against the live caches).

(the game thread = frame - wait - sched; 1 200-4 200 matched frames a state.) In every run all four rows lean the same way: the
