**Reading it.** The finder clips are ~19% and the segment queries ~12% cheaper per call riding in Vita3K (in-run, the same frames),
with the original's answers in every one of ~1.08 M compared clips and queries (p2-p8); at ~20 clips and ~12 queries a frame that is
~0.3 ms a frame of Vita3K host time, and the sampler pair puts the collision family at 12.50 -> 9.93% of the game thread riding (-2.57 points, ~1.1 ms of a ~45 ms Vita3K frame). The two disagree by ~3x (the per-call times carry
two timer reads each; the sampler's windows are matched by time, not by frame) and the whole-frame A/B (r125all +0.44 / +0.24 ms on
the quiet machine) cannot separate either from its noise. On the console: between ~0.2 ms (the per-call sums at round 113's 0.65
factor) and ~1.2 ms (2.6% of round 124's 48 ms game thread), more if the A9's memory latency dominates as it did for coll115 (Vita3K
does not model it): a finder clip used to make four to ten dependent loads into guest memory per entry and now reads one 16-byte
host plane, and round 124's console log had ~88 finder clips a frame at 15 us. **Far below the -4 ms target.** What the round did not reach: the object / part loop itself is now the largest
collision item and stays memory-bound in its object, class, DB and matrix reads (obj125 removed its frame bookkeeping and the
clamped transforms, ~10-20% of it); coll115's walk and leaves (1.5-2%); the ground fill's skinned finder step (decomp_finder::finder
+ corners ~1-1.5% standing on route 6: still a guest-exact translation); the flushes and attribute scans (~1%). Collision as a whole
was ~15% of the game thread and is now ~12-13%: even all of it native at zero cost would be ~6 ms on the console, and the rest of
the -4 ms has to come from the characters' script callbacks and the display path (round 122's note).

### Not done
- The ground fill's finder step (decomp_finder::finder, the skinned triangles' loop, ~1% of the game thread standing on route 6 with
  corners 0.45%): still the guest-exact translation (every VU0 / FPU operation on the context's registers, the frame as the MIPS
  writes it). A host loop over the cached triangle spheres (four at a time) with the corners called straight is the next item; the
  finder list order and the callbacks' arguments are what the game sees.
- coll115's walk itself (1.0-1.5%) and its leaves (0.5-0.8%): unchanged.
- The work flushes (0.3-0.5%) would need every producer of a modified-list entry tracked (the recompiled code may append to a list
  without the native EntryModifiedManager), not done.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r125.vpk with r125/env-console.txt (round 123's flags, `SOTC_AB_FLAG=r125all,fin125,obj125`):
read with `build/agent-scratch/r125/read125.sh err.txt <from>` and `python3 build/agent-scratch/r125/t125.py err.txt <from>`. What to
look for: the r125all / fin125 / obj125 rows (positive = gain), [fin125t] / [obj125t] (the clips' and the queries' time on the A9 by
state: the console's ~88 finder clips a frame at 15 us of round 124's log should drop by a third or more), [fin125e] (flushes by work /
other), [obj125] (the part filters called). Gameplay: Wander's footing (no falling through, no snagging on edges, the IK feet on
slopes and steps), landing from jumps and climbs, the camera's collision (no clipping into walls), Agro's riding (the ground under
him, the slopes), a colossus fight (ClipCollisionDirectCallBackObjAry: the probes against its body, grabbing and climbing).

## Round 127: the display path on the game thread: where it stands; the model hooks' scroll rows kept across frames (scroll127); the GL cache's eviction sort; walk67 to the console's A/B (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r127/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / ab127.sh / samp.sh, two own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r127 and -r127b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0; top.py: one sampler profile's top functions;
env-console.txt; STATE.md). Base p0 = main 67030c3 (= celosia-r125.vpk / r125 p9); p1 = this round = celosia-r127.vpk.

**What the display path is now (sampler, the attract demo riding, r125 p9 400-700 s).** The brief: round 113's item 2,
~8.8 ms of the console's game thread riding, as a native system (a host scene table, NEON visibility, model / light
setup emitting draw records). The sampler shows what rounds 49-117 left: the walk and its natives are already A9 code
(walk83's clip in plain floats, the hook's plan / part walk / packet loop, the light pass, the particle and haze
quads), and the path is flat: quad117 1.73%, the walk 1.33, hookScrollRows 1.04, clip83 1.10, mdsPartWalk 0.78 (the
lane's jobs run by the game thread's joins), mdsPlanPackets 0.62, modelDispHook 0.60, strips 0.57, prefetch::note
0.52, sortOrder 0.49, texreset 0.47, reflectionBegin 0.44, lightPass 0.42, gsRegHook / gsReg / vertex2D 0.9 (the
immediate quads' GIF pairs parsed back at glEnd), the rest below 0.3 each; at the shrine (r125 sampR5) the same names
within +-0.3. No piece of it is above ~2%, and most of what remains is memory latency on guest data (pointer chains per
object / surface) and per-call guest bookkeeping (the recompiled callers' registers, VU0 / CLIP state the natives
leave for them). A host scene table replacing the walk would have to reproduce every guest-visible write of the 50+
class callbacks (round 116's finding stands); this round did not get there. What it did: the largest single
function's work made per-texture-and-change instead of per-surface-and-frame, and one renderer cost on the game
thread that was not the game's.

**scroll127 (`SOTC_SCROLL127`, default on; A/B `scroll127` / `r127all`; sotc_native hookScrolls127).** At every
model hook the job takes the plan's texture scroll rows (round 34: the rows' two words read at the hook, as the job
may run after the game moved them). Each row's address is a chain: surface record +0x2c (an index) -> the header's
object table (+0x40, +0x44 entries of 0x20) entry +0x10 (the object) -> +0x20 (its nto2) -> +0xc (the row). The memos
(per surface record, per plan) lasted one frame, so every frame each plan's surface records walked their chains again
(the walk67 prefetch of them included): 1.04% of the game thread riding. Now per (plan, header) the distinct table
entries are kept with the object / nto2 / row they gave and the rows in first-appearance order; a later frame checks
the header's table words and those chains (a few words a texture) and reuses the rows, else makes them again. The
plan itself is checked against its packet list every frame (its listHash, LOD and the header's surface array are
part of the key). The two words of each row are still read at each hook. Checks (`SOTC_SCROLL_CHECK=1`: the
per-surface walk run beside it, every hook compared, address and both words): runs/chkA1 (attract, 480 s) 371 867
hooks, 0 differ; runsb/smkR1 (route 6, 600 s: the shrine, the walk out, the plain) 518 511 hooks, 0 differ, no fault. Kept 97% of the time (`[scroll127]`: ~13 900 made in
487 000; ~600 after a chain moved: the texture animations' object swaps).

**The GL cache's eviction (native_renderer_gl evictKept; no switch, the same entries evicted).** At the hand-over (the
game thread) a pressure / aging / budget pass lists the cache's candidates and sorted them by last use. Only the
budget's cut depends on the order; the aged and pressure cuts take every candidate older than their frame. Now the
sort runs only for a budget cut, and a mesh a heap-only pressure pass would spare is counted as spared without being
listed. Vita3K's heap sits above the pressure mark (104 MB), so every 16 frames ~20 000 spared candidates were sorted:
0.98% of the game thread in the sampler. The console's logs show pressure 0 (heap ~98 MB): no change expected there.

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz).** Sampler, the attract demo 400-700 s, p1 (runs/sampA1) against r125's p9 (sampA9on,
the same window): hookScrollRows + hookScrolls 1.10% -> scroll127's functions 0.17%; the eviction sort 0.98% -> 0.
In-run A/B (runsb/abA1, attract from frame 3 000, 60-frame windows, `SOTC_AB_FLAG=r127all,walk67`, ~4 500 frames a
state, matched by draws, off minus on): r127all game +0.06 / frame +0.17 ms (within the A/B's +-0.2 noise at the
Mac's load 10-23); walk67 off game -0.61 / frame -0.46 (the walk's prefetch records cost Vita3K, which has no cache
to fill, as round 76 measured: -1.9 there).

**walk67 on the console: never measured.** Round 67's prefetch records (prefetch::note / window / objectLines67, the
sort lists' sortOrder / sortAhead, the group runner, the scroll chains ahead, ~1.5-2.3% of the game thread in Vita3K)
were kept for the console's memory on an estimate (0.25-0.5 ms); round 76 put `walk67` in the console's A/B and no
console log with it came back (none of the console logs since has a `walk67 off` window). It is in this round's
env-console.txt: if the console agrees with Vita3K (walk67 off faster), the default flips; if the prefetches pay
there, scroll127's own share of them (the scroll chains ahead) is already gone.

**Not done / next.** The ~-3 ms console target of the brief was not reached: this round's measurable gain is ~0.9% of
the game thread (scroll127; ~0.4 ms console if the share holds) plus walk67's console verdict. The candidates in the
order the sampler gives them: (1) the immediate-mode quads straight to the 2D assembler (quad117 1.73 + strips 0.57 +
glBegin 0.36 + the GIF pairs parsed back at glEnd ~0.9: ~3.5% riding where the haze / particle quads are on screen),
which needs glBegin's packet header (TEST / PRIM from the gl state) made natively and glEnd's chaining of the packet
into the layer list shown unread in native mode; (2) the hook's game-thread half (modelDispHook + the lane jobs the
joins run + mdsPlanPackets: ~2%) as one per-instance record built once per (instance, plan) and checked by the words
it read; (3) texreset's ~1 000-node list three times a frame (0.47%) from a host index kept by the texture manager's
own insert / remove.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r127.vpk with r127/env-console.txt (round 125's log flags, SOTC_SCROLL127_LOG=1,
`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r127all,walk67` rotating every 60 frames). Read with `python3 build/agent-scratch/r127/ab89.py err.txt
--from <frame> --min-draws 300`: the r127all row (scroll127 off) and the walk67 row (the prefetch records off),
positive = the switch's gain. No picture change expected (scroll127 gives the same rows; the eviction the same
entries); look at the textures that scroll (water, waterfalls, the sky's clouds, the shrine's light shafts) moving as
before.

## Round 126: the characters' and the camera's shared getters as host code (geo126, ctl126); the camera and the characters lifted whole to host C++ (tools/lift126.py) measured slower and left out; the camera filter's table (ray126) dropped (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r126/` (build.sh, run.sh / r.sh / rb.sh: own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r126 and
-r126b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0, the console card copied in only there; ab119.py; rec.py, cg.py (the static call
graph of the generated code: callers, subtrees with their sampled self share), callers.py (a sampled function's callers by
lr), top.py / cands.py / charroots.py (which functions the lifter takes), cmp126.py / perfn.py (the round's code in two
sampler windows), dt.sh + dtenv.txt (a difftest over a long name list), campath.py; camprobes.txt (SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF over 50
camera functions); lifted/ (the generated lift files of p6, not in the build)). Runs: runs/sampA0 / runsb/sampL1 (main's
sampler, attract / the console card's shrine), runs/camP0 (camera probes), runs/abA3 / abA4, runsb/abL4 (A/B with the lifted
code), runs/sampOn5 / sampOff5 and sampOn6 / runsb/sampOff6 (the same build with the round on / off), runsb/dtG2, dt150c (difftests),
runs/smkA3 (smoke). Builds: p0-p1 lost (a build stopped mid-way), p2 first full (title hang, below), p3 the s-register fix,
p4 + jump tables / jalr / callMaySleep in the lifter, p5 + div / break / cfc2 Q, p6 written-only syncs, p7 without the
lifted code and ray126, p8 = p7 rebased on round 125, p9 = p8 rebased on round 127 (shipped: celosia-r126.vpk, symbols r126/celosia-r126.elf).

### Where the camera's and the characters' guest time is

The camera (doit_cameraman_manager, task 013451C0) reaches 999 recompiled functions statically (66 600 MIPS instructions); in
the attract sampler (main, runs/sampA0) their self time is 2.2% of the game thread exclusive to the camera plus 2.5% in
helpers shared with the characters, no function above 0.06% except a handful of shared getters. The probes
(runs/camP0, inflated per call) put the camera manager at ~4.0 ms of a ~77 ms probed frame: the default angle / target offset /
follow rotation branch 1.2, the subjective visibility and update 0.9, the parameter manager 0.33 (a blend of seven parameter
blocks, ~3 400 instructions of `out = a w1 + b w2` per field), six direct collision tests 1.0. The characters' remaining guest
code is a flat list too: the motion accessors (010AEE18, GetMotionRootFloatFrame, 010AD048), the geometry pointer getters,
MVHIST_Update, AI_GetYRotQuaternion, the option nodes' getters (called in place by round 47's native node passes through
callGuest), _setRootXYZHPB, player_HellDangerDetect, each 0.05-0.17%. The largest single item in the camera is a native:
the surface filter of its rays (attributeAddress from cameraVisibility, 0.5%).

### What ships (A/B names in brackets, `r126all` both off)

- **geo126** (`SOTC_GEO126`, default on; decomp_cam126.cpp): the geometry pointer getters as host code: GetGeometryPointerPosition
  (0x1131d80), GetGeometryPointerQuaternion (0x1132098), GetGeometryPointerQuatPos (0x1132270) for the kinds that are a copy,
  a point / rotation in a quaternion + position frame, or a character node's frame (round 44's manager_sub_010AC4A0 for the
  node), recognised by their jump table's label read from guest RAM (any other kind: the recompiled function, before
  anything is written); GetMatrixFromQuatPos, ExchangeLWQuaternion, GetMotionNodeQuaternionPos,
  GetCharacterClassNodeQuaternionPos. The quaternion product and the quaternion-to-matrix rows are the VU0 sequences'
  algebra in plain NEON (worked out lane by lane from the macros); the half-turn / quarter-turn quaternions from the boot
  ELF's quarter-wave table as round 122's; f0 left as the originals leave it.
- **ctl126** (`SOTC_CTL126`, default on; decomp_cam126.cpp, decomp_hot47a.cpp): MVHIST_Update (Wander's 90-frame velocity
  history: the slot written, the 90 slots summed in order and divided by the weights' sum, as one NEON loop instead of 90
  VU0 macro rounds), AI_GetYRotQuaternion (the z axis turned, flattened, normalised, the half-angle quaternion from its
  cosine), manager_sub_010AD048 (a motion root track's key: constant, float or 16-bit quantised), and the option nodes'
  GetMotionOptionNodeParentId / GetCharacterClassOptionNodeLocalQuaternionPos, the last two also made in place by
  decomp_hot47a's child / root node passes (cam126.h: no callGuest round trip; the guest call stays when the table holds
  anything else).

**A native that calls guest code without an epilogue of its own must put the callee-saved registers back** (p2's hang at
the title, three bisections: the geometry getters' node path went through round 44's nodeQuatPos, which leaves s0 as its
caller's epilogue would restore it; the recompiled getters restore s0 in their own epilogue, these natives have none, so
their callers lost s0. The difftest found it at once: `MISMATCH (r16 ...)`). decomp_cam126's `Saved` keeps s0-s7, gp, sp,
fp, ra around every guest call.

### Checks and tolerances

Difftest on the Vita build (check VPKs with `_newlib_heap_size_user` 240 MB, never shipped), new knobs in sotc_decomp.cpp:
`SOTC_DIFFTEST_FTOL=<rel>` (a word of RAM or f0 that differs passes when both are finite floats within that relative
difference or 1e-5 absolute; `[difftest] ftol` lines give the worst accepted), `SOTC_DIFFTEST_NOV0=1` (v0 not compared:
void natives that leave another scratch v0), `SOTC_DIFFTEST_DEPTH=<1-3>` (how deep checks nest: each level holds two 32 MB
copies; three levels of lifted callers ran out of the 240 MB heap and hung Vita3K in dt150b).

- runsb/dtG2 / dt150c (pchk3 / pchk5, FTOL 0.002): the twelve hand natives, every check 0 RAM differences beyond float
  rounding (worst accepted 1.2e-7 relative); f0 differed in ExchangeLWQuaternion / GetMotionNodeQuaternionPos /
  010AD048 (the scratch value the originals leave in f0, which no caller reads) until p6 set it as they do.
- dt150c also checked 85 lifted functions (the 150 with the most samples, one check each to frame 7 590): 0 differences
  beyond the known noise word at 0x29126c and four single bytes far from the function's data (0x93abac, 0x41998c,
  0x17dbe**: most likely other threads writing between the two legs).

### The lifter (tools/lift126.py): whole subtrees as host C++, measured slower, not in the build

tools/lift126.py turns a guest function's MIPS (the words in the generated code's listing) into C++ with registers as host
locals, plain floats, VU0 macro ops as SSE / NEON lanes, jump tables from the generated code's case lists, relocated words
read at run time, and calls through callMaySleep with every written register put back first (so a call that sleeps or
switches threads leaves the context exactly as the original would and the recompiled function resumes at the return label).
It took 1 732 functions of the camera's and the characters' subtrees (3.7% and 4.9% of the game thread's self time;
refused: VU0 integer / flag ops, MMI, ldl / ldr, FPU accumulator ops, sleeps). They ran clean (the title, both attract
demos, the shrine save; 85 functions difftested), but **the lifted code was slower than the recompiled code**: same build,
same window, the lifted set 7.36 -> 10.99% of the game thread (p5), 9.02 -> 10.08% (p6, only written registers synced at
calls); some functions 6-10x (player_HellDangerDetect 0.05 -> 0.41%, gamecore_sub_013B8438, manager_sub_010D5130,
IsInsideOfRegion), a few faster (manager_sub_01164AC0 0.16 -> 0.08%). Likely causes, for whoever takes it up: every guest
register as an int64 local (ARM32: two registers and two instructions each, and the large functions spill), the VU0 lanes
through sse2neon (p6 still had the memcpy lane reads; a NEON header is in the tool now, unbuilt), the full register sync at
every call, and the lifted code outside the PGO profile and the hot order. The generated files of p6 are in
r126/lifted/; the tool stays in tools/ (its switch names are arguments).

**ray126 (dropped):** the camera filter's answers kept in a 512-slot table while doit_cameraman_manager runs (exact by
construction; 50% of the calls answered from it): the sampler put the filter at 0.57% of the game thread without it and
0.88% with it (the table's own hashing and misses cost more than the three dependent loads it saves), and round 125 now
answers GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr from its finder cache.

### Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz)

Sampler, same build, round off / on: attract 420-600 s (p5, runs/sampOff5 / sampOn5): the twelve getters' recompiled self time
0.98 -> 0.06% of the game thread, their natives 0 -> 0.28%: **-0.64%**; the console card's save 600-790 s (p8, runsb/sampLoff8 /
runs/sampLon8; the two runs' scripted input parted, so only these functions compare): 1.07 -> 0.02%, natives 0.16 -> 0.24%:
**-0.97%**. That is ~0.3-0.5 ms of a 45-55 ms console frame at round 113's ratio, plus round 47's node passes without two
callGuest round trips a node (in the native bucket).

In-run A/B (`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r126all,geo126,ctl126`, 60-frame windows, off minus on, game thread):

| run | part | game thread (all on) | r126all | geo126 | ctl126 (matched by draws, ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/abA8 (p8, shipped) | attract, the demos (player placed) | 28.1 | +0.36 | +0.12 | +0.59 |
| runs/abA8 | attract from frame 3 000 | 19.1 | +0.05 | +0.37 | +0.54 |
| runsb/abL8 (p8) | the console card's shrine save | 47.7 | -1.17 | +0.24 | -0.57 |

(abA3 / abA4 / abL4 had the lifted code in the same switches and are not comparable.)

The A/B's noise on this host (load 10-20 from other agents' emulators) is +-1 ms; the sampler is the reliable number.

**Against the target.** The brief asked for -3 ms of the console's game thread from the characters' and the camera's guest
code. What ships is ~0.6-1.0% of the game thread (~0.3-0.5 ms console). The camera has no hot spot to rewrite by hand (a thousand
functions under 0.06% each); the whole-system route was the lifter, and in this form it loses. A lifter worth turning on
needs 32-bit locals where the code is 32-bit (sd / ld / 64-bit ops make a register wide), NEON lanes, syncs limited to the
registers a callee or a resume can read, and its output under the profile; then the same difftest (FTOL) and sampler
comparison decide.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r126.vpk with r126/env-console.txt (round 122's log flags, `SOTC_CAM126_LOG=600`,
`SOTC_AB_FLAG=r126all,geo126,ctl126`): read with `python3 build/agent-scratch/r126/ab119.py err.txt --from <frame>
[--riding]`; positive = the round's gain (expected small: ~0.3-0.5 ms, below the A/B's noise). Look at: anything that follows a node or a point on
a character or an object (the camera's target and look-at while riding and fighting, Wander's hands on the reins and the
sword's light, the IK of the feet on slopes), Wander's start and stop (MVHIST: the movement history behind his turns),
the animals' / colossi's turning (AI_GetYRotQuaternion), the root motion of every animation (010AD048).

## Round 129: the console's own sampling profiler of the game thread (SOTC_PROF129); fix 129: its boot crash on the console (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r129/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh / v3kb.sh, two own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r129 and -r129b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0; env-console.txt; STATE.md; console/: the crash log
and core dump of p1). Code: game/overrides/sotc_prof129.cpp, ps2_thread_load.h, ps2_runtime.cpp; readers tools/prof129.py,
tools/fmean129.py.

**Why.** Every round since 113 picks its target from Vita3K's host sampler, which has no A9 caches or memory latency;
console results keep disagreeing (coll115, char104, walk67). The console needs its own hot list.

**How it samples.** Vita user mode cannot read another thread's registers (sceKernelGetThreadCpuRegisters is a kernel
export), so the sampler reads what the game thread already keeps in memory: the running EE context's pc (the generated
code sets it to the target at every jal / jalr / j and to the return address at every jr ra; callGuest the same: the
guest function running now at call granularity, at no cost) and $ra; ps2_load::Wait now publishes the wait site the game
thread blocks at; handleSyscall the syscall id (two relaxed stores per wait / syscall: the game thread's whole cost). A
pthread moved to cores 1-2 wakes every `SOTC_PROF129_US` (1000) us from the second game frame, adds the sample to a fixed
16 384-entry table (no allocation) and every `SOTC_PROF129_SECS` (60) s writes a window to err.txt: `[prof129] w` (samples,
states, frames, gaps, the sampler's own CPU ms from runClocks), `h` (each distinct pc's function-table host function as an
offset from an anchor symbol: the native, or the recompiled function a return site belongs to), `e` (pc:ra:count[:state[:zone]]
by count), `end`. `SOTC_PROF129_RA=0` drops ra; `SOTC_PROF129_RUNSTATUS=1` (off by default, see the fix) marks samples
where sceKernelGetThreadRunStatus says the game thread was off a core.

What it cannot see: inside a native (natives calling natives, host helpers, memcpy inside a native are charged to the
outermost native entered through the table or callGuest); host code outside guest dispatch is charged to the last guest pc
except the marked waits and syscalls. A native that joins a job by spinning shows as that native (below: tex64's wrap<12>).

**The reader** (`python3 tools/prof129.py err.txt --elf <the build's elf> [--t A-B | --windows A-B | --frames A-B]
[--group REGEX] [--host prof.txt --base prof.base]`): the game thread by state (running, each wait site, no EE thread),
the running samples by subsystem (round 113's areas: display, characters, scripts/AI, collision, particles, camera,
runtime/libc, kernel/syscalls, worker gates, unnamed guest code placed by its caller where it can be), the top functions
(natives marked), and with --host the same grouping of a Vita3K host profile beside it.

**Vita3K (attract demo, 400-700 s, runs/sampOn against runsb/sampOff, both with the host sampler).** 230 404 samples,
mean interval 1.30 ms, 0 dropped, 2 100-3 700 distinct keys a 30 s window. Overhead: frame 26.25 ms with the sampler,
26.90 without (the Mac's load 13-14 on both: noise; no cost measurable). Shares (prof129 / host sampler, % of the busy
game thread): display 48.1 / 25.4, characters 13.7 / 18.7, scripts/AI 9.2 / 14.1, collision 6.0 / 8.4, runtime/libc
0.1 / 8.9, particles 1.1 / 5.7, worker gates 3.7 / 0. The differences are the attribution rule, not errors: prof129 charges
memcpy, libc and the particle natives' helpers to the native that called them, and `decomp_tex64::wrap<12>` alone is 31.6%
(its join with the texture offload spins on the game thread, unmarked; the host sampler charges that time to the spin's
helpers). So prof129's list reads "which guest-level entry point holds the game thread", the host sampler's "which
instructions"; on the console the first is what is available. Next step for prof129: mark tex64's join as a Wait (its
kSiteTex wait covers only part of it) so the reader shows it as a wait, not as display work.

**Fix 129: the boot crash.** celosia-r129.vpk (p1) with SOTC_PROF129=1 crashed the console at boot right after
`[sotc:decomp] 371 decompiled functions in place`, before any [prof129] line; SOTC_PROF129=0 booted. The first thing the
sampler thread did was call sceKernelGetThreadRunStatus (vitasdk links the import whether or not the firmware resolves it
for user mode; Vita3K answered zeros), from a thread made with sceKernelCreateThread (priority 100, cores 1-2) before the
game ran. Now: RunStatus only with SOTC_PROF129_RUNSTATUS=1, the thread a plain pthread like the runtime's others (moved
to cores 1-2 with sceKernelChangeThreadCpuAffinityMask, as threads::place does), nothing read until the second game frame,
the runtime pointer null-checked. The core dump was not parsed (no vita-parse-core here), so which of the two it was is
not proven; p2 avoids both.
## Round 128: the immediate-mode quads straight to the native 2D assembler (imm128); texreset's list from a host index (texr128, console A/B only); the model hook's per-instance record not built (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs and logs: `build/agent-scratch/r128/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / ab128.sh / samp.sh, two own Vita3K trees
../vita3k-celosia-r128 and -r128b, 222 MHz, 3 cores, audio-volume 0; top.py; env-console.txt; STATE.md). p0 = r127's
p1 (main 71f540e); p2 = this round on 71f540e (checks, sampler); p4 = this round rebased on round 126 (main 445b3b0) =
celosia-r128.vpk. spalign: 691 NEON :128/:256, 0 sp-based. No elf-room change.

**What round 127 sized.** (1) The immediate-mode quads (the heat haze strips behind Wander, 01142350's particle quads,
~108 kicks a frame riding): quad117 makes each vertex's GIF pairs in the guest packet glBegin opened, glEnd's hook
parses them back into the 2D assembler, then the recompiled glEnd closes the GIF / DMA tags, sets the packet pointer,
chains the packet into the layer's list and pops glBegin's layer. (2) The model hook's game-thread half as one
per-instance record. (3) texreset's ~1 000-node walk three times a frame.

**imm128 (`SOTC_IMM128`, default on; A/B `imm128` / `r128all`; decomp_walk prim128 / begin128 / imm128, sotc_native
immFeed128).** What glEnd does after its hook only feeds the PS2's GS: in native mode (`nativeDraws`: the hook
installed, no PS2 lists, GS::skipRaster) the GS draws nothing and the DMA chains are walked for SIGNAL / FINISH /
LABEL only; glEnd's packet is A+D TEST / PRIM / RGBAQ / ST / XYZ, none of them. Round 103's ptcl103 leaves its packets
out the same way. So at the two quad sites, in native mode: glBegin's own writes to the gl block (begin128: +0xc,
+0x41f0, +0x5220, +0x14, +0x10 from the primitive table at 0x11916c0, +0x1b8, +0x1b4 from 0x11916a0, +0x1b0 bit 4) and
its TEST and PRIM pairs made natively (the PRIM's anti-aliasing bit by glBegin's jump table at 0x11916e0, read and
matched by target), quad117's pairs written into a host array instead of the packet (its other writes as before),
and the pairs fed to the 2D assembler as glEndHook feeds them: the frame sync and the join, the layer glBegin would
have pushed (iosDlGetLayer's), the haze's screen copy as header, the same `not drawn` conditions. glEnd's 0108CD80
(the software clip of the primitives the kicks flagged with an ADC byte at +0x41f8; its own glBegin .. glEnd, hooked)
is called as glEnd calls it, after the feed, when a flag is set (none in any run: the haze and the particle quads are
on screen when drawn). Not taken (the calls as before): another renderer, a packet already open (glBegin would return
-1), an unknown table entry, quad117 declining the vertices. The packet pool no longer holds these packets (no other
reader). `SOTC_IMM128_CHECK=<n>`: every n-th quad both ways from the same state, the new path dry: the 2D assembler's
whole input (the layer, the texture header, every pair in order, TEST / PRIM included), the gl block (0x5300 bytes but
the packet pointers +4 / +8), VU0 / ACC / Q / CLIP and f0 - f2 compared, the old path's result kept: runs/chkA1 (the
attract demo, 480 s) 189 000 quads, runsb/chkR1 (route 6, 600 s) 46 500 quads, 0 differ. The assembler gets the same
pairs in the same order with the same layer and header, so the draws (and the pixels) are the old path's.

**texr128 (`SOTC_TEXR128`, default off: `=1` on; A/B `texr128`; decomp_texreset resetIndexed).** The list kept as host
arrays of its nodes and records; a call checks each kept node's record and next words (addresses known in advance:
independent loads, prefetched 8 ahead) and clears as the walk does; at the first node whose words moved it walks on
the original way and keeps what it finds. The two-pass order (next read before the clear) is the walk's only when no
record's cleared bytes overlap a node's words: checked when the index is made (sorted, never seen). Kept 99.8% of
calls (chkA1 88 made in 57 000, chkR1 99 in 87 000). `SOTC_TEXR128_CHECK=1` (the list walked read-only first, every
record's 16 bytes compared after): 0 differ in both. But on Vita3K it is slower: the sampler has resetIndexed at
1.00% of the game thread against resetFast's 0.53% (Vita3K has no memory latency for independent loads to hide; the
extra checks are pure instructions there). On the console the old walk is one dependent load after another
(~1 000 x 3 a frame); whether the prefetched checks win there only the console can say: off by default, on in the
console env (`SOTC_TEXR128=1`) with `texr128` in its A/B.

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz; the Mac at load 20-58 the whole session, other rounds building).**

  glEnd, glEndHook, feed2D, vertex2D, the layer push / pop and their hooks, chainTail, 0108CD80, the packet pointer

## Round 130: the diagnostics' cost ("garbage" in the code): off the game thread, a cheap console env, a release build (2026-11-09)

**Question.** Do 130 rounds of logs, timers, checks and A/B switches slow the game down? Measured with a counting build
(PS2X_VITA_DIAGCOUNT=ON: every clock read, getenv, thread-info and formatting call counted by caller, `[diag130]`) in
Vita3K and priced with console unit costs: sceKernelGetThreadInfo ~57 us (r122's console log: `sync ... log 0.81` for 14
calls a frame), a clock read <= ~1.0-1.4 us (the console's [coll119t]: near-empty timed calls at 1.46 us with two reads).

| item (attract demo, Vita3K counts) | thread | console env (r127's flags) / frame | cheap env | console ms saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threads::sample (14 sceKernelGetThreadInfo every frame) | game | 14 | 0.3 (log thread) | **0.8 off the game thread** |
| SOTC_GL_SPIKE_LOG per-draw timers | render | 1 316 reads | 0 | **1.3-1.8 render thread** |
| SOTC_FRAME_LOG_ALL lines (formatting + err.txt writer) | log, cores 1-2 | every frame | 1 / 60 frames + hitches | ~1.2-1.8 (`cpu log`) |
| hook / particle / lane / collision (SOTC_COLL115_LOG) timers | game | ~240 reads | ~100 | 0.15-0.2 |
| job hand-over stamps (lag) | game | 3 attract, ~80 riding | 0 | up to 0.1 |
| getenv, switch tests, A/B rotation, check branches | game | cached; 5 getenv a frame | same | ~0 |

With no log switches (the play config) the dev build already pays ~0: every diagnostic is behind a cached switch. The
console env itself cost ~1.0-1.2 ms of game thread, 1.3-1.8 ms of render thread and ~1.5 ms of cores 1-2.

**Changes.**
- The frame log's thread (log76) reads the threads' run clocks itself and formats the 60-frame line too: nothing of
  native_renderer::threads on the game thread. A frame's `cpu` column is the CPU since the log thread's last read divided
  by the frames since then (it keeps up within ~20 ms); the 60-frame line's is the window's total as before. The thread
  looks every 20 ms; the game thread wakes it only at a half-full ring (no mutex / semaphore signal per frame).
- `SOTC_FRAME_SLOW_MS=<ms>` (default 50): riding frames sit near 50 ms on the console, so the default printed a long
  "[frame] slow" line for 30-50% of them.
- The job hand-over stamps only with `SOTC_FRAME_LOG_ALL` or `SOTC_DIAG_TIMERS=1` (the `lag` column is 0 otherwise).
- runtime/ps2_diag.h: `ps2_diag::env()` for ~170 diagnostic switches (*_CHECK, *_VERIFY, *_LOG, *_STATS, the difftest,
  the A/B rotation, the profilers, dumps; build/r130/diagenv.py made the change). `PS2X_VITA_RELEASE=ON` (SOTC_RELEASE=1
  on the runtime, the sound side and the overrides) makes it a constexpr nullptr, so those paths fold away; no per-call
  timers (`ps2_diag::kTimers`), no subsystem-profiler scopes. The frame summary still works (its `hooks` / `jobs` / `join`
  read 0, so its `game` column includes the hooks: not comparable with the dev build's). SOTC_PROF129 stays available.
- build/agent-scratch/r130/env-console.txt: SOTC_FRAME_LOG=1, SOTC_FRAME_SLOW_MS=100, SOTC_AUDIO_LOG=0, SOTC_BODY_SHADOWS=1.

**Measured (Vita3K 222 MHz, attract).** Clock reads, all threads: 1 743 -> 274 a frame (console env -> cheap env); thread
info 14 -> 0.29; snprintf 17 -> 0.05. Dev against release, cheap env, quiet host (load ~2.5), sampler 300-600 s: game
thread 5.10 M (dev) vs 4.71 / 4.95 M (release) weight a frame, -3..-8% (attract positions drift; ~1 ms noise). Vita3K's HLE
thread-info / clock calls are cheap, so most of the console cost above does not show there (`sync log` 0.10 ms).

**Not done.** GCC's hot / cold block splitting (-freorder-blocks-and-partition) refuses ARM EHABI with exceptions; turning
exceptions off would change every function's CFG and drop its PGO profile. Functions whose diagnostic branches fold away
in the release build lose their profile too (compiled as without PGO); a release PGO training would recover it.

## Round 132: prof129's wrap<12> (46% of the console's game thread) is the game held by the display pacing; pace132 (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r132/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh: own tree ../vita3k-celosia-r132; STATE.md).

**What wrap<12> is.** `decomp_tex64::kSites[12]` = modelDisp (0x01097118): the tex64 join check in front of modelDisp's table
entry, `sotc_native::modelDispHook`. prof129 names a native by the table entry it was entered at, so wrap<12> is the whole hook,
waits included. The frame's first modelDisp runs syncFrame -> endFrame -> `waitData` (native_renderer_gl.cpp): the game thread
waits for the render thread to take the frame handed over before, in `wait_for(2 ms)` loops that were not marked as a wait.
The r130 console log agrees: `sync end` (= that wait) ~15-25 ms a frame in play, `present` 15-42 ms; the game thread's own
work ~15-24 ms. Not tex64: its join is free by then (`wait tex` 0.00).

**Why the render thread is late.** It presents after giving the data back (glPresent86); vglSwapBuffers blocks while vitaGL's
display queue is full, and the queue drains as round 110's display callback (pace110) lets each picture on at its slot (previous
slot + the frame's release interval). The console's `[pace110]`: waited 0.7-1.3 refreshes a picture in the callback (the GPU
done ~1 refresh early), latency 9-12 refreshes (round 110 expected 4-6). A loop: frame N waits for the render thread, which
waits in the swap for a picture ~3 back to leave the screen, so frame N's release interval = that picture's hold, and picture
N's hold = frame N's interval: intervals repeat and only grow. pace110's pulls (after 6 queued pictures in a row, above the
floor A = least arrival latency of the last 64, itself raised by the blocked swaps) fire ~14 times in 600.

**What changed.**
- `SOTC_PACE132` (default on; A/B `pace132`, raylib_vita.cpp): while the callback holds a slot it looks every 1 ms
  (sceKernelDelayThread instead of sceDisplayWaitVblankStart; off: as before); when the game thread is in the hand-over's wait
  (`ps2x_vita_render_wait`, set by waitData) and the render thread is in vglSwapBuffers, the slot comes one refresh earlier
  (once a picture, not below the previous slot + the minimum hold; the chain goes on from the pulled slot). `[pace110]` lines
  end with `| r132: game held N, pulled M`.
- prof129 marks: `wait render` (waitData / waitIdle), `wait hookring` (the hook ring full), hookJoin's wait (`wait hookjoin`),
  modelDispHook's phases (gameZone 0x2000 | phase, printed as "modelDispHook running, by phase").

**Measured (Vita3K 222, own tree, console card, Load Game, 300 s, A/B pace132 windows of 60).** Vita3K's steady state is game
thread bound (wait 0.15 ms a frame outside its ~1 s host stalls), so the held state shows only around boot / stalls (game held
18-23, pulled 15-24 in the first 1 200 pictures, 0 after): frame 31.78 on / 31.72 off, the same. With the marks, wrap<12> is
1.1% of busy and `wait render` 15-29% (all at the stalls). Pictures checked (window shots): normal. ELF spalign 0 sp-based.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r132.vpk; r132/env-console.txt = r130's prof env + `SOTC_AB_FLAG=pace132`. Read:
`tools/prof129.py err.txt --elf celosia-r132.elf` (`wait render` should fall and the frame with it), the `[pace110]` lines'
`r132:` counts and latency (expect 4-6), `build/agent-scratch/tools/abframes.py err.txt` per A/B state.

## Round 134: the console profile's hotspots read; clip134 (the haze strips' lane join), pf134 (prefetch), prof129 zones (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r134/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh: own tree ../vita3k-celosia-r134; STATE.md).
Source: the r132 console profile, riding (`tools/prof129.py r132/console/err2.txt`), callers through the samples' ra.

**What the top entries are.**
- `manager_sub_010F3FB0` (3.2%, "unnamed guest code"): not guest code. prof129's pc is set at calls / returns only, and
  decomp_walk's native heat haze strips (010F3EB8, `strips()`, Wander's haze segments) run their whole segment loop after
  glZOffset's return (pc 0x10f4020, inside 010F3FB0) with no guest call. Zones in Vita3K: the cost is the quads
  (quad117 + begin128: 1.41% of all), not the segment math (0.26%) nor the 2D feed (0.41%, all quads). In quad117,
  `clipNeeded` joined the model lane (mdslane) for the CLIP register: the frame's first immediate quad after the model hooks
  ran the lane's pending modelDispState jobs on the game thread (the console's `[mdslane] joins at clip` ~1 a frame).
- `Sg2RemoteTickProc` (0.9%): the time after its `sceSifCallRpc` (0x109980) to the sound driver's status RPC (HLE:
  Sg2Driver::handleRpc under the mixer's lock, the commands, the 400-byte reply). Moving it off the game thread changes the
  reply's timing (the game reads voice states from it): not done; measured now (zone 0x2030).
- `iosSendMsg` (0.8%): pc 0x1b10dc = after iosSleepThread: blocking sends to the idle box, i.e. EE thread switches (the
  dispatcher's own time is now zone 0x2040).
- `decomp_subthread::wake` / `sleep` (1.4 / 0.6%): the script sub-threads' 0x2c0-byte register frames; each sub-thread's frame
  is cold on the console (one wake a frame), the load waits line by line.
- `sotc_worker::gate<14>` / `<13>` / `<4>`: the particle module's functions run on the game thread (gate = the wrapper;
  0113B928 an emitter's particles, 0113B610 an emitter, doit_particle_manager): the geodisps with attached emitters, kept on the
  game thread by round 91 (they read the characters' motion). Not joins.
- `mdsjoin::wrap<8>` (1.2%) = modelResetSurface's lane join (the game thread helping with lane jobs);
  `decomp_tex64::wrap<10>` = DispDispObjGroupModel (the walk, inclusive).
- `directCallBack` (3.6%): obj125's object loop after isysGroupForFirst (pc 0x112d628); objAry the array variant.

**What changed.**
- `clip134` (`SOTC_CLIP134`, default on; A/B `clip134`): quad117 on a fresh primitive (vertex index 0) records its vertices'
  CLIP judgements (`clipShift`) instead of joining the lane, as clipByMinMaxCube's corners do; the next reader's join puts the
  lane's register shifted by them in the context (`combine`). Exact: every decision in the kick's cases masks the judgements of
  vertices index .. index - 2, all made by the same call (index 0 = the primitive's first vertex), and a 4-vertex quad leaves
  the register = its own four judgements. imm128's clipped path (guest 0108CD80) joins first. Checked with
  SOTC_MDS_LANE_VERIFY=1 (the records against the register at the next hook).
- `pf134` (`SOTC_PF134`, default on; A/B `pf134`): PLD of the sub-thread's frame at wake (and the waker's at sleep), and of the
  next object's header / layout class lines in obj125's loops (group: the next link's object; array: object i + 1). No read
  or write changes (prefetch only); a console-only gain if any (Vita3K has no memory latency: no change there).
- prof129 zones (gameZone 0x2000 | id; prof129.py prints them on the "running, by zone" line): 0x10 / 0x11 / 0x12 strips'
  set-up, segment math, quads; 0x13 immFeed128; 0x20 syncFrame's frame change (any hook); 0x30 SifCallRpc; 0x40 the EE
  dispatcher between guest runs.

**Measured (Vita3K 222, own tree, attract demo with its ride, 420 s, A/B rotation).** clip134: `[mdslane] joins at clip` 0 in
its on windows (600 per 600 frames in its off window); SOTC_MDS_LANE_VERIFY=1 run: 52 413 lane jobs 0 differ, CLIP records
45 466 checked (the strips' records now among them), 0 differ. Vita3K's lane is mostly done by the strips, so the quads' zone
stays ~1.3% there (their own quad117 math); the console's helping joins are what clip134 removes. Frame dt (the [pos] samples):
all on 21.3, clip134 off 21.9, pf134 off 22.9, texr128 off 20.0 ms (noise-level; Vita3K has no memory latency for pf134).
Pictures (window shots, riding over the bridge, the plains, the title): normal. spalign 0 sp-based.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r134.vpk (dev), r134/env-console.txt: prof129 + `SOTC_AB_FLAG=pf134,clip134,texr128`
(texr128 turned on by the env so its windows are the console's verdict on round 128's exact-but-Vita3K-slower switch). Read:
`tools/prof129.py err.txt --elf celosia-r134.elf` (the zone line; manager_sub_010F3FB0 should drop), `[mdslane]` joins at clip.

cloth / bridle, the strands callback 0.14, velocity 0.37, round 122's GetClothDynamics 0.38, DispCloth 0.46, tension 0.21);
curveEval 0.79 (0.55 of it GetMotionIntFrame's per-channel guest calls); floatFrame 0.70 (keys122, rootBlend / geometryStep);
GetEulerYXZFromQuaternion 0.54 (setNodeHPB 0.49); gaze 0.55 (round 41's, gaze122 off); charaLinks 0.55; the particle module's
emitters on the game thread (gate<14> = 0113B928, gate<13> = 0113B610, gate<4> = doit_particle_manager: ~2.2 together,
recompiled VU0 code, not joins). The list is flat: no single character function is above 1.4%.

**What changed (A/B names = the switch names).**
- `pose136` (`SOTC_POSE136`, **default off**, decomp_pose82.cpp): GetMotionMatrix (round 82's pose) keeps each bone's
  results per buffer set (matrices / quaternions / locals / skeleton address; host arrays, a thread's own, 24 sets) with the
  inputs they were made from (the local as read and normalised, the offset, the parent's index; the root's position, rotation
  and scale); a bone whose parent is unchanged and whose inputs are the same bits takes the kept matrix and quaternion
  instead of the arithmetic, and a local read back as last written skips its normalisation. Everything is still written.
  Exact: SOTC_POSE136_CHECK=1 (round 82's pose into host buffers first, compared bit for bit) found **0 differing bones** in
  every call (attract 480 s: 6 000 checks a 600-frame window; the console card's shrine 360 s: 12 600 a window). Kept: 17%
  (the title / demos), 24% (the shrine, 21 calls / 466 bones a frame), 43% (the ride, 10 calls / 255 bones). Not faster in
  Vita3K (host sampler, attract 300-540 s: round 82's pose 1.19% of the game thread, round 136's 1.22%: the kept arrays' stores
  and compares cost what the skipped bones save); off by default, turned on by r136/env-console.txt so the console's A/B
  (memory latency, which Vita3K does not have) decides. `SOTC_POSE136_LOG=<n>`: `[pose136]` (calls, bones, kept).
- `key136` (`SOTC_KEY136`, default on, decomp_motionframe.cpp / decomp_char122.cpp): GetMotionIntFrame's channels decoded by
  round 122's decodeKey into a host buffer (as keys122 does a float frame with no fraction) and copied out, instead of a
  curveEval guest call a channel; v0 / v1 as the loop leaves them (curveEval's last: 1 for a format with no data). Any format
  decodeKey does not know, over 256 channels or a range outside RAM: the old loop. Tolerance (SOTC_KEY136_CHECK=1, every 16th
  call against the old loop): worst 1.8e-4 in a component (0.02 deg), typical 1e-6 (the 9-bit keys' w = sqrt(1 - |xyz|^2)
  rounding), as keys122. Vita3K sampler: evalKeyFast 0.39 -> 0.20%, decodeKey 0.15 -> 0.27% (curveEval + intFrame -0.1%).
- `euler136` (`SOTC_EULER136`, default on, decomp_quat.cpp): GetEulerYXZFromQuaternion (0x1ba880; setNodeHPB's, ~17 calls a
  frame) as plain floats: the original's VU0 statements in their order on the same values (the z / y axes of q, the xz
  normalisation by 1 / sqrt with VU0's FLT_MAX for zero, the turns by the boot ELF's quarter-wave table in 1/65536 steps, the
  conjugate's rows) without the clamps and the VU0 register file; atan2 / asin as the host's (quat122's choice). Written: out
  and f0 (the scratch VU0 registers, Q and v0 not: leaf helper, as quat122). Tolerance (SOTC_EULER136_CHECK=1, every call, the
  old code after it on the same input, its result kept; 316 000 calls attract, 176 000 at the shrine): worst x 3.5e-4, y 1e-5,
  z 2.7e-4 rad (0.02 deg: a 1/65536-turn step at the truncation boundary), typical 1e-7; none over 1e-3. prof129 in Vita3K:
  eulerYXZ 1.08 -> 0.25% of the game thread's running samples.

**Not done (measured / read).** The cloth step (011370E8) is already round 49's clamp-light NEON with the VU0 R stream
three LCG draws a point (cloth122's fused version of it measured no faster in round 122); the emitters' gates are recompiled
VU0 code (0113B928: 536 instructions with its own matrix products) that reads the characters' motion, so it cannot move to the
worker earlier without a dependency rework; GetMotionMatrix's topology pre-pass (0.15%) stays (no half-written skeleton).

## Round 135: fin125 made exact (why its cache missed hits: a stale attribute address, objects replaced in their slots), pf135, a draw-matched A/B for the console's summaries (2026-11-09)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r135/` (build.sh pN, run.sh `<a|b> <none|min|console> <load|walk|ride|attract> <vpk> <name>
<secs> [env]`, own trees ../vita3k-celosia-r135 / -r135b, in_walk2.txt / in_ride.txt (the console card's save), speed.py
(Wander's / Agro's speed from `[pos]`), STATE.md).

**Why fin125's cache missed hits (round 131's 57 "original hits, host no hit").** Round 135's check mode prints, for a
differing clip, the slot, what the host run did with the entry (`[fin135t]`), the id filter asked both ways (`[fin135f]`)
and the entry clipped both ways (`[fin135c]`). Two causes, both found on the console card's save (Agro beside Wander at the
shrine, frames ~1475-1740) and in the attract demo's ride:
1. **A stale attribute address (the misses).** The host clip hit (`r 1`, the kept triangle the same as the game's, ClipCollisionDB
   hits with the same u / v / point), then the id filter said no: `character_ikcolattrfilter` (0x01374F08, the IK feet's
   probes) on one of Agro's surfaces (object type 10, independent part 0). The filter reads GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr, which
   fin125 answered from the address kept when the surface was made (00c879e0); the game's own lookup gives 00c878a0 (20
   records on). The surface's plane, boundary and vertices were unchanged, so no check saw it. The original asks the filter
   "yes" and the feet probe lands on Agro; fin125 skipped it (a probe that misses for a frame, the kind of event that changes
   the riding state). Fix: no attribute address is kept; GetCollisionDBAttributeAdr always asks the game's tables.
2. **Objects replaced in their slots (checks that passed on old bytes).** Round 125's check (once a frame and after a flush)
   compared the plane / boundary flags and values at the addresses kept at the making. When an object's slot is taken over
   (the area loads; the id words and the layout class the same, its collision work or record not), the old bytes stay, so the
   old surface passed. `[fin135] r125 missed` counts these: 88 at the card save's load, 132 walking out of the shrine, 334 in the
   attract demo by frame 16 500; all "chain" (the work / record behind the id changed). Fix: `validate()` walks the chain
   again from the id words (layout class, collision work, record, every flag / slot address, the vertex cache list) and
   compares everything ClipCollisionDB reads: the plane / boundary / three vertex flags and the plane, boundary and vertex qwords
   (round 125 kept no vertex check: a flush of the vertex caches alone, or a skinned blend, would have passed too).
Also: FlushModifiedManager's native moves the worker epoch again at its end (a check between a worker flush's start and its
last cleared flag is not kept). `[fin135] cur bad` (a surface used as current, no flush seen, that is not what ClipCollisionDB
would read now) was 0 in every run: no change without a flush.

**Checks (Vita3K 222 MHz, SOTC_FIN125=1 SOTC_FIN125_CHECK=1: each clip the original way first, its answer used, the host's
compared; final build).**
| run | build | scene | clips compared | hit / no hit | other surface | point max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runsb/chkA1 | p1 (validate(), the attribute address still kept) | attract demo to frame ~20 000 | - | 9 | 0 | - |
| runs/dgW2, runsb/dgW3, dgW4 | p2-p4 (+ the diagnostics) | the card's save, the load at the shrine | - | 4 each (frames 1475-1740, all Agro's surfaces, `filtered 1`) | 0 | - |
| runsb/chkA5 | p5 (no attribute address kept) | attract demo 1560 s (49 450 frames, both ride loops) | 241 061 | **0** | **0** | 0.00 mm |
| runs/ride5 | p5 | the card's save 900 s (17 570 frames: the load with Agro beside Wander, out of the shrine, the plain) | 358 311 | **0** | **0** | 0.00 mm |
| runsb/chkA7 | p7 (= the pushed main, with round 136) | attract demo 1100 s (34 090 frames, both ride loops) | 155 006 | **0** | **0** | 0.00 mm |

In all, 754 378 clips compared on the final logic (2 600 s of attract demo with four rides, 900 s of the card's save), 0
differences. `[fin135]` over those runs: 14.3 M kept-surface uses validated in full, cur bad 0; r125 missed 891 / 196 (attract)
and 109 (card), all "chain".

fin125 is on by default again (SOTC_FIN125=0 turns it off; A/B name `fin125`). seg123 stays off (no answers kept across frames).

**Gameplay.** (1) fin125 on (p6, the default, no check; runs/smkA6on, attract
960 s, `[pos]` with Agro's position, speed.py --horse): Agro at 12-15 units/s (the gallop) in 478 of 634 samples, both rides
galloping without a break until the demo's cut, as in the check run (whose answers are the original's); window shots at 540 /
600 s: Agro galloping over the plain with Wander on him, his shadow under the hooves. (2) The console card's save (runs/ride5,
check run): Wander on the shrine floor at y 11.31, down the ramp, on the plain at y -2.2 .. -4.7; his feet on the ground in the
shots. Riding from the card could not be scripted: Agro stands beside Wander after the load, but TRIANGLE (8-90 frames, with
stick nudges), CIRCLE, R1, SQUARE and UP did not mount him (runs/mount1, mount2); he walks off on his own ~frame 2450 and comes
back ~3500. The ride checks are the attract demo's; the console run is the gallop's judge.

**pf135 (`SOTC_PF135`, default on; A/B `pf135`): prefetch only.** The console profile's top two: `finderLeaf<true>` (3.35%; prof129
names a native by its table entry, so this is the leaf's whole host time: the boundary scan, the plane tests, the duplicate
search, EntryCollisionFinder) and `directCallBack` (3.23%, obj125's object / part loop). (a) finderScan (the leaf's boundary
scan over a run of surfaces) asks for the boundary record and the flag byte of the surface 4 ahead (the ids are known
ahead; the records are spread over the class's table, a miss each on the A9). (b) obj125's part loop asks for the next part's
0x90-byte record (4 lines) and its matrix while this part is tested. No read or write changes; Vita3K has no memory latency,
so only the console's A/B can show it.

**Measured (Vita3K 222, p7, runs/abA7: attract 1200 s, the console env + per-frame lines, A/B `fin125,pf135` rotating by
600).** The finder clips' host time by fin125's state ([fin125t]): 33.45 us a call on (175 385 calls) against 36.07 off
(96 451): -7% with round 135's full checks. Frames, draw-matched on the summaries (bins of 100 draws): fin125 off -0.97 +- 1.14
ms, pf135 off -0.78 +- 1.38 (82 / 70 summaries matched): no difference Vita3K can see (it has no memory latency, the A9's
cost of fin125's lookup chain and of the misses pf135 asks for early). The console's A/B decides both; fin125's reason to be
on is the console's collision share (finderClip<true> + <false> 2.0% of the game thread in r134's profile, ClipCollisionDB's
chain per entry).

**Draw-matched A/B (tooling).** `build/agent-scratch/tools/abframes.py err.txt --summary [--bin N] [--bins]` (a copy in
`tools/abframes.py`): the console env logs only the 60-frame `[frame] N:` summaries; a summary counts for a state when its 60
frames lie in one A/B window, the summaries go in bins by draws a frame (default 50; a bin = a scene load), each state is
compared with "all on" inside a bin and the bins' differences are averaged with weight min(n_off, n_on) (bins with fewer than
`--min` summaries on a side left out), with +- 2 standard errors from the bins. Chosen by itself when the log has no `[frame]
each` lines. On r134's console log (bins of 100): `clip134` off -3.40 +- 2.10 ms frame / -2.54 +- 1.80 game (27 of 36 summaries
matched) where the plain means said -3.1 / -1.8 with different scenes; `pf134` off -3.8 +- 3.7 (18 matched): not significant.

**Console.** build/agent-scratch/celosia-r135.vpk (dev, prof129), r135/env-console.txt (`SOTC_AB_FLAG=fin125,pf135`, rotate,
600). Ride the field at a gallop; read `tools/prof129.py err.txt --elf r135/celosia-r135.elf` (collision's ms/frame, finderClip,
finderLeaf<true>, directCallBack) and `build/agent-scratch/tools/abframes.py err.txt --summary --bin 100` (fin125 / pf135 off
against on in matched scenes). The gallop must hold with fin125 on.

## Round 138: what fin125 does on the console (round 135's "-8.5 ms" was the title screen), validate138: fin125's check without its chain of dependent loads (2026-11-10)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r138/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh / stop.sh on the own tree ../vita3k-celosia-r138,
speed.py, env-console.txt, STATE.md).

**Round 135's console log, read again (build/agent-scratch/r135/console/err.txt, celosia-r135.elf).**
- The draw-matched A/B's `fin125 off -8.50 +- 4.93 ms game` is an artifact. The first fin125-off window (frames 600-1200) is the
  title screen and the save's load (game 16-20 ms a frame at 144-1108 draws: the title menu draws ~1100 a frame), and the bins
  of 100 draws matched it with "all on" summaries of the field that happen to draw as many (frames 9018-9198: game 36-44 ms at
  ~1130 draws). With the summaries before frame 1500 left out (`abframes.py --summary --from 1500`): fin125 off minus on
  **-3.4 +- 5.1 ms** (bins of 100, 5 bins), -1.7 +- 4.2 (200), -2.8 +- 3.7 (400); pf135 +2.8 +- 4.4 / -1.5 +- 3.7 / -1.1 +- 3.7.
  None of these is a difference: the field windows differ by scene far more than by switch (the two field fin125-off windows
  against the "all on" window just before them: -6.2 ms and +5.4 ms).
- The profile cannot be split by A/B window: prof129's windows are 60 s (~1250-1775 frames) and the A/B's 600 frames, so each
  holds two or three states. Its windows hold 0-49% fin125-off frames, and the collision group follows the scene, not that share
  (w1 0% off 4.86 ms a frame, w2 49% 3.73, w3 0% 4.73, w4 36% 7.42, w5 6% 7.05; finderClip<true> + <false> 1.28 / 0.57 / 1.16 /
  2.40 / 1.91% of the busy samples).
- Whole runs, r134 (fin125 off throughout) against r135 (on 5/6 of the time), windows 1-5 (300 s, two sessions of a similar ride): collision
  7.38 -> 5.67 ms a frame; finderClip<true> 1.19 -> 0.89%, finderClip<false> 0.88 -> 0.60%, clipKeep 0.49 -> 0.29%,
  finderLeaf<true> 3.80 -> 1.26% (pf135's prefetch, not fin125). The functions fin125 replaces got cheaper with it on.
- Verdict: no sign that fin125 costs the console anything; the A/B could not resolve its size (a 0.2-0.5 ms change under scene
  noise of +-4 ms). validate() is inlined in finderClip<..> (prof129 names the native by its entry), so its whole cost is inside
  those 1.5%; it is real memory latency though (a dependent chain of five to seven loads to cold lines per kept surface and
  frame, plus the flags and values), so round 138 makes it cheaper and gives the console a direct per-call reading.

**validate138 (`SOTC_FIN138`, default on; A/B `fin138`; coll125.h).** validate() walks the chain from the id words: the
object's +8 (layoutClass), the class's +0x174 / +0x184 (work, record), then for a mesh surface the record's +0x20, its +8, the
slot list and the index, for an independent one the work's part table; then the work's / part's flag and slot bases, the vertex
cache list, and only then the five flags and the plane / boundary / three vertex qwords. Each load's address comes from the one
before: on the A9 one memory wait per link. Round 138 keeps each link's value at the making (Meta: type, partTab, t2, t2v8, rv,
index) and validate138 reads every link at its kept address and compares it with its kept value: all ~17 addresses are known
before the first load, so they are asked for together (PLD) and the comparisons wait on memory about once. When every link reads
as kept, derive() from the id words follows the same addresses and gives the same Addr, so the flag / value compares (validate()'s
own) decide the same; a link that differs remakes the surface (validate() might have reached the same addresses another way: a
remake, never a wrong answer). The clip loop also asks for the next entry's lines when that entry is kept and not current
(prefetch138). Nothing else changes (the epochs, the frame stamp, make(), clip()).

**Checks (Vita3K 222, SOTC_FIN125_CHECK=1: each clip the original way first, its answer used; check mode also runs validate138
and validate() on every use of a kept surface and prints `[fin138] UNSAFE` when validate138 says good where validate() does not).**
| run | build | scene | clips compared | hit / no hit | other surface or point > 1 cm | validate138 unsafe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| runs/chkA1 | p1 | attract demo 1150 s (35 940 frames, Agro's gallop) | (not counted: the [fin125] lines need the log path) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| runs/chkA2 | p1 | attract demo 1200 s (43 230 frames; Agro 12-15 u/s in 835 of 979 `[pos]` samples, 0 gallop drops) | 680 312 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
2 350 s of attract demo with its ride loops, 0 differences, 0 unsafe; `[fin135] cur bad` 0. (p1's SOTC_FIN138_LOG wrapper
skipped coll125::log(), so the runs printed no [fin125] / [fin138] count lines, only the per-difference lines, of which there
were none; p2 = the shipped build calls it. The counts come from [fin138t]: 680 312 clips, 1.84 M re-validations in chkA2.)
A third run with the counting build (p2) and a no-check gameplay run could not start: Vita3K crashes at boot while the Mac's
screen is locked (every tree, the other agent's too: `Unhandled access to 0x0` after settings.cfg).

## Round 139: the scripts' sub-thread switch, the sound driver's status request and the pad sends, the isys locks' kernel calls, the garbage walk, iosGetRandom (sub139, sg2q139, rpc139, sem139, gc139, rnd139) (2026-11-10)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r139/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh / v3kb.sh / stop.sh on the own trees
../vita3k-celosia-r139 / -r139b, 222 MHz, muted; zones.py: prof129's samples of guest functions by pc / ra / zone; asm.sh;
speed.py; env-console.txt; STATE.md). Source: the r135 console profile riding (scripts/AI 5.2 ms, the guest code around it).

**What the console's entries are** (`r139/zones.py r135/console/err.txt r135/celosia-r135.elf <pattern>`; 1% of the busy
game thread = 0.38 ms).
- `Sg2RemoteTickProc` 0.76% = pc 0x1d2340 in zone 0x2030: the HLE `SifCallRpc` of the sound driver's status request (the
  syscall stub sets pc to ra before the handler), ~1-3 a frame (the VBlank thread's sound tick). `sceDbcSendData2` 0.21% the
  same zone: the DualShock actuator sends (sids 0x8000131e / 0x8000131f, which the native IOP completes without a service).
- `iosSendMsg` 0.58% = 0x1b10dc (the main thread parked at its frame end, iosSleepThread): 0.40 of it zone 0x2040, the
  dispatcher after the park.
- `kernel_sub_001C81B0` 0.45% = pc 0x1c81e8: decomp_gctick's native garbage walk (prof129 names it by the pc its time
  check last set): ~450 blocks a frame.
- `decomp_subthread::wake` / `sleep` 0.62 / 0.43%: the script sub-threads' 0x2c0-byte register frames (~50 wakes a frame).
- `iosGetRandom` 0.36%: the particle emitters' random floats (VU0 R register code).
- `decomp_isys::*` / `isys48::*`: the group / object locks' kernel calls (GetThreadId, PollSema) through the syscall stubs.

**Measured first** (SOTC_STAT139=1: `[stat139]` every 600 frames: EE dispatches, thread runs, parks by ra and reason, the
RPCs' host time, sub-thread wakes; Vita3K 222, p1 = main + the counters, attract demo riding): 18-19 dispatches, 9-10
thread runs, 6 parks a frame (main at 0x1b10dc, the callback thread at 0x1b2d08, the VBlank thread at 0x1c8108); the
status request ~2 a frame at ~200 us each in Vita3K (the driver ~90 us of it, of which ~65 us waiting for the mixer's
lock: `[audio-ticks]`; the rest the generic SifCallRpc: ABI selection, client / server maps under their mutexes, debug
events), the pad sends ~35 us each; 31 800 sub-thread wakes / 600 frames. Vita3K host sampler (profA1, p1): Sg2 lock spin
(trylock + CAS + handleRpc) 0.38%, gctick 0.81%, the sub-thread switch 1.58%, the isys kernel calls (bindMainContextForSyscall,
GetThreadId, pollSemaphore, publishSnapshot, eeScheduler()) ~0.5% of the game thread.

**What changed (A/B names = the switch names; `r139all` all six off together).**
- `sub139` (`SOTC_SUB139`, default on; decomp_subthread.cpp; port): the switch is a call on both sides (the waker's jal
  isysWakeupSubThread, the sub-thread's jal isysSleepSubThread), so by the R5900 ABI the code after it reads only the
  callee-saved registers. The frames now keep s0-s7, fp, f20-f31, hi / lo / sa / hi1 / lo1 (v0 = lo1 as before), and in the
  waker's frame a0-a3 (the sleep reads a1-a3 back); the sub-thread's load also takes a0, which isysStartSubThread (0x1c98a0)
  puts in a new sub-thread's first frame (the script's argument). 9 of a sub-thread frame's 22 lines (11 of the waker's)
  instead of all. The recompiled paths (start, end at 0x1c9e28, fallbacks) still copy whole frames; a whole load of a lean
  frame gives the caller-saved registers stale words, unread. Found on the way: without a0 the scripts' first wake went wrong
  and the boot stopped at the logo (p2; bisected by switch). `SOTC_SUB139_POISON=1`: after each lean load the caller-saved
  registers (at, v1, a0-a3 where not kept, t0-t9, f0-f19) are set to 0xBAD1BAD1 / NaN.
- `sg2q139` (`SOTC_SG2Q139`, default on; iop_sg2.cpp, sound_mixer.h/.cpp; port): the status request never waits for the
  audio thread's mix piece. When the mixer's lock is taken, the request's commands go to a queue and the request answers
  with the last reply made, as the PS2's no-wait RPC does (the EE reads what the IOP sent for an earlier request); the audio
  thread runs the queue and makes the next reply between its pieces (SoundMixer::runPieceHook, lock held), the next request
  that gets the lock runs what is left first. At most 3 in a row are left before one waits. `SOTC_SG2Q139_ALWAYS=1`
  (measuring): every request left for the audio thread. Counts on the `[stat139]` line.
- `rpc139` (`SOTC_RPC139`, default on; RPC.cpp; exact): SifCallRpc for the status request and the pad sends (no-wait, no end
  function, the register convention, a sid whose first generic call was answered by the HLE side with no guest server
  function or buffer) without the generic call's bookkeeping: a binding cache made again after any bind / register / init, no
  ABI selection (no service overrides it), no maps or debug events. The guest sees the same: the client's command / end
  function / parameter / mode / server, the server record's fields, the reply, the completion semaphore signalled as the
  generic path signals it, v0 = 0.
- `sem139` (`SOTC_SEM139`, default on; decomp_sema.cpp, decomp_isys / isys48, ee_scheduler.h; exact): GetThreadId (0x106ed0)
  and PollSema (0x107030) as table natives, and for the isys natives, with a thread running: the running thread, or the
  count taken / KE_SEMA_ZERO, without the syscall's binding call and snapshot publish. The scheduler's semaphore lookups
  (these, SignalSema's fast path, semaphore()) go through a 16-entry direct-mapped cache (one entry thrashed between the isys
  lock, the RPC completions and the kernel's message semaphore); deleteSemaphore / reset clear it.
- `gc139` (`SOTC_GC139`, default on; decomp_gctick.cpp; exact): while round 58's kept time check holds (no guest call since,
  the EE clock unchanged), a run of blocks with nothing to move (in use, last, followed by a free block or by one with no
  handler) is stepped in host locals: the budget's arithmetic on the block count, no per-block clock read, count call or
  register writes; s1 / s2 / s3 get what the per-block code leaves. The block that stops the pass or moves goes to the old
  code. `SOTC_GC139_CHECK=1`: each run stepped again the per-block way and compared (`[gc139]`).
- `rnd139` (`SOTC_RND139`, default on; decomp_r139.cpp; exact): iosGetRandom (0x1be7e8) as host code: 14 steps of the 23-bit
  R register in a host register, R / vf5 / a3 / f0 written once. `SOTC_RND139_CHECK=1`: every call also runs the recompiled
  code on a copy of the context and compares (`[rnd139]`).

**Checks (Vita3K 222).**

| runs/walkW4 | p4 | the console card's save walked out of the shrine onto the plain, 720 s, poison + rnd check | rnd139 1.0 M 0 differ; 2.2 M poisoned loads; Wander's walk as before (y -3.5 .. 11.3) |

## Round 140: the display walk's group pass and sort lists, the strips' quads: clip140 (the layout objects' clips on a helper thread), sort140, quad140 (2026-11-10)

Scripts, runs: `build/agent-scratch/r140/` (build.sh pN, run.sh / v3k.sh / v3kb.sh / stop.sh on the own trees
../vita3k-celosia-r140 / -r140b, 222 MHz, muted; zpc.py: prof129's running samples by zone and guest pc;
env-console.txt; STATE.md). Source: the r135 console profile riding (display 6.81 ms of the game thread).

**What the console's display entries are** (`r140/zpc.py r135/console/err.txt r135/celosia-r135.elf`, % of the busy thread).
- `decomp_tex64::wrap<12>` 2.37% = modelDisp's table entry: 2.28 of it in zone 0x2020, the frame change (syncFrame) the
  frame's first modelDisp meets, running (its waits are marked apart). The frame log's own timing of that block on the
  console (`sync ... end`) is 0.1-0.2 ms over its render wait, not 0.87 ms: prof129's sampler (cores 1-2) runs most when
  those cores go idle, which is the frame change (round 129's caveat); not chased.
- `decomp_walk::solidDisp` 0.93% = the model hook's phases called from it as a native (zones 0x2002-0x2005).
- `decomp_tex64::wrap<10>` 2.11% = DispDispObjGroupModel's own code; its samples sit after ClipLayoutObjModel's return
  (ra 0x10f550c, 0.55) and AddSortObj's (0x10f55a4, 0.37): the walk's next object's loads.
- `decomp_walk::clipLayoutObjModel` 2.06%, all from the group pass (ra 0x10f550c): the layout objects' update.
- `manager_sub_010F3FB0` 1.65% = the heat-haze strips (round 134): quads 0.97, segment math 0.41, 2D feed 0.25.
- `decomp_layoutclass::getLayoutClass` 0.59%: called from the scripts / AI all over, not the walk.
- Vita3K's host sampler (attract demo, the game thread) adds what prof129 cannot split: quad117 and its helpers 2.3%,
  the sort lists' bucket loops (sortOrder 0.73, clearSortList 0.41: ~1000 buckets, a few dozen used, cleared twice,
  copied twice and scanned twice a walk), clip83::clip 0.9%.

**What changed (A/B names = the switch names).**
- `clip140` (`SOTC_CLIP140`, default on; decomp_walk.cpp; exact): at the group pass's start the group's chain is read
  as isysGroupForNext walks it (without its counters' writes) and the layout objects whose update is ClipLayoutObjModel
  (no billboard / camera link, no clip callback) are listed for a helper thread (`threads::kOffload`, cores 1-2, the
  game thread's FP mode), which computes their clips from the list's end back: clip83's arithmetic on the same words,
  writing nothing; each result is the words the clip writes (rec +0x20 .. +0x34, geo +0x230 .. +0x23c and +0x250 ..
  +0x257) and its v0 / f0. The walk, at such an object, writes them there and sets what the call leaves (ra, sp, pc,
  v0, f0) instead of the call; an object the helper has not finished (not reached, or being clipped now) the walk
  claims and clips as before: the walk never waits for the helper. Objects off clip83's fast path (skinned, self-LOD:
  the characters) go to the walk. A generation number in each slot's state keeps a late helper from touching the next
  walk's slots; the walk does not wait for the helper at its end. Nothing between the pass's start and an object's
  turn writes what its clip reads (the earlier objects' clips, the billboards' simple updates, the particle geodisps'
  updates, the visibility callbacks, AddSortObj): `SOTC_CLIP140_CHECK=1` runs every taken object's clip the old way
  too and compares its writes and registers (`[clip140] differ`); `SOTC_CLIP140_LOG=1`: `[clip140]` counts every 600
  walks.
- `sort140` (`SOTC_SORT140`, default on; exact): the walk's sort lists' bucket arrays as host words (in plain RAM, away
  from the list's own words): the clears as 16-byte stores, the order copies and the next-bucket scans 8 buckets a
  test, the list's count and array read once. The same words written, the same values left (the index word as
  GetFirstSortObj / GetNextSortObj leave it). `SOTC_SORT140_CHECK=1`: every scan also bucket by bucket ([sort140]).
- `quad140` (`SOTC_QUAD140`, default on; exact): quad117 (the strips' and the immediate quads' four vertices) is now
  quad117Body, called as before when off; on, through a copy with everything inlined (`flatten`): the PGO build left
  its per-vertex helpers as calls, several through long-branch veneers (the VU0 product lambda three times a vertex,
  the blend `sel`, the GIF pair emitter, glColor4f / glTexCoord2f). Same operations in the same order (the A9 has no
  fused multiply-add). `SOTC_QUAD140_CHECK=<n>`: every n-th quad run both ways from the same state (gl block, the
  packet's next 0x100 bytes, the host pairs, the context, the lane's CLIP record) ([quad140]).

**Checks (Vita3K 222, the check switches on: every taken clip compared, every bucket scan, every quad).**
